**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 6, verses 1–12:**

It is Meccan in its entirety, except for six verses. Among them, ﴿They did not measure God with His true measure﴾ (6:91) and the following three verses were revealed in Medina, as was ﴿Say: Come, I will recite to you what your Lord has forbidden﴾ (6:151) up to ﴿so that you may be God-fearing﴾ (6:153). These six verses are Medinan, and the rest of the surah is Meccan.

It was revealed at Mecca all at once, at night, accompanied by seventy thousand angels who filled the space between the two horizons, with a loud sound of glorification and praise. The Prophet ﷺ said, "Glory be to God, the Mighty," and fell into prostration. Then he summoned the scribes, and they wrote it down that same night. [125] It has one hundred and sixty-five verses, all of them proofs against the polytheists. Its words number three thousand and fifty-two, and its letters number twelve thousand four hundred and twenty.

Ibn 'Abbas related from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Surat al-An'am was revealed to me all at once, escorted by seventy thousand angels, who had a loud sound of glorification and praise. Whoever recites Surat al-An'am, those seventy thousand angels will send blessings upon him, a day and a night for each verse of al-An'am." [126]

Muslim related from Abu Salih, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Whoever recites the first three verses of Surat al-An'am, up to His saying ﴿and He knows what you earn﴾ (6:3), God will assign to him forty thousand angels who will write for him the like of their worship until the Day of Resurrection. A angel will descend from the seventh heaven with an iron mace, and whenever Satan wishes to whisper to him and inspire something into his heart, the angel will strike him with it, a blow that leaves seventy veils between him and Satan. And when he dies, on the Day of Resurrection, he will say to the Lord, blessed and exalted: 'Give me good news, in Your shade, and eat of the fruits of Your Garden, and drink from the water of al-Kawthar, and wash in the water of al-Sabil, for You are my servant and I am your Lord.'" [127]

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: No revelation descended except that Gabriel was accompanied by four angels who guard it ﴿before him and behind him﴾ (72:27), and this is His saying, exalted is He, ﴿that He may know that they have conveyed the messages of their Lord﴾ (72:28). Except for al-An'am, for it descended accompanied by seventy thousand angels.

Sufyan related from Abu Ishaq, from 'Abd Allah ibn Khalifa, who said: 'Umar (may God be pleased with him) said:

"Al-An'am is among the essentials of the Qur'an."

In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Praise belongs to God, who created the heavens and the earth﴾ (6:1), the verse.

Muqatil said: The polytheists said to the Prophet ﷺ, "Who is your Lord?" He said: "He who created the heavens and the earth." They denied him, so God, mighty and majestic, revealed praising Himself and indicating by His attributes His existence and oneness. ﴿Praise belongs to God, who created the heavens and the earth . . .﴾ (6:1) ... ﴿in two days﴾ (41:9), Sunday and Monday, ﴿the earth in two days﴾, Tuesday and Wednesday. ﴿And He made the darknesses and the light﴾ (6:1).

al-Suddi said: It means the darkness of night and the light of day.

al-Waqidi said: Wherever in the Qur'an the words "darknesses" and "light" appear, they mean disbelief and faith.

Qatada said: It means Paradise and Hellfire. The plural "darknesses" and the singular "light" are used because light extends, whereas darkness does not extend.

The scholars of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: "Made" (ja'ala) here is a connecting element, and the Arabs mean "made" in speech.

Abu 'Ubayda said: "I have begun to see two as four, and one as two, since old age has worn me down." [128] The meaning of the verse is: Praise belongs to God who created the heavens and the earth and the darknesses and the light. It was also said: its meaning is that He created the heavens and the earth, and He has made the darknesses and the light, because He created darkness and light before creating the heavens and the earth.

Qatada said: God created the heavens before the earth, darkness before light, and Paradise before Hellfire.

Wahb said: The first thing God created was a dark place. Then He created a jewel, and it became that place. Then He looked at the jewel with a look of awe, and it turned to blood, and its vapour and foam rose up. From the vapour He created the heavens, and from the foam the earths.

'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr related from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "God, mighty and majestic, created His creation in darkness, then cast upon them some of His light. Whoever was struck by that light that day was guided, and whoever missed it went astray." [129]

﴿Yet those who disbelieve ascribe equals to their Lord﴾ (6:1).

Qutrub said: It is abbreviated, meaning: those who disbelieve after this clarification ascribe equals to their Lord, that is, they associate idols with Him. Its root is the equality of one thing with another. It is said: "I equated this with that," when I made them equal.

al-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: The "bi" in His saying ﴿ascribe equals to their Lord﴾ means "'an" (concerning), and His saying "ya'dilun" (they ascribe equals) is from 'adl (equating). That is, "yakun" and "ya'rifun" (they exist and they know).

He recited:

"And a seeker, with Tha'laba ibn Sayyar,
and she was held fast by Tha'laba's clinging."

(His reference to "ibn Sayyr" is to "ibn Sayyar"; the verse belongs to al-Mufaddal al-Bakri. See al-Sihah.)

He also recited:

"They drink with sea-water, then they are lifted up,
when the green seas have their roaring." [130]

Meaning: from the sea. God, exalted is He, said: ﴿a spring from which the servants of God drink﴾ (76:6), meaning: from it.

Muhammad ibn al-Mu'afa, from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, said: The creation was opened with praise of God, when He said: ﴿Praise belongs to God, who created the heavens and the earth﴾ (6:1), and it was closed with praise, when He said: ﴿And it will be judged between them with truth, and it will be said: Praise belongs to God, Lord of the worlds﴾ (39:75).

Hammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn al-Harith, from Wahb, said: God opened the Torah with praise, when He said: ﴿Praise belongs to God, who created the heavens and the earth﴾ (6:1), and closed it with praise, when He said: ﴿And say: Praise belongs to God, who has not taken a son﴾ (17:111), the verse. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿It is He who created you from clay﴾ (6:2), means Adam (peace be upon him). He expressed it in the form of address to them, since they were his offspring. [131]

al-Suddi said: God sent Gabriel to the earth to bring him a handful of its clay. The earth said: "I seek refuge in God from you, lest you diminish me." So he returned without taking any. He said: "O Lord, it has sought refuge in You." So He sent Michael, and it sought refuge; he returned. Then He sent the Angel of Death, and it sought refuge in God from him. He said: "I seek refuge in God from disobeying His command." He took from the surface of the earth and mixed the red, the black and the white soil. That is why the colours of the children of Adam differ. Then he kneaded it with sweet water, salt water and bitter water, and that is why their characters differ. God, mighty and majestic, said to the Angel of Death: "Gabriel and Michael had mercy on the earth, and you did not have mercy on it. Undoubtedly, I will place the spirits of whomever I create from this clay in your hand."

Abu Hurayra related from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "God created Adam from dust, made it into clay, then left it until it became black, malleable mud. He shaped and formed him, then left him until he became dry clay like pottery. [Iblis would pass by him and say:] 'You were created for a great matter!' Then God breathed into him His spirit." [132]

﴿Then He decreed a term, and a term specified with Him﴾ (6:2).

al-Hasan, Qatada and al-Dahhak said: The first term is what lies between one's creation and one's death. The second term is what lies between one's death and one's resurrection, which is the barzakh (intermediate state).

Mujahid and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: ﴿Then He decreed a term﴾ means the term of this world, ﴿and a term specified with Him﴾ is the Hereafter.

'Ata' related from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Then He decreed a term﴾ is sleep, in which the soul is seized and then returned to its owner when awake. ﴿A term specified with Him﴾ is the term of a person's death. ﴿Then He decreed a term﴾ means He made a duration for your lives, at which you will end, which you do not exceed. ﴿And a term specified﴾ means, and it is a term specified with Him, which no one knows except Him. The specified term is the term that comes later.

﴿Then you doubt﴾ (6:2), that is, you are uncertain about resurrection. ﴿And He is God in the heavens and on the earth. He knows your secret and your open﴾ (6:3), meaning: He is the God of the heavens and the God of the earth. ﴿And He knows what you earn﴾ (6:3), meaning: what you do of good and evil.

Muqatil: He knows the secrets of your deeds and their open aspects. He said: We heard Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi say: I heard Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Balkhi say: This is one of the inverted forms of speech, and its sense is: "He is God, He knows your secret and your open in the heavens and the earth, so nothing is hidden from Him."

﴿And no sign from the signs of their Lord comes to them﴾ (6:4), meaning the disbelievers of Mecca, such as the splitting of the moon or otherwise, ﴿except that they turn away from it﴾, they abandon it and deny it. ﴿They have denied the truth﴾ (6:5), meaning the Qur'an; it was also said: Muhammad (peace be upon him), ﴿when it came to them. So soon there will come to them the news of what they used to mock﴾ (6:5), that is, the reports of their mockery and its recompense. This is a warning to them, and the warning befell them on the day they saw it.

﴿Did they not see how many generations We destroyed before them?﴾ (6:6). Generations means the past nations. A "qarn" is a group of people, and its plural is "qurun." It was also said: a "qarn" is a period of time, said to be eighty years, or a hundred years. On this view, the meaning would be: people of a generation. ﴿We had established them on the earth as We had not established you﴾ (6:6), meaning We gave them what We had not given you.

Ibn 'Abbas said: We gave them respite in life, in bodies and in children, like the people of Noah, 'Ad and Thamud. It is also said: "I established him, and I established for him," and it came [ ... ] all together. ﴿And We sent the sky upon them in abundant rain﴾ (6:6), meaning the rain.

The Arabs say: "We kept seeing the sky until we came to you in abundant rain," meaning copious, abundant, lasting. It is an intensive form (mif'al) from the root "durr" (pouring), and the masculine and feminine are alike in it.

The poet said:

"May a cloud from the star Pleiades' rain water you,
dripping heavily, a pouring downpour."

As for His saying ﴿as We had not established you﴾, it is a second-person address that is in the form of the "tanwin" (mood). Like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿until, when you are in the ship and they sail with them﴾ (10:22).

The scholars of Basra said: He spoke of them with His saying ﴿Did they not see﴾, and among them were Muhammad and his companions, then He addressed them. The Arabs say: "I said to 'Abd Allah, how noble he is," and "I said to 'Abd Allah, I honour you." And We made the rivers flow beneath them. ﴿So We destroyed them for their sins and We raised up after them another generation﴾ (6:6), meaning We created and originated after them another generation.

﴿And had We sent down to you a book on parchment﴾ (6:7), the verse.

al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: It was revealed concerning al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Umayya and Nawfal ibn Khuwaylid. They said: "O Muhammad, we will not believe in you until you bring us a book from God, with four angels accompanying it who will testify that it is from God and that you are His messenger." So God, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿And had We sent down to you a book on parchment﴾, written from God in a sheet, ﴿and they had touched it with their hands﴾, that is, they witnessed it directly and touched it with their hands, ﴿those who disbelieve would certainly say: This is nothing but clear magic﴾ (6:7), because of what had preceded regarding them in My knowledge.

﴿And they say: Why has no angel been sent down to him?﴾ (6:8), meaning to Muhammad. ﴿Had We sent down an angel, the matter would have been decided﴾ (6:8), that is, the punishment would have become due, and their destruction would have been completed, since angels do not descend except with revelation [and the lawful]. ﴿Then they would not be respited﴾ (6:8), that is, the disbelievers would not be given time.

Mujahid said: ﴿the matter would have been decided﴾ means the Hour would have been established.

al-Dahhak said: If an angel came to them in his true form, they would die.

Qatada said: Even if We had sent down the angel and they did not believe, He would have hastened the punishment for them and not delayed them for the blink of an eye.

﴿And if We had made him an angel﴾ (6:9), meaning if We had sent an angel to them, ﴿We would have made him a man﴾, meaning in the form of a human man, because they cannot bear to look at angels. ﴿And We would have confused them﴾, meaning We would have mixed up and obscured for them ﴿what they confuse﴾, that is, they confuse and obscure for themselves, until they doubt, so that it cannot be known whether he is an angel or a human.

al-Dahhak and 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas, said: They are the People of the Book. They divided their religion and denied their messengers, and this is altering words from their places. So God confused them with what they had confused for themselves.

Qatada said: No people confused themselves without God confusing them.

al-Azhari recited "wa-la-labasna" with the doubled letter, indicating repetition. It is said: the Arabs "albasa" (confuse) "albasahu labsan," and "iltabasa 'alayhim al-amr" (the matter was confused for them), "albasahu labsan."

﴿And mocked were messengers before you﴾ (6:10), just as you were mocked, O Muhammad, consoling His Prophet ﷺ. ﴿So there surrounded﴾.

al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: "Tarak" (abandoned). 'Ata' said: "Ahal" (made lawful). Muqatil said: "Dar" (turned). al-Dahhak said: "Ihata" (encompassed).

al-Zajjaj said: "Al-hayq" in language is what overtakes a person of harm, which he has done. From it is: ﴿evil planning encompasses only its planners﴾ (35:43).

It was also said: "Wajaba" (became obligatory). "Al-hayq" and "al-hayuq" mean obligation.

﴿Those who mocked, they mocked them﴾ (6:10), ﴿what they used to mock﴾. So the punishment and the hastening of retribution surrounded those who mocked the messengers.

﴿Say, O Muhammad, to these deniers and mockers: Travel⁠ (sir), journey in the earth, taking heed; then look at how the end of the deniers was﴾ (6:11), that is, their final outcome, and how disbelief and falsehood brought them to destruction and punishment. He warns the disbelievers of Mecca of the punishment of past nations.

﴿Say: To whom belongs what is in the heavens and the earth?﴾ (6:12). If they answer you, well and good; otherwise, ﴿say: To God﴾ (6:12). He says: He will test you by the number of days, not [ ... ] and the idols. Then He said: ﴿Your Lord has prescribed for Himself mercy﴾ (6:12), that is, He decreed, out of grace and generosity, and made obligatory.

Mentioning "the self" (nafs) here is an expression of His existence and an emphasis of unity, and of the absence of intermediaries besides Him. This is an appeal from Him, exalted is He, to those who turn away from Him to turn toward Him, and an announcement that He is merciful to His servants, that He does not hasten to punish them, and that He accepts their repentance and return.

Hisham ibn Munabbih said: Abu 'Urwa related to us from Muhammad, the Messenger of God ﷺ, who said: "When God had decreed creation, He wrote in a book that is with Him above the Throne: 'Indeed My mercy precedes My wrath.'" [133]

'Umar said to Ka'b al-Ahbar: "What is the first thing God began of His creation?" Ka'b said: "God wrote a book, not with a pen or ink, but He wrote with His finger, recited by chrysolite, pearls and rubies: 'Indeed I am God, there is no god but I; My mercy has preceded My wrath.'"

Sulayman and 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar said: God, exalted is He, has a hundred mercies, each mercy of which covers what lies between the heaven and the earth. He sent down one mercy to the people of the world, and by it the humans, jinn, birds of the sky, fish of the sea, what lies between the air and the animals, and the creatures of the earth show mercy to one another. He keeps ninety-nine mercies with Himself. When the Day of Resurrection comes, He will add that mercy to what He has.

﴿He will surely gather you﴾ (6:12), the lam here is the lam of oath and the nun is the nun of emphasis. Its meaning: "By God, He will surely gather you ﴿to the Day of Resurrection﴾ (6:12)," meaning on the Day of Resurrection. "Ila" means "fi" (in). It was also said: the meaning is that He will surely gather you ﴿to the Day of Resurrection﴾ in [others], ﴿about which there is no doubt﴾ (6:12).

﴿Those who have lost themselves﴾ (6:12), meaning they were overcome by their own souls. The tanwin is in the place of the accusative, referring back to the kaf and the nun of His saying ﴿He will surely gather you﴾. It may also be nominative, as the subject, with its predicate: ﴿so they do not believe﴾ (6:12). So God, exalted is He, informed that the one who denies the Hereafter is ruined and a loser.

So soon there will come to them the news of what they used to mock﴾ (6:5), that is, the reports of their mockery and its recompense. This is a warning to them, and the warning befell them on the day they saw it.

﴿Did they not see how many generations We destroyed before them?﴾ (6:6). Generations means the past nations. A "qarn" is a group of people, and its plural is "qurun." It was also said: a "qarn" is a period of time, said to be eighty years, or a hundred years. On this view, the meaning would be: people of a generation. ﴿We had established them on the earth as We had not established you﴾ (6:6), meaning We gave them what We had not given you.

Ibn 'Abbas said: We gave them respite in life, in bodies and in children, like the people of Noah, 'Ad and Thamud. It is also said: "I established him, and I established for him," and it came [ ... ] all together. ﴿And We sent the sky upon them in abundant rain﴾ (6:6), meaning the rain.

The Arabs say: "We kept seeing the sky until we came to you in abundant rain," meaning copious, abundant, lasting. It is an intensive form (mif'al) from the root "durr" (pouring), and the masculine and feminine are alike in it.

The poet said:

"May a cloud from the star Pleiades' rain water you,
dripping heavily, a pouring downpour."

As for His saying ﴿as We had not established you﴾, it is a second-person address that is in the form of the "tanwin" (mood). Like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿until, when you are in the ship and they sail with them﴾ (10:22).

The scholars of Basra said: He spoke of them with His saying ﴿Did they not see﴾, and among them were Muhammad and his companions, then He addressed them. The Arabs say: "I said to 'Abd Allah, how noble he is," and "I said to 'Abd Allah, I honour you." And We made the rivers flow beneath them. ﴿So We destroyed them for their sins and We raised up after them another generation﴾ (6:6), meaning We created and originated after them another generation.

﴿And had We sent down to you a book on parchment﴾ (6:7), the verse.

al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: It was revealed concerning al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Umayya and Nawfal ibn Khuwaylid. They said: "O Muhammad, we will not believe in you until you bring us a book from God, with four angels accompanying it who will testify that it is from God and that you are His messenger." So God, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿And had We sent down to you a book on parchment﴾, written from God in a sheet, ﴿and they had touched it with their hands﴾, that is, they witnessed it directly and touched it with their hands, ﴿those who disbelieve would certainly say: This is nothing but clear magic﴾ (6:7), because of what had preceded regarding them in My knowledge.

﴿And they say: Why has no angel been sent down to him?﴾ (6:8), meaning to Muhammad. ﴿Had We sent down an angel, the matter would have been decided﴾ (6:8), that is, the punishment would have become due, and their destruction would have been completed, since angels do not descend except with revelation [and the lawful]. ﴿Then they would not be respited﴾ (6:8), that is, the disbelievers would not be given time.

Mujahid said: ﴿the matter would have been decided﴾ means the Hour would have been established.

al-Dahhak said: If an angel came to them in his true form, they would die.

Qatada said: Even if We had sent down the angel and they did not believe, He would have hastened the punishment for them and not delayed them for the blink of an eye.

﴿And if We had made him an angel﴾ (6:9), meaning if We had sent an angel to them, ﴿We would have made him a man﴾, meaning in the form of a human man, because they cannot bear to look at angels. ﴿And We would have confused them﴾, meaning We would have mixed up and obscured for them ﴿what they confuse﴾, that is, they confuse and obscure for themselves, until they doubt, so that it cannot be known whether he is an angel or a human.

al-Dahhak and 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas, said: They are the People of the Book. They divided their religion and denied their messengers, and this is altering words from their places. So God confused them with what they had confused for themselves.

Qatada said: No people confused themselves without God confusing them.

al-Azhari recited "wa-la-labasna" with the doubled letter, indicating repetition. It is said: the Arabs "albasa" (confuse) "albasahu labsan," and "iltabasa 'alayhim al-amr" (the matter was confused for them), "albasahu labsan."

﴿And mocked were messengers before you﴾ (6:10), just as you were mocked, O Muhammad, consoling His Prophet ﷺ. ﴿So there surrounded﴾.

al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: "Tarak" (abandoned). 'Ata' said: "Ahal" (made lawful). Muqatil said: "Dar" (turned). al-Dahhak said: "Ihata" (encompassed).

al-Zajjaj said: "Al-hayq" in language is what overtakes a person of harm, which he has done. From it is: ﴿evil planning encompasses only its planners﴾ (35:43).

It was also said: "Wajaba" (became obligatory). "Al-hayq" and "al-hayuq" mean obligation.

﴿Those who mocked, they mocked them﴾ (6:10), ﴿what they used to mock﴾. So the punishment and the hastening of retribution surrounded those who mocked the messengers.

﴿Say, O Muhammad, to these deniers and mockers: Travel⁠ (sir), journey in the earth, taking heed; then look at how the end of the deniers was﴾ (6:11), that is, their final outcome, and how disbelief and falsehood brought them to destruction and punishment. He warns the disbelievers of Mecca of the punishment of past nations.

﴿Say: To whom belongs what is in the heavens and the earth?﴾ (6:12). If they answer you, well and good; otherwise, ﴿say: To God﴾ (6:12). He says: He will test you by the number of days, not [ ... ] and the idols. Then He said: ﴿Your Lord has prescribed for Himself mercy﴾ (6:12), that is, He decreed, out of grace and generosity, and made obligatory.

Mentioning "the self" (nafs) here is an expression of His existence and an emphasis of unity, and of the absence of intermediaries besides Him. This is an appeal from Him, exalted is He, to those who turn away from Him to turn toward Him, and an announcement that He is merciful to His servants, that He does not hasten to punish them, and that He accepts their repentance and return.

Hisham ibn Munabbih said: Abu 'Urwa related to us from Muhammad, the Messenger of God ﷺ, who said: "When God had decreed creation, He wrote in a book that is with Him above the Throne: 'Indeed My mercy precedes My wrath.'" [133]

'Umar said to Ka'b al-Ahbar: "What is the first thing God began of His creation?" Ka'b said: "God wrote a book, not with a pen or ink, but He wrote with His finger, recited by chrysolite, pearls and rubies: 'Indeed I am God, there is no god but I; My mercy has preceded My wrath.'"

Sulayman and 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar said: God, exalted is He, has a hundred mercies, each mercy of which covers what lies between the heaven and the earth. He sent down one mercy to the people of the world, and by it the humans, jinn, birds of the sky, fish of the sea, what lies between the air and the animals, and the creatures of the earth show mercy to one another. He keeps ninety-nine mercies with Himself. When the Day of Resurrection comes, He will add that mercy to what He has.

﴿He will surely gather you﴾ (6:12), the lam here is the lam of oath and the nun is the nun of emphasis. Its meaning: "By God, He will surely gather you ﴿to the Day of Resurrection﴾ (6:12)," meaning on the Day of Resurrection. "Ila" means "fi" (in). It was also said: the meaning is that He will surely gather you ﴿to the Day of Resurrection﴾ in [others], ﴿about which there is no doubt﴾ (6:12).

﴿Those who have lost themselves﴾ (6:12), meaning they were overcome by their own souls. The tanwin is in the place of the accusative, referring back to the kaf and the nun of His saying ﴿He will surely gather you﴾. It may also be nominative, as the subject, with its predicate: ﴿so they do not believe﴾ (6:12). So God, exalted is He, informed that the one who denies the Hereafter is ruined and a loser.

These six verses are Medinan, and the rest of the surah is Meccan.

It was revealed at Mecca all at once, at night, accompanied by seventy thousand angels who filled the space between the two horizons, with a loud sound of glorification and praise. The Prophet ﷺ said, "Glory be to God, the Mighty," and fell into prostration. Then he summoned the scribes, and they wrote it down that same night. [125] It has one hundred and sixty-five verses, all of them proofs against the polytheists. Its words number three thousand and fifty-two, and its letters number twelve thousand four hundred and twenty.

Ibn 'Abbas related from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Surat al-An'am was revealed to me all at once, escorted by seventy thousand angels, who had a loud sound of glorification and praise. Whoever recites Surat al-An'am, those seventy thousand angels will send blessings upon him, a day and a night for each verse of al-An'am." [126]

Muslim related from Abu Salih, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Whoever recites the first three verses of Surat al-An'am, up to His saying ﴿and He knows what you earn﴾ (6:3), God will assign to him forty thousand angels who will write for him the like of their worship until the Day of Resurrection. A angel will descend from the seventh heaven with an iron mace, and whenever Satan wishes to whisper to him and inspire something into his heart, the angel will strike him with it, a blow that leaves seventy veils between him and Satan. And when he dies, on the Day of Resurrection, he will say to the Lord, blessed and exalted: 'Give me good news, in Your shade, and eat of the fruits of Your Garden, and drink from the water of al-Kawthar, and wash in the water of al-Sabil, for You are my servant and I am your Lord.'" [127]

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: No revelation descended except that Gabriel was accompanied by four angels who guard it ﴿before him and behind him﴾ (72:27), and this is His saying, exalted is He, ﴿that He may know that they have conveyed the messages of their Lord﴾ (72:28). Except for al-An'am, for it descended accompanied by seventy thousand angels.

Sufyan related from Abu Ishaq, from 'Abd Allah ibn Khalifa, who said: 'Umar (may God be pleased with him) said:

"Al-An'am is among the essentials of the Qur'an."

In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Praise belongs to God, who created the heavens and the earth﴾ (6:1), the verse.

Muqatil said: The polytheists said to the Prophet ﷺ, "Who is your Lord?" He said: "He who created the heavens and the earth." They denied him, so God, mighty and majestic, revealed praising Himself and indicating by His attributes His existence and oneness. ﴿Praise belongs to God, who created the heavens and the earth . . .﴾ (6:1) ... ﴿in two days﴾ (41:9), Sunday and Monday, ﴿the earth in two days﴾, Tuesday and Wednesday. ﴿And He made the darknesses and the light﴾ (6:1).

al-Suddi said: It means the darkness of night and the light of day.

al-Waqidi said: Wherever in the Qur'an the words "darknesses" and "light" appear, they mean disbelief and faith.

Qatada said: It means Paradise and Hellfire. The plural "darknesses" and the singular "light" are used because light extends, whereas darkness does not extend.

The scholars of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: "Made" (ja'ala) here is a connecting element, and the Arabs mean "made" in speech.

Abu 'Ubayda said: "I have begun to see two as four, and one as two, since old age has worn me down." [128] The meaning of the verse is: Praise belongs to God who created the heavens and the earth and the darknesses and the light. It was also said: its meaning is that He created the heavens and the earth, and He has made the darknesses and the light, because He created darkness and light before creating the heavens and the earth.

Qatada said: God created the heavens before the earth, darkness before light, and Paradise before Hellfire.

Wahb said: The first thing God created was a dark place. Then He created a jewel, and it became that place. Then He looked at the jewel with a look of awe, and it turned to blood, and its vapour and foam rose up. From the vapour He created the heavens, and from the foam the earths.

'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr related from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "God, mighty and majestic, created His creation in darkness, then cast upon them some of His light. Whoever was struck by that light that day was guided, and whoever missed it went astray." [129]

﴿Yet those who disbelieve ascribe equals to their Lord﴾ (6:1).

Qutrub said: It is abbreviated, meaning: those who disbelieve after this clarification ascribe equals to their Lord, that is, they associate idols with Him. Its root is the equality of one thing with another. It is said: "I equated this with that," when I made them equal.

al-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: The "bi" in His saying ﴿ascribe equals to their Lord﴾ means "'an" (concerning), and His saying "ya'dilun" (they ascribe equals) is from 'adl (equating). That is, "yakun" and "ya'rifun" (they exist and they know).

He recited:

"And a seeker, with Tha'laba ibn Sayyar,
and she was held fast by Tha'laba's clinging."

(His reference to "ibn Sayyr" is to "ibn Sayyar"; the verse belongs to al-Mufaddal al-Bakri. See al-Sihah.)

He also recited:

"They drink with sea-water, then they are lifted up,
when the green seas have their roaring." [130]

Meaning: from the sea. God, exalted is He, said: ﴿a spring from which the servants of God drink﴾ (76:6), meaning: from it.

Muhammad ibn al-Mu'afa, from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, said: The creation was opened with praise of God, when He said: ﴿Praise belongs to God, who created the heavens and the earth﴾ (6:1), and it was closed with praise, when He said: ﴿And it will be judged between them with truth, and it will be said: Praise belongs to God, Lord of the worlds﴾ (39:75).

Hammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn al-Harith, from Wahb, said: God opened the Torah with praise, when He said: ﴿Praise belongs to God, who created the heavens and the earth﴾ (6:1), and closed it with praise, when He said: ﴿And say: Praise belongs to God, who has not taken a son﴾ (17:111), the verse. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿It is He who created you from clay﴾ (6:2), means Adam (peace be upon him). He expressed it in the form of address to them, since they were his offspring. [131]

al-Suddi said: God sent Gabriel to the earth to bring him a handful of its clay. The earth said: "I seek refuge in God from you, lest you diminish me." So he returned without taking any. He said: "O Lord, it has sought refuge in You." So He sent Michael, and it sought refuge; he returned. Then He sent the Angel of Death, and it sought refuge in God from him. He said: "I seek refuge in God from disobeying His command." He took from the surface of the earth and mixed the red, the black and the white soil. That is why the colours of the children of Adam differ. Then he kneaded it with sweet water, salt water and bitter water, and that is why their characters differ. God, mighty and majestic, said to the Angel of Death: "Gabriel and Michael had mercy on the earth, and you did not have mercy on it. Undoubtedly, I will place the spirits of whomever I create from this clay in your hand."

Abu Hurayra related from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "God created Adam from dust, made it into clay, then left it until it became black, malleable mud. He shaped and formed him, then left him until he became dry clay like pottery. [Iblis would pass by him and say:] 'You were created for a great matter!' Then God breathed into him His spirit." [132]

﴿Then He decreed a term, and a term specified with Him﴾ (6:2).

al-Hasan, Qatada and al-Dahhak said: The first term is what lies between one's creation and one's death. The second term is what lies between one's death and one's resurrection, which is the barzakh (intermediate state).

Mujahid and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: ﴿Then He decreed a term﴾ means the term of this world, ﴿and a term specified with Him﴾ is the Hereafter.

'Ata' related from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Then He decreed a term﴾ is sleep, in which the soul is seized and then returned to its owner when awake. ﴿A term specified with Him﴾ is the term of a person's death. ﴿Then He decreed a term﴾ means He made a duration for your lives, at which you will end, which you do not exceed. ﴿And a term specified﴾ means, and it is a term specified with Him, which no one knows except Him. The specified term is the term that comes later.

﴿Then you doubt﴾ (6:2), that is, you are uncertain about resurrection. ﴿And He is God in the heavens and on the earth. He knows your secret and your open﴾ (6:3), meaning: He is the God of the heavens and the God of the earth. ﴿And He knows what you earn﴾ (6:3), meaning: what you do of good and evil.

Muqatil: He knows the secrets of your deeds and their open aspects. He said: We heard Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi say: I heard Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Balkhi say: This is one of the inverted forms of speech, and its sense is: "He is God, He knows your secret and your open in the heavens and the earth, so nothing is hidden from Him."

﴿And no sign from the signs of their Lord comes to them﴾ (6:4), meaning the disbelievers of Mecca, such as the splitting of the moon or otherwise, ﴿except that they turn away from it﴾, they abandon it and deny it. ﴿They have denied the truth﴾ (6:5), meaning the Qur'an; it was also said: Muhammad (peace be upon him), ﴿when it came to them. "May a cloud from the star Pleiades' rain water you,

﴿And had We sent down to you a book on parchment﴾ (6:7), the verse.

[125] It has one hundred and sixty-five verses, all of them proofs against the polytheists. Its words number three thousand and fifty-two, and its letters number twelve thousand four hundred and twenty.

Ibn 'Abbas related from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Surat al-An'am was revealed to me all at once, escorted by seventy thousand angels, who had a loud sound of glorification and praise. Whoever recites Surat al-An'am, those seventy thousand angels will send blessings upon him, a day and a night for each verse of al-An'am." [126]

Muslim related from Abu Salih, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Whoever recites the first three verses of Surat al-An'am, up to His saying ﴿and He knows what you earn﴾ (6:3), God will assign to him forty thousand angels who will write for him the like of their worship until the Day of Resurrection. A angel will descend from the seventh heaven with an iron mace, and whenever Satan wishes to whisper to him and inspire something into his heart, the angel will strike him with it, a blow that leaves seventy veils between him and Satan. And when he dies, on the Day of Resurrection, he will say to the Lord, blessed and exalted: 'Give me good news, in Your shade, and eat of the fruits of Your Garden, and drink from the water of al-Kawthar, and wash in the water of al-Sabil, for You are my servant and I am your Lord.'" [127]

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: No revelation descended except that Gabriel was accompanied by four angels who guard it ﴿before him and behind him﴾ (72:27), and this is His saying, exalted is He, ﴿that He may know that they have conveyed the messages of their Lord﴾ (72:28). Except for al-An'am, for it descended accompanied by seventy thousand angels.

Sufyan related from Abu Ishaq, from 'Abd Allah ibn Khalifa, who said: 'Umar (may God be pleased with him) said:

"Al-An'am is among the essentials of the Qur'an."

In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Praise belongs to God, who created the heavens and the earth﴾ (6:1), the verse.

Muqatil said: The polytheists said to the Prophet ﷺ, "Who is your Lord?" He said: "He who created the heavens and the earth." They denied him, so God, mighty and majestic, revealed praising Himself and indicating by His attributes His existence and oneness. ﴿Praise belongs to God, who created the heavens and the earth . . .﴾ (6:1) ... ﴿in two days﴾ (41:9), Sunday and Monday, ﴿the earth in two days﴾, Tuesday and Wednesday. ﴿And He made the darknesses and the light﴾ (6:1).

al-Suddi said: It means the darkness of night and the light of day.

al-Waqidi said: Wherever in the Qur'an the words "darknesses" and "light" appear, they mean disbelief and faith.

Qatada said: It means Paradise and Hellfire. The plural "darknesses" and the singular "light" are used because light extends, whereas darkness does not extend.

The scholars of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: "Made" (ja'ala) here is a connecting element, and the Arabs mean "made" in speech.

Abu 'Ubayda said: "I have begun to see two as four, and one as two, since old age has worn me down." [128] The meaning of the verse is: Praise belongs to God who created the heavens and the earth and the darknesses and the light. It was also said: its meaning is that He created the heavens and the earth, and He has made the darknesses and the light, because He created darkness and light before creating the heavens and the earth.

Qatada said: God created the heavens before the earth, darkness before light, and Paradise before Hellfire.

Wahb said: The first thing God created was a dark place. Then He created a jewel, and it became that place. Then He looked at the jewel with a look of awe, and it turned to blood, and its vapour and foam rose up. From the vapour He created the heavens, and from the foam the earths.

'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr related from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "God, mighty and majestic, created His creation in darkness, then cast upon them some of His light. Whoever was struck by that light that day was guided, and whoever missed it went astray." [129]

﴿Yet those who disbelieve ascribe equals to their Lord﴾ (6:1).

Qutrub said: It is abbreviated, meaning: those who disbelieve after this clarification ascribe equals to their Lord, that is, they associate idols with Him. Its root is the equality of one thing with another. It is said: "I equated this with that," when I made them equal.

al-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: The "bi" in His saying ﴿ascribe equals to their Lord﴾ means "'an" (concerning), and His saying "ya'dilun" (they ascribe equals) is from 'adl (equating). That is, "yakun" and "ya'rifun" (they exist and they know).

He recited:

"And a seeker, with Tha'laba ibn Sayyar,
and she was held fast by Tha'laba's clinging."

(His reference to "ibn Sayyr" is to "ibn Sayyar"; the verse belongs to al-Mufaddal al-Bakri. See al-Sihah.)

He also recited:

"They drink with sea-water, then they are lifted up,
when the green seas have their roaring." [130]

Meaning: from the sea. God, exalted is He, said: ﴿a spring from which the servants of God drink﴾ (76:6), meaning: from it.

Muhammad ibn al-Mu'afa, from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, said: The creation was opened with praise of God, when He said: ﴿Praise belongs to God, who created the heavens and the earth﴾ (6:1), and it was closed with praise, when He said: ﴿And it will be judged between them with truth, and it will be said: Praise belongs to God, Lord of the worlds﴾ (39:75).

Hammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn al-Harith, from Wahb, said: God opened the Torah with praise, when He said: ﴿Praise belongs to God, who created the heavens and the earth﴾ (6:1), and closed it with praise, when He said: ﴿And say: Praise belongs to God, who has not taken a son﴾ (17:111), the verse. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿It is He who created you from clay﴾ (6:2), means Adam (peace be upon him). He expressed it in the form of address to them, since they were his offspring. [131]

al-Suddi said: God sent Gabriel to the earth to bring him a handful of its clay. The earth said: "I seek refuge in God from you, lest you diminish me." So he returned without taking any. He said: "O Lord, it has sought refuge in You." So He sent Michael, and it sought refuge; he returned. Then He sent the Angel of Death, and it sought refuge in God from him. He said: "I seek refuge in God from disobeying His command." He took from the surface of the earth and mixed the red, the black and the white soil. That is why the colours of the children of Adam differ. Then he kneaded it with sweet water, salt water and bitter water, and that is why their characters differ. God, mighty and majestic, said to the Angel of Death: "Gabriel and Michael had mercy on the earth, and you did not have mercy on it. Undoubtedly, I will place the spirits of whomever I create from this clay in your hand."

Abu Hurayra related from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "God created Adam from dust, made it into clay, then left it until it became black, malleable mud. He shaped and formed him, then left him until he became dry clay like pottery. [Iblis would pass by him and say:] 'You were created for a great matter!' Then God breathed into him His spirit." [132]

﴿Then He decreed a term, and a term specified with Him﴾ (6:2).

al-Hasan, Qatada and al-Dahhak said: The first term is what lies between one's creation and one's death. The second term is what lies between one's death and one's resurrection, which is the barzakh (intermediate state).

Mujahid and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: ﴿Then He decreed a term﴾ means the term of this world, ﴿and a term specified with Him﴾ is the Hereafter.

'Ata' related from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Then He decreed a term﴾ is sleep, in which the soul is seized and then returned to its owner when awake. ﴿A term specified with Him﴾ is the term of a person's death. ﴿Then He decreed a term﴾ means He made a duration for your lives, at which you will end, which you do not exceed. ﴿And a term specified﴾ means, and it is a term specified with Him, which no one knows except Him. The specified term is the term that comes later.

﴿Then you doubt﴾ (6:2), that is, you are uncertain about resurrection. ﴿And He is God in the heavens and on the earth. He knows your secret and your open﴾ (6:3), meaning: He is the God of the heavens and the God of the earth. ﴿And He knows what you earn﴾ (6:3), meaning: what you do of good and evil.

Muqatil: He knows the secrets of your deeds and their open aspects. He said: We heard Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi say: I heard Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Balkhi say: This is one of the inverted forms of speech, and its sense is: "He is God, He knows your secret and your open in the heavens and the earth, so nothing is hidden from Him."

﴿And no sign from the signs of their Lord comes to them﴾ (6:4), meaning the disbelievers of Mecca, such as the splitting of the moon or otherwise, ﴿except that they turn away from it﴾, they abandon it and deny it. ﴿They have denied the truth﴾ (6:5), meaning the Qur'an; it was also said: Muhammad (peace be upon him), ﴿when it came to them. So soon there will come to them the news of what they used to mock﴾ (6:5), that is, the reports of their mockery and its recompense. This is a warning to them, and the warning befell them on the day they saw it.

﴿Did they not see how many generations We destroyed before them?﴾ (6:6). Generations means the past nations. A "qarn" is a group of people, and its plural is "qurun." It was also said: a "qarn" is a period of time, said to be eighty years, or a hundred years. On this view, the meaning would be: people of a generation. ﴿We had established them on the earth as We had not established you﴾ (6:6), meaning We gave them what We had not given you.

Ibn 'Abbas said: We gave them respite in life, in bodies and in children, like the people of Noah, 'Ad and Thamud. It is also said: "I established him, and I established for him," and it came [ ... ] all together. ﴿And We sent the sky upon them in abundant rain﴾ (6:6), meaning the rain.

The Arabs say: "We kept seeing the sky until we came to you in abundant rain," meaning copious, abundant, lasting. It is an intensive form (mif'al) from the root "durr" (pouring), and the masculine and feminine are alike in it.

The poet said:

"May a cloud from the star Pleiades' rain water you,
dripping heavily, a pouring downpour."

As for His saying ﴿as We had not established you﴾, it is a second-person address that is in the form of the "tanwin" (mood). Like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿until, when you are in the ship and they sail with them﴾ (10:22).

The scholars of Basra said: He spoke of them with His saying ﴿Did they not see﴾, and among them were Muhammad and his companions, then He addressed them. The Arabs say: "I said to 'Abd Allah, how noble he is," and "I said to 'Abd Allah, I honour you." And We made the rivers flow beneath them. ﴿So We destroyed them for their sins and We raised up after them another generation﴾ (6:6), meaning We created and originated after them another generation.

﴿And had We sent down to you a book on parchment﴾ (6:7), the verse.

al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: It was revealed concerning al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Umayya and Nawfal ibn Khuwaylid. They said: "O Muhammad, we will not believe in you until you bring us a book from God, with four angels accompanying it who will testify that it is from God and that you are His messenger." So God, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿And had We sent down to you a book on parchment﴾, written from God in a sheet, ﴿and they had touched it with their hands﴾, that is, they witnessed it directly and touched it with their hands, ﴿those who disbelieve would certainly say: This is nothing but clear magic﴾ (6:7), because of what had preceded regarding them in My knowledge.

﴿And they say: Why has no angel been sent down to him?﴾ (6:8), meaning to Muhammad. ﴿Had We sent down an angel, the matter would have been decided﴾ (6:8), that is, the punishment would have become due, and their destruction would have been completed, since angels do not descend except with revelation [and the lawful]. ﴿Then they would not be respited﴾ (6:8), that is, the disbelievers would not be given time.

Mujahid said: ﴿the matter would have been decided﴾ means the Hour would have been established.

al-Dahhak said: If an angel came to them in his true form, they would die.

Qatada said: Even if We had sent down the angel and they did not believe, He would have hastened the punishment for them and not delayed them for the blink of an eye.

﴿And if We had made him an angel﴾ (6:9), meaning if We had sent an angel to them, ﴿We would have made him a man﴾, meaning in the form of a human man, because they cannot bear to look at angels. ﴿And We would have confused them﴾, meaning We would have mixed up and obscured for them ﴿what they confuse﴾, that is, they confuse and obscure for themselves, until they doubt, so that it cannot be known whether he is an angel or a human.

al-Dahhak and 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas, said: They are the People of the Book. They divided their religion and denied their messengers, and this is altering words from their places. So God confused them with what they had confused for themselves.

Qatada said: No people confused themselves without God confusing them.

al-Azhari recited "wa-la-labasna" with the doubled letter, indicating repetition. It is said: the Arabs "albasa" (confuse) "albasahu labsan," and "iltabasa 'alayhim al-amr" (the matter was confused for them), "albasahu labsan."

﴿And mocked were messengers before you﴾ (6:10), just as you were mocked, O Muhammad, consoling His Prophet ﷺ. ﴿So there surrounded﴾.

al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: "Tarak" (abandoned). 'Ata' said: "Ahal" (made lawful). Muqatil said: "Dar" (turned). al-Dahhak said: "Ihata" (encompassed).

al-Zajjaj said: "Al-hayq" in language is what overtakes a person of harm, which he has done. From it is: ﴿evil planning encompasses only its planners﴾ (35:43).

It was also said: "Wajaba" (became obligatory). "Al-hayq" and "al-hayuq" mean obligation.

﴿Those who mocked, they mocked them﴾ (6:10), ﴿what they used to mock﴾. So the punishment and the hastening of retribution surrounded those who mocked the messengers.

﴿Say, O Muhammad, to these deniers and mockers: Travel⁠ (sir), journey in the earth, taking heed; then look at how the end of the deniers was﴾ (6:11), that is, their final outcome, and how disbelief and falsehood brought them to destruction and punishment. He warns the disbelievers of Mecca of the punishment of past nations.

﴿Say: To whom belongs what is in the heavens and the earth?﴾ (6:12). If they answer you, well and good; otherwise, ﴿say: To God﴾ (6:12). He says: He will test you by the number of days, not [ ... ] and the idols. Then He said: ﴿Your Lord has prescribed for Himself mercy﴾ (6:12), that is, He decreed, out of grace and generosity, and made obligatory.

Mentioning "the self" (nafs) here is an expression of His existence and an emphasis of unity, and of the absence of intermediaries besides Him. This is an appeal from Him, exalted is He, to those who turn away from Him to turn toward Him, and an announcement that He is merciful to His servants, that He does not hasten to punish them, and that He accepts their repentance and return.

Hisham ibn Munabbih said: Abu 'Urwa related to us from Muhammad, the Messenger of God ﷺ, who said: "When God had decreed creation, He wrote in a book that is with Him above the Throne: 'Indeed My mercy precedes My wrath.'" [133]

'Umar said to Ka'b al-Ahbar: "What is the first thing God began of His creation?" Ka'b said: "God wrote a book, not with a pen or ink, but He wrote with His finger, recited by chrysolite, pearls and rubies: 'Indeed I am God, there is no god but I; My mercy has preceded My wrath.'"

Sulayman and 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar said: God, exalted is He, has a hundred mercies, each mercy of which covers what lies between the heaven and the earth. He sent down one mercy to the people of the world, and by it the humans, jinn, birds of the sky, fish of the sea, what lies between the air and the animals, and the creatures of the earth show mercy to one another. He keeps ninety-nine mercies with Himself. When the Day of Resurrection comes, He will add that mercy to what He has.

﴿He will surely gather you﴾ (6:12), the lam here is the lam of oath and the nun is the nun of emphasis. Its meaning: "By God, He will surely gather you ﴿to the Day of Resurrection﴾ (6:12)," meaning on the Day of Resurrection. "Ila" means "fi" (in). It was also said: the meaning is that He will surely gather you ﴿to the Day of Resurrection﴾ in [others], ﴿about which there is no doubt﴾ (6:12).

﴿Those who have lost themselves﴾ (6:12), meaning they were overcome by their own souls. The tanwin is in the place of the accusative, referring back to the kaf and the nun of His saying ﴿He will surely gather you﴾. It may also be nominative, as the subject, with its predicate: ﴿so they do not believe﴾ (6:12). So God, exalted is He, informed that the one who denies the Hereafter is ruined and a loser.

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 6, verses 1–12:**

It is Meccan in its entirety, except for six verses. Among them, ﴿They did not measure God with His true measure﴾ (6:91) and the following three verses were revealed in Medina, as was ﴿Say: Come, I will recite to you what your Lord has forbidden﴾ (6:151) up to ﴿so that you may be God-fearing﴾ (6:153). These six verses are Medinan, and the rest of the surah is Meccan.

It was revealed at Mecca all at once, at night, accompanied by seventy thousand angels who filled the space between the two horizons, with a loud sound of glorification and praise. The Prophet ﷺ said, "Glory be to God, the Mighty," and fell into prostration. Then he summoned the scribes, and they wrote it down that same night. [125] It has one hundred and sixty-five verses, all of them proofs against the polytheists. Its words number three thousand and fifty-two, and its letters number twelve thousand four hundred and twenty.

Ibn 'Abbas related from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Surat al-An'am was revealed to me all at once, escorted by seventy thousand angels, who had a loud sound of glorification and praise. Whoever recites Surat al-An'am, those seventy thousand angels will send blessings upon him, a day and a night for each verse of al-An'am." [126]

A angel will descend from the seventh heaven with an iron mace, and whenever Satan wishes to whisper to him and inspire something into his heart, the angel will strike him with it, a blow that leaves seventy veils between him and Satan. And when he dies, on the Day of Resurrection, he will say to the Lord, blessed and exalted: 'Give me good news, in Your shade, and eat of the fruits of Your Garden, and drink from the water of al-Kawthar, and wash in the water of al-Sabil, for You are my servant and I am your Lord.'" [127]

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: No revelation descended except that Gabriel was accompanied by four angels who guard it ﴿before him and behind him﴾ (72:27), and this is His saying, exalted is He, ﴿that He may know that they have conveyed the messages of their Lord﴾ (72:28). Except for al-An'am, for it descended accompanied by seventy thousand angels.

Sufyan related from Abu Ishaq, from 'Abd Allah ibn Khalifa, who said: 'Umar (may God be pleased with him) said:

"Al-An'am is among the essentials of the Qur'an."

In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Praise belongs to God, who created the heavens and the earth﴾ (6:1), the verse.

Muqatil said: The polytheists said to the Prophet ﷺ, "Who is your Lord?" He said: "He who created the heavens and the earth." They denied him, so God, mighty and majestic, revealed praising Himself and indicating by His attributes His existence and oneness. ﴿Praise belongs to God, who created the heavens and the earth . . .﴾ (6:1) ... ﴿in two days﴾ (41:9), Sunday and Monday, ﴿the earth in two days﴾, Tuesday and Wednesday. ﴿And He made the darknesses and the light﴾ (6:1).

al-Suddi said: It means the darkness of night and the light of day.

al-Waqidi said: Wherever in the Qur'an the words "darknesses" and "light" appear, they mean disbelief and faith.

Qatada said: It means Paradise and Hellfire. The plural "darknesses" and the singular "light" are used because light extends, whereas darkness does not extend.

[128] The meaning of the verse is: Praise belongs to God who created the heavens and the earth and the darknesses and the light. It was also said: its meaning is that He created the heavens and the earth, and He has made the darknesses and the light, because He created darkness and light before creating the heavens and the earth.

Qatada said: God created the heavens before the earth, darkness before light, and Paradise before Hellfire.

Wahb said: The first thing God created was a dark place. Then He created a jewel, and it became that place. Then He looked at the jewel with a look of awe, and it turned to blood, and its vapour and foam rose up. From the vapour He created the heavens, and from the foam the earths.

He recited:

"And a seeker, with Tha'laba ibn Sayyar,
and she was held fast by Tha'laba's clinging."

(His reference to "ibn Sayyr" is to "ibn Sayyar"; the verse belongs to al-Mufaddal al-Bakri. See al-Sihah.)

He also recited:

"They drink with sea-water, then they are lifted up,
when the green seas have their roaring." [130]

Meaning: from the sea. God, exalted is He, said: ﴿a spring from which the servants of God drink﴾ (76:6), meaning: from it.

Muhammad ibn al-Mu'afa, from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, said: The creation was opened with praise of God, when He said: ﴿Praise belongs to God, who created the heavens and the earth﴾ (6:1), and it was closed with praise, when He said: ﴿And it will be judged between them with truth, and it will be said: Praise belongs to God, Lord of the worlds﴾ (39:75).

Hammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn al-Harith, from Wahb, said: God opened the Torah with praise, when He said: ﴿Praise belongs to God, who created the heavens and the earth﴾ (6:1), and closed it with praise, when He said: ﴿And say: Praise belongs to God, who has not taken a son﴾ (17:111), the verse. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿It is He who created you from clay﴾ (6:2), means Adam (peace be upon him). He expressed it in the form of address to them, since they were his offspring. [131]

al-Suddi said: God sent Gabriel to the earth to bring him a handful of its clay. The earth said: "I seek refuge in God from you, lest you diminish me." So he returned without taking any. He said: "O Lord, it has sought refuge in You." So He sent Michael, and it sought refuge; he returned. Then He sent the Angel of Death, and it sought refuge in God from him. He shaped and formed him, then left him until he became dry clay like pottery. [Iblis would pass by him and say:] 'You were created for a great matter!' Then God breathed into him His spirit." [132]

﴿Then He decreed a term, and a term specified with Him﴾ (6:2).

al-Hasan, Qatada and al-Dahhak said: The first term is what lies between one's creation and one's death. The second term is what lies between one's death and one's resurrection, which is the barzakh (intermediate state).

Mujahid and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: ﴿Then He decreed a term﴾ means the term of this world, ﴿and a term specified with Him﴾ is the Hereafter.

'Ata' related from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Then He decreed a term﴾ is sleep, in which the soul is seized and then returned to its owner when awake. ﴿A term specified with Him﴾ is the term of a person's death. ﴿Then He decreed a term﴾ means He made a duration for your lives, at which you will end, which you do not exceed. ﴿And a term specified﴾ means, and it is a term specified with Him, which no one knows except Him. The specified term is the term that comes later.

﴿Then you doubt﴾ (6:2), that is, you are uncertain about resurrection. ﴿And He is God in the heavens and on the earth. He knows your secret and your open﴾ (6:3), meaning: He is the God of the heavens and the God of the earth. ﴿And He knows what you earn﴾ (6:3), meaning: what you do of good and evil.

Muqatil: He knows the secrets of your deeds and their open aspects. He said: We heard Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi say: I heard Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Balkhi say: This is one of the inverted forms of speech, and its sense is: "He is God, He knows your secret and your open in the heavens and the earth, so nothing is hidden from Him."

﴿And no sign from the signs of their Lord comes to them﴾ (6:4), meaning the disbelievers of Mecca, such as the splitting of the moon or otherwise, ﴿except that they turn away from it﴾, they abandon it and deny it. ﴿They have denied the truth﴾ (6:5), meaning the Qur'an; it was also said: Muhammad (peace be upon him), ﴿when it came to them. So soon there will come to them the news of what they used to mock﴾ (6:5), that is, the reports of their mockery and its recompense. This is a warning to them, and the warning befell them on the day they saw it.

It was also said: a "qarn" is a period of time, said to be eighty years, or a hundred years. On this view, the meaning would be: people of a generation. ﴿We had established them on the earth as We had not established you﴾ (6:6), meaning We gave them what We had not given you.

Ibn 'Abbas said: We gave them respite in life, in bodies and in children, like the people of Noah, 'Ad and Thamud. It is also said: "I established him, and I established for him," and it came [ ... ] all together. ﴿And We sent the sky upon them in abundant rain﴾ (6:6), meaning the rain.

The Arabs say: "We kept seeing the sky until we came to you in abundant rain," meaning copious, abundant, lasting. It is an intensive form (mif'al) from the root "durr" (pouring), and the masculine and feminine are alike in it.

The poet said:

"May a cloud from the star Pleiades' rain water you,
dripping heavily, a pouring downpour."

As for His saying ﴿as We had not established you﴾, it is a second-person address that is in the form of the "tanwin" (mood). Like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿until, when you are in the ship and they sail with them﴾ (10:22).

The scholars of Basra said: He spoke of them with His saying ﴿Did they not see﴾, and among them were Muhammad and his companions, then He addressed them. The Arabs say: "I said to 'Abd Allah, how noble he is," and "I said to 'Abd Allah, I honour you." And We made the rivers flow beneath them. ﴿So We destroyed them for their sins and We raised up after them another generation﴾ (6:6), meaning We created and originated after them another generation.

﴿And had We sent down to you a book on parchment﴾ (6:7), the verse.

al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: It was revealed concerning al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Umayya and Nawfal ibn Khuwaylid. They said: "O Muhammad, we will not believe in you until you bring us a book from God, with four angels accompanying it who will testify that it is from God and that you are His messenger." So God, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿And had We sent down to you a book on parchment﴾, written from God in a sheet, ﴿and they had touched it with their hands﴾, that is, they witnessed it directly and touched it with their hands, ﴿those who disbelieve would certainly say: This is nothing but clear magic﴾ (6:7), because of what had preceded regarding them in My knowledge.

﴿And they say: Why has no angel been sent down to him?﴾ (6:8), meaning to Muhammad. ﴿Had We sent down an angel, the matter would have been decided﴾ (6:8), that is, the punishment would have become due, and their destruction would have been completed, since angels do not descend except with revelation [and the lawful]. ﴿Then they would not be respited﴾ (6:8), that is, the disbelievers would not be given time.

Mujahid said: ﴿the matter would have been decided﴾ means the Hour would have been established.

al-Dahhak said: If an angel came to them in his true form, they would die.

Qatada said: Even if We had sent down the angel and they did not believe, He would have hastened the punishment for them and not delayed them for the blink of an eye.

﴿And if We had made him an angel﴾ (6:9), meaning if We had sent an angel to them, ﴿We would have made him a man﴾, meaning in the form of a human man, because they cannot bear to look at angels. ﴿And We would have confused them﴾, meaning We would have mixed up and obscured for them ﴿what they confuse﴾, that is, they confuse and obscure for themselves, until they doubt, so that it cannot be known whether he is an angel or a human.

al-Dahhak and 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas, said: They are the People of the Book. They divided their religion and denied their messengers, and this is altering words from their places. So God confused them with what they had confused for themselves.

Qatada said: No people confused themselves without God confusing them.

al-Azhari recited "wa-la-labasna" with the doubled letter, indicating repetition. It is said: the Arabs "albasa" (confuse) "albasahu labsan," and "iltabasa 'alayhim al-amr" (the matter was confused for them), "albasahu labsan."

﴿And mocked were messengers before you﴾ (6:10), just as you were mocked, O Muhammad, consoling His Prophet ﷺ. ﴿So there surrounded﴾.

al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: "Tarak" (abandoned). 'Ata' said: "Ahal" (made lawful). Muqatil said: "Dar" (turned). al-Dahhak said: "Ihata" (encompassed).

al-Zajjaj said: "Al-hayq" in language is what overtakes a person of harm, which he has done. From it is: ﴿evil planning encompasses only its planners﴾ (35:43).

It was also said: "Wajaba" (became obligatory). "Al-hayq" and "al-hayuq" mean obligation.

﴿Those who mocked, they mocked them﴾ (6:10), ﴿what they used to mock﴾. So the punishment and the hastening of retribution surrounded those who mocked the messengers.

﴿Say, O Muhammad, to these deniers and mockers: Travel⁠ (sir), journey in the earth, taking heed; then look at how the end of the deniers was﴾ (6:11), that is, their final outcome, and how disbelief and falsehood brought them to destruction and punishment. He warns the disbelievers of Mecca of the punishment of past nations.

﴿Say: To whom belongs what is in the heavens and the earth?﴾ (6:12). If they answer you, well and good; otherwise, ﴿say: To God﴾ (6:12). He says: He will test you by the number of days, not [ ... ] and the idols. Then He said: ﴿Your Lord has prescribed for Himself mercy﴾ (6:12), that is, He decreed, out of grace and generosity, and made obligatory.

Mentioning "the self" (nafs) here is an expression of His existence and an emphasis of unity, and of the absence of intermediaries besides Him. This is an appeal from Him, exalted is He, to those who turn away from Him to turn toward Him, and an announcement that He is merciful to His servants, that He does not hasten to punish them, and that He accepts their repentance and return.

Hisham ibn Munabbih said: Abu 'Urwa related to us from Muhammad, the Messenger of God ﷺ, who said: "When God had decreed creation, He wrote in a book that is with Him above the Throne: 'Indeed My mercy precedes My wrath.'" [133]

'Umar said to Ka'b al-Ahbar: "What is the first thing God began of His creation?" Ka'b said: "God wrote a book, not with a pen or ink, but He wrote with His finger, recited by chrysolite, pearls and rubies: 'Indeed I am God, there is no god but I; My mercy has preceded My wrath.'"

Sulayman and 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar said: God, exalted is He, has a hundred mercies, each mercy of which covers what lies between the heaven and the earth. He sent down one mercy to the people of the world, and by it the humans, jinn, birds of the sky, fish of the sea, what lies between the air and the animals, and the creatures of the earth show mercy to one another. He keeps ninety-nine mercies with Himself. When the Day of Resurrection comes, He will add that mercy to what He has.

﴿He will surely gather you﴾ (6:12), the lam here is the lam of oath and the nun is the nun of emphasis. Its meaning: "By God, He will surely gather you ﴿to the Day of Resurrection﴾ (6:12)," meaning on the Day of Resurrection. "Ila" means "fi" (in). It was also said: the meaning is that He will surely gather you ﴿to the Day of Resurrection﴾ in [others], ﴿about which there is no doubt﴾ (6:12).

﴿Those who have lost themselves﴾ (6:12), meaning they were overcome by their own souls. The tanwin is in the place of the accusative, referring back to the kaf and the nun of His saying ﴿He will surely gather you﴾. It may also be nominative, as the subject, with its predicate: ﴿so they do not believe﴾ (6:12). So God, exalted is He, informed that the one who denies the Hereafter is ruined and a loser.

These six verses are Medinan, and the rest of the surah is Meccan.

It was revealed at Mecca all at once, at night, accompanied by seventy thousand angels who filled the space between the two horizons, with a loud sound of glorification and praise. The Prophet ﷺ said, "Glory be to God, the Mighty," and fell into prostration. Then he summoned the scribes, and they wrote it down that same night. [125] It has one hundred and sixty-five verses, all of them proofs against the polytheists. Its words number three thousand and fifty-two, and its letters number twelve thousand four hundred and twenty.

Ibn 'Abbas related from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Surat al-An'am was revealed to me all at once, escorted by seventy thousand angels, who had a loud sound of glorification and praise. Whoever recites Surat al-An'am, those seventy thousand angels will send blessings upon him, a day and a night for each verse of al-An'am." [126]

Muslim related from Abu Salih, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Whoever recites the first three verses of Surat al-An'am, up to His saying ﴿and He knows what you earn﴾ (6:3), God will assign to him forty thousand angels who will write for him the like of their worship until the Day of Resurrection. A angel will descend from the seventh heaven with an iron mace, and whenever Satan wishes to whisper to him and inspire something into his heart, the angel will strike him with it, a blow that leaves seventy veils between him and Satan. And when he dies, on the Day of Resurrection, he will say to the Lord, blessed and exalted: 'Give me good news, in Your shade, and eat of the fruits of Your Garden, and drink from the water of al-Kawthar, and wash in the water of al-Sabil, for You are my servant and I am your Lord.'" [127]

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: No revelation descended except that Gabriel was accompanied by four angels who guard it ﴿before him and behind him﴾ (72:27), and this is His saying, exalted is He, ﴿that He may know that they have conveyed the messages of their Lord﴾ (72:28). Except for al-An'am, for it descended accompanied by seventy thousand angels.

Sufyan related from Abu Ishaq, from 'Abd Allah ibn Khalifa, who said: 'Umar (may God be pleased with him) said:

"Al-An'am is among the essentials of the Qur'an."

In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Praise belongs to God, who created the heavens and the earth﴾ (6:1), the verse.

al-Waqidi said: Wherever in the Qur'an the words "darknesses" and "light" appear, they mean disbelief and faith.

Qatada said: It means Paradise and Hellfire. The plural "darknesses" and the singular "light" are used because light extends, whereas darkness does not extend.

The scholars of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: "Made" (ja'ala) here is a connecting element, and the Arabs mean "made" in speech.

Abu 'Ubayda said: "I have begun to see two as four, and one as two, since old age has worn me down." [128] The meaning of the verse is: Praise belongs to God who created the heavens and the earth and the darknesses and the light. It was also said: its meaning is that He created the heavens and the earth, and He has made the darknesses and the light, because He created darkness and light before creating the heavens and the earth.

Qatada said: God created the heavens before the earth, darkness before light, and Paradise before Hellfire.

Wahb said: The first thing God created was a dark place. Then He created a jewel, and it became that place. Then He looked at the jewel with a look of awe, and it turned to blood, and its vapour and foam rose up. From the vapour He created the heavens, and from the foam the earths.

'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr related from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "God, mighty and majestic, created His creation in darkness, then cast upon them some of His light. Whoever was struck by that light that day was guided, and whoever missed it went astray." [129]

﴿Yet those who disbelieve ascribe equals to their Lord﴾ (6:1).

Qutrub said: It is abbreviated, meaning: those who disbelieve after this clarification ascribe equals to their Lord, that is, they associate idols with Him. Its root is the equality of one thing with another. It is said: "I equated this with that," when I made them equal.

al-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: The "bi" in His saying ﴿ascribe equals to their Lord﴾ means "'an" (concerning), and His saying "ya'dilun" (they ascribe equals) is from 'adl (equating). That is, "yakun" and "ya'rifun" (they exist and they know).

He recited:

"And a seeker, with Tha'laba ibn Sayyar,
and she was held fast by Tha'laba's clinging."

(His reference to "ibn Sayyr" is to "ibn Sayyar"; the verse belongs to al-Mufaddal al-Bakri. See al-Sihah.)

He also recited:

"They drink with sea-water, then they are lifted up,
when the green seas have their roaring." [130]

Meaning: from the sea. God, exalted is He, said: ﴿a spring from which the servants of God drink﴾ (76:6), meaning: from it.

Muhammad ibn al-Mu'afa, from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, said: The creation was opened with praise of God, when He said: ﴿Praise belongs to God, who created the heavens and the earth﴾ (6:1), and it was closed with praise, when He said: ﴿And it will be judged between them with truth, and it will be said: Praise belongs to God, Lord of the worlds﴾ (39:75).

Hammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn al-Harith, from Wahb, said: God opened the Torah with praise, when He said: ﴿Praise belongs to God, who created the heavens and the earth﴾ (6:1), and closed it with praise, when He said: ﴿And say: Praise belongs to God, who has not taken a son﴾ (17:111), the verse. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿It is He who created you from clay﴾ (6:2), means Adam (peace be upon him). He expressed it in the form of address to them, since they were his offspring. [131]

al-Suddi said: God sent Gabriel to the earth to bring him a handful of its clay. The earth said: "I seek refuge in God from you, lest you diminish me." So he returned without taking any. He said: "O Lord, it has sought refuge in You." So He sent Michael, and it sought refuge; he returned. Then He sent the Angel of Death, and it sought refuge in God from him. He said: "I seek refuge in God from disobeying His command." He took from the surface of the earth and mixed the red, the black and the white soil. That is why the colours of the children of Adam differ. Then he kneaded it with sweet water, salt water and bitter water, and that is why their characters differ. God, mighty and majestic, said to the Angel of Death: "Gabriel and Michael had mercy on the earth, and you did not have mercy on it. Undoubtedly, I will place the spirits of whomever I create from this clay in your hand."

Abu Hurayra related from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "God created Adam from dust, made it into clay, then left it until it became black, malleable mud. ﴿Then He decreed a term, and a term specified with Him﴾ (6:2).

al-Hasan, Qatada and al-Dahhak said: The first term is what lies between one's creation and one's death. The second term is what lies between one's death and one's resurrection, which is the barzakh (intermediate state).

Mujahid and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: ﴿Then He decreed a term﴾ means the term of this world, ﴿and a term specified with Him﴾ is the Hereafter.

'Ata' related from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Then He decreed a term﴾ is sleep, in which the soul is seized and then returned to its owner when awake. ﴿A term specified with Him﴾ is the term of a person's death. ﴿Then He decreed a term﴾ means He made a duration for your lives, at which you will end, which you do not exceed. ﴿And a term specified﴾ means, and it is a term specified with Him, which no one knows except Him. The specified term is the term that comes later.

﴿Then you doubt﴾ (6:2), that is, you are uncertain about resurrection. ﴿And He is God in the heavens and on the earth. He knows your secret and your open﴾ (6:3), meaning: He is the God of the heavens and the God of the earth. ﴿And He knows what you earn﴾ (6:3), meaning: what you do of good and evil.

Muqatil: He knows the secrets of your deeds and their open aspects. He said: We heard Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi say: I heard Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Balkhi say: This is one of the inverted forms of speech, and its sense is: "He is God, He knows your secret and your open in the heavens and the earth, so nothing is hidden from Him."

﴿And no sign from the signs of their Lord comes to them﴾ (6:4), meaning the disbelievers of Mecca, such as the splitting of the moon or otherwise, ﴿except that they turn away from it﴾, they abandon it and deny it. ﴿They have denied the truth﴾ (6:5), meaning the Qur'an; it was also said: Muhammad (peace be upon him), ﴿when it came to them. So soon there will come to them the news of what they used to mock﴾ (6:5), that is, the reports of their mockery and its recompense. This is a warning to them, and the warning befell them on the day they saw it.

﴿Did they not see how many generations We destroyed before them?﴾ (6:6). Generations means the past nations. A "qarn" is a group of people, and its plural is "qurun." It was also said: a "qarn" is a period of time, said to be eighty years, or a hundred years. On this view, the meaning would be: people of a generation. ﴿We had established them on the earth as We had not established you﴾ (6:6), meaning We gave them what We had not given you.

Ibn 'Abbas said: We gave them respite in life, in bodies and in children, like the people of Noah, 'Ad and Thamud. It is also said: "I established him, and I established for him," and it came [ ... ] all together. ﴿And We sent the sky upon them in abundant rain﴾ (6:6), meaning the rain.

"May a cloud from the star Pleiades' rain water you,

﴿And had We sent down to you a book on parchment﴾ (6:7), the verse.

al-Dahhak said: If an angel came to them in his true form, they would die.
