"May a cloud from the star Pleiades' rain water you,
dripping heavily, a pouring downpour."

As for His saying ﴿as We had not established you﴾, it is a second-person address that is in the form of the "tanwin" (mood). Like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿until, when you are in the ship and they sail with them﴾ (10:22).

The scholars of Basra said: He spoke of them with His saying ﴿Did they not see﴾, and among them were Muhammad and his companions, then He addressed them. The Arabs say: "I said to 'Abd Allah, how noble he is," and "I said to 'Abd Allah, I honour you." And We made the rivers flow beneath them. ﴿So We destroyed them for their sins and We raised up after them another generation﴾ (6:6), meaning We created and originated after them another generation.

﴿And had We sent down to you a book on parchment﴾ (6:7), the verse.

al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: It was revealed concerning al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Umayya and Nawfal ibn Khuwaylid. They said: "O Muhammad, we will not believe in you until you bring us a book from God, with four angels accompanying it who will testify that it is from God and that you are His messenger." So God, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿And had We sent down to you a book on parchment﴾, written from God in a sheet, ﴿and they had touched it with their hands﴾, that is, they witnessed it directly and touched it with their hands, ﴿those who disbelieve would certainly say: This is nothing but clear magic﴾ (6:7), because of what had preceded regarding them in My knowledge.

﴿And they say: Why has no angel been sent down to him?﴾ (6:8), meaning to Muhammad. ﴿Had We sent down an angel, the matter would have been decided﴾ (6:8), that is, the punishment would have become due, and their destruction would have been completed, since angels do not descend except with revelation [and the lawful]. ﴿Then they would not be respited﴾ (6:8), that is, the disbelievers would not be given time.

Mujahid said: ﴿the matter would have been decided﴾ means the Hour would have been established.

al-Dahhak said: If an angel came to them in his true form, they would die.

Qatada said: Even if We had sent down the angel and they did not believe, He would have hastened the punishment for them and not delayed them for the blink of an eye.

﴿And if We had made him an angel﴾ (6:9), meaning if We had sent an angel to them, ﴿We would have made him a man﴾, meaning in the form of a human man, because they cannot bear to look at angels. ﴿And We would have confused them﴾, meaning We would have mixed up and obscured for them ﴿what they confuse﴾, that is, they confuse and obscure for themselves, until they doubt, so that it cannot be known whether he is an angel or a human.

al-Dahhak and 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas, said: They are the People of the Book. They divided their religion and denied their messengers, and this is altering words from their places. So God confused them with what they had confused for themselves.

Qatada said: No people confused themselves without God confusing them.

al-Azhari recited "wa-la-labasna" with the doubled letter, indicating repetition. It is said: the Arabs "albasa" (confuse) "albasahu labsan," and "iltabasa 'alayhim al-amr" (the matter was confused for them), "albasahu labsan."

﴿And mocked were messengers before you﴾ (6:10), just as you were mocked, O Muhammad, consoling His Prophet ﷺ. ﴿So there surrounded﴾.

al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: "Tarak" (abandoned). 'Ata' said: "Ahal" (made lawful). Muqatil said: "Dar" (turned). al-Dahhak said: "Ihata" (encompassed).

al-Zajjaj said: "Al-hayq" in language is what overtakes a person of harm, which he has done. From it is: ﴿evil planning encompasses only its planners﴾ (35:43).

It was also said: "Wajaba" (became obligatory). "Al-hayq" and "al-hayuq" mean obligation.

﴿Those who mocked, they mocked them﴾ (6:10), ﴿what they used to mock﴾. So the punishment and the hastening of retribution surrounded those who mocked the messengers.

﴿Say, O Muhammad, to these deniers and mockers: Travel⁠ (sir), journey in the earth, taking heed; then look at how the end of the deniers was﴾ (6:11), that is, their final outcome, and how disbelief and falsehood brought them to destruction and punishment. He warns the disbelievers of Mecca of the punishment of past nations.

﴿Say: To whom belongs what is in the heavens and the earth?﴾ (6:12). If they answer you, well and good; otherwise, ﴿say: To God﴾ (6:12). He says: He will test you by the number of days, not [ ... ] and the idols. Then He said: ﴿Your Lord has prescribed for Himself mercy﴾ (6:12), that is, He decreed, out of grace and generosity, and made obligatory.

Mentioning "the self" (nafs) here is an expression of His existence and an emphasis of unity, and of the absence of intermediaries besides Him. This is an appeal from Him, exalted is He, to those who turn away from Him to turn toward Him, and an announcement that He is merciful to His servants, that He does not hasten to punish them, and that He accepts their repentance and return.

Hisham ibn Munabbih said: Abu 'Urwa related to us from Muhammad, the Messenger of God ﷺ, who said: "When God had decreed creation, He wrote in a book that is with Him above the Throne: 'Indeed My mercy precedes My wrath.'" [133]

'Umar said to Ka'b al-Ahbar: "What is the first thing God began of His creation?" Ka'b said: "God wrote a book, not with a pen or ink, but He wrote with His finger, recited by chrysolite, pearls and rubies: 'Indeed I am God, there is no god but I; My mercy has preceded My wrath.'"

Sulayman and 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar said: God, exalted is He, has a hundred mercies, each mercy of which covers what lies between the heaven and the earth. He sent down one mercy to the people of the world, and by it the humans, jinn, birds of the sky, fish of the sea, what lies between the air and the animals, and the creatures of the earth show mercy to one another. He keeps ninety-nine mercies with Himself. When the Day of Resurrection comes, He will add that mercy to what He has.

﴿He will surely gather you﴾ (6:12), the lam here is the lam of oath and the nun is the nun of emphasis. Its meaning: "By God, He will surely gather you ﴿to the Day of Resurrection﴾ (6:12)," meaning on the Day of Resurrection. "Ila" means "fi" (in). It was also said: the meaning is that He will surely gather you ﴿to the Day of Resurrection﴾ in [others], ﴿about which there is no doubt﴾ (6:12).

﴿Those who have lost themselves﴾ (6:12), meaning they were overcome by their own souls. The tanwin is in the place of the accusative, referring back to the kaf and the nun of His saying ﴿He will surely gather you﴾. It may also be nominative, as the subject, with its predicate: ﴿so they do not believe﴾ (6:12). So God, exalted is He, informed that the one who denies the Hereafter is ruined and a loser.

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 6, verses 1–12:**

It is Meccan in its entirety, except for six verses. Among them, ﴿They did not measure God with His true measure﴾ (6:91) and the following three verses were revealed in Medina, as was ﴿Say: Come, I will recite to you what your Lord has forbidden﴾ (6:151) up to ﴿so that you may be God-fearing﴾ (6:153). These six verses are Medinan, and the rest of the surah is Meccan.

It was revealed at Mecca all at once, at night, accompanied by seventy thousand angels who filled the space between the two horizons, with a loud sound of glorification and praise. The Prophet ﷺ said, "Glory be to God, the Mighty," and fell into prostration. Then he summoned the scribes, and they wrote it down that same night. [125] It has one hundred and sixty-five verses, all of them proofs against the polytheists. Its words number three thousand and fifty-two, and its letters number twelve thousand four hundred and twenty.

Ibn 'Abbas related from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Surat al-An'am was revealed to me all at once, escorted by seventy thousand angels, who had a loud sound of glorification and praise. Whoever recites Surat al-An'am, those seventy thousand angels will send blessings upon him, a day and a night for each verse of al-An'am." [126]

Muslim related from Abu Salih, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Whoever recites the first three verses of Surat al-An'am, up to His saying ﴿and He knows what you earn﴾ (6:3), God will assign to him forty thousand angels who will write for him the like of their worship until the Day of Resurrection. A angel will descend from the seventh heaven with an iron mace, and whenever Satan wishes to whisper to him and inspire something into his heart, the angel will strike him with it, a blow that leaves seventy veils between him and Satan. And when he dies, on the Day of Resurrection, he will say to the Lord, blessed and exalted: 'Give me good news, in Your shade, and eat of the fruits of Your Garden, and drink from the water of al-Kawthar, and wash in the water of al-Sabil, for You are my servant and I am your Lord.'" [127]

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: No revelation descended except that Gabriel was accompanied by four angels who guard it ﴿before him and behind him﴾ (72:27), and this is His saying, exalted is He, ﴿that He may know that they have conveyed the messages of their Lord﴾ (72:28). Except for al-An'am, for it descended accompanied by seventy thousand angels.

Sufyan related from Abu Ishaq, from 'Abd Allah ibn Khalifa, who said: 'Umar (may God be pleased with him) said:

"Al-An'am is among the essentials of the Qur'an."

In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Praise belongs to God, who created the heavens and the earth﴾ (6:1), the verse.

Muqatil said: The polytheists said to the Prophet ﷺ, "Who is your Lord?" He said: "He who created the heavens and the earth." They denied him, so God, mighty and majestic, revealed praising Himself and indicating by His attributes His existence and oneness. ﴿Praise belongs to God, who created the heavens and the earth . . .﴾ (6:1) ... ﴿in two days﴾ (41:9), Sunday and Monday, ﴿the earth in two days﴾, Tuesday and Wednesday. ﴿And He made the darknesses and the light﴾ (6:1).

al-Suddi said: It means the darkness of night and the light of day.

al-Waqidi said: Wherever in the Qur'an the words "darknesses" and "light" appear, they mean disbelief and faith.

Qatada said: It means Paradise and Hellfire. The plural "darknesses" and the singular "light" are used because light extends, whereas darkness does not extend.

The scholars of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: "Made" (ja'ala) here is a connecting element, and the Arabs mean "made" in speech.

Abu 'Ubayda said: "I have begun to see two as four, and one as two, since old age has worn me down." [128] The meaning of the verse is: Praise belongs to God who created the heavens and the earth and the darknesses and the light. It was also said: its meaning is that He created the heavens and the earth, and He has made the darknesses and the light, because He created darkness and light before creating the heavens and the earth.

Qatada said: God created the heavens before the earth, darkness before light, and Paradise before Hellfire.

Wahb said: The first thing God created was a dark place. Then He created a jewel, and it became that place. Then He looked at the jewel with a look of awe, and it turned to blood, and its vapour and foam rose up. From the vapour He created the heavens, and from the foam the earths.

'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr related from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "God, mighty and majestic, created His creation in darkness, then cast upon them some of His light. Whoever was struck by that light that day was guided, and whoever missed it went astray." [129]

﴿Yet those who disbelieve ascribe equals to their Lord﴾ (6:1).

Qutrub said: It is abbreviated, meaning: those who disbelieve after this clarification ascribe equals to their Lord, that is, they associate idols with Him. Its root is the equality of one thing with another. It is said: "I equated this with that," when I made them equal.

al-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: The "bi" in His saying ﴿ascribe equals to their Lord﴾ means "'an" (concerning), and His saying "ya'dilun" (they ascribe equals) is from 'adl (equating). That is, "yakun" and "ya'rifun" (they exist and they know).

He recited:

"And a seeker, with Tha'laba ibn Sayyar,
and she was held fast by Tha'laba's clinging."

(His reference to "ibn Sayyr" is to "ibn Sayyar"; the verse belongs to al-Mufaddal al-Bakri. See al-Sihah.)

He also recited:

"They drink with sea-water, then they are lifted up,
when the green seas have their roaring." [130]

Meaning: from the sea. God, exalted is He, said: ﴿a spring from which the servants of God drink﴾ (76:6), meaning: from it.

Muhammad ibn al-Mu'afa, from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, said: The creation was opened with praise of God, when He said: ﴿Praise belongs to God, who created the heavens and the earth﴾ (6:1), and it was closed with praise, when He said: ﴿And it will be judged between them with truth, and it will be said: Praise belongs to God, Lord of the worlds﴾ (39:75).

Hammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn al-Harith, from Wahb, said: God opened the Torah with praise, when He said: ﴿Praise belongs to God, who created the heavens and the earth﴾ (6:1), and closed it with praise, when He said: ﴿And say: Praise belongs to God, who has not taken a son﴾ (17:111), the verse. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿It is He who created you from clay﴾ (6:2), means Adam (peace be upon him). He expressed it in the form of address to them, since they were his offspring. [131]

al-Suddi said: God sent Gabriel to the earth to bring him a handful of its clay. The earth said: "I seek refuge in God from you, lest you diminish me." So he returned without taking any. He said: "O Lord, it has sought refuge in You." So He sent Michael, and it sought refuge; he returned. Then He sent the Angel of Death, and it sought refuge in God from him. He said: "I seek refuge in God from disobeying His command." He took from the surface of the earth and mixed the red, the black and the white soil. That is why the colours of the children of Adam differ. Then he kneaded it with sweet water, salt water and bitter water, and that is why their characters differ. God, mighty and majestic, said to the Angel of Death: "Gabriel and Michael had mercy on the earth, and you did not have mercy on it. Undoubtedly, I will place the spirits of whomever I create from this clay in your hand."

Abu Hurayra related from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "God created Adam from dust, made it into clay, then left it until it became black, malleable mud. He shaped and formed him, then left him until he became dry clay like pottery. [Iblis would pass by him and say:] 'You were created for a great matter!' Then God breathed into him His spirit." [132]

﴿Then He decreed a term, and a term specified with Him﴾ (6:2).

al-Hasan, Qatada and al-Dahhak said: The first term is what lies between one's creation and one's death. The second term is what lies between one's death and one's resurrection, which is the barzakh (intermediate state).

Mujahid and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: ﴿Then He decreed a term﴾ means the term of this world, ﴿and a term specified with Him﴾ is the Hereafter.

'Ata' related from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Then He decreed a term﴾ is sleep, in which the soul is seized and then returned to its owner when awake. ﴿A term specified with Him﴾ is the term of a person's death. ﴿Then He decreed a term﴾ means He made a duration for your lives, at which you will end, which you do not exceed. ﴿And a term specified﴾ means, and it is a term specified with Him, which no one knows except Him. The specified term is the term that comes later.

﴿Then you doubt﴾ (6:2), that is, you are uncertain about resurrection. ﴿And He is God in the heavens and on the earth. He knows your secret and your open﴾ (6:3), meaning: He is the God of the heavens and the God of the earth. ﴿And He knows what you earn﴾ (6:3), meaning: what you do of good and evil.

Muqatil: He knows the secrets of your deeds and their open aspects. He said: We heard Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi say: I heard Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Balkhi say: This is one of the inverted forms of speech, and its sense is: "He is God, He knows your secret and your open in the heavens and the earth, so nothing is hidden from Him."

﴿And no sign from the signs of their Lord comes to them﴾ (6:4), meaning the disbelievers of Mecca, such as the splitting of the moon or otherwise, ﴿except that they turn away from it﴾, they abandon it and deny it. ﴿They have denied the truth﴾ (6:5), meaning the Qur'an; it was also said: Muhammad (peace be upon him), ﴿when it came to them. So soon there will come to them the news of what they used to mock﴾ (6:5), that is, the reports of their mockery and its recompense. This is a warning to them, and the warning befell them on the day they saw it.

﴿Did they not see how many generations We destroyed before them?﴾ (6:6). Generations means the past nations. A "qarn" is a group of people, and its plural is "qurun." It was also said: a "qarn" is a period of time, said to be eighty years, or a hundred years. On this view, the meaning would be: people of a generation. ﴿We had established them on the earth as We had not established you﴾ (6:6), meaning We gave them what We had not given you.

Ibn 'Abbas said: We gave them respite in life, in bodies and in children, like the people of Noah, 'Ad and Thamud. It is also said: "I established him, and I established for him," and it came [ ... ] all together. ﴿And We sent the sky upon them in abundant rain﴾ (6:6), meaning the rain.

The Arabs say: "We kept seeing the sky until we came to you in abundant rain," meaning copious, abundant, lasting. It is an intensive form (mif'al) from the root "durr" (pouring), and the masculine and feminine are alike in it.

The poet said:

"May a cloud from the star Pleiades' rain water you,
dripping heavily, a pouring downpour."

As for His saying ﴿as We had not established you﴾, it is a second-person address that is in the form of the "tanwin" (mood). Like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿until, when you are in the ship and they sail with them﴾ (10:22).

The scholars of Basra said: He spoke of them with His saying ﴿Did they not see﴾, and among them were Muhammad and his companions, then He addressed them. The Arabs say: "I said to 'Abd Allah, how noble he is," and "I said to 'Abd Allah, I honour you." And We made the rivers flow beneath them. ﴿So We destroyed them for their sins and We raised up after them another generation﴾ (6:6), meaning We created and originated after them another generation.

﴿And had We sent down to you a book on parchment﴾ (6:7), the verse.

al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: It was revealed concerning al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Umayya and Nawfal ibn Khuwaylid. They said: "O Muhammad, we will not believe in you until you bring us a book from God, with four angels accompanying it who will testify that it is from God and that you are His messenger." So God, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿And had We sent down to you a book on parchment﴾, written from God in a sheet, ﴿and they had touched it with their hands﴾, that is, they witnessed it directly and touched it with their hands, ﴿those who disbelieve would certainly say: This is nothing but clear magic﴾ (6:7), because of what had preceded regarding them in My knowledge.

﴿And they say: Why has no angel been sent down to him?﴾ (6:8), meaning to Muhammad. ﴿Had We sent down an angel, the matter would have been decided﴾ (6:8), that is, the punishment would have become due, and their destruction would have been completed, since angels do not descend except with revelation [and the lawful]. ﴿Then they would not be respited﴾ (6:8), that is, the disbelievers would not be given time.

Mujahid said: ﴿the matter would have been decided﴾ means the Hour would have been established.

al-Dahhak said: If an angel came to them in his true form, they would die.

Qatada said: Even if We had sent down the angel and they did not believe, He would have hastened the punishment for them and not delayed them for the blink of an eye.

﴿And if We had made him an angel﴾ (6:9), meaning if We had sent an angel to them, ﴿We would have made him a man﴾, meaning in the form of a human man, because they cannot bear to look at angels. ﴿And We would have confused them﴾, meaning We would have mixed up and obscured for them ﴿what they confuse﴾, that is, they confuse and obscure for themselves, until they doubt, so that it cannot be known whether he is an angel or a human.

al-Dahhak and 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas, said: They are the People of the Book. They divided their religion and denied their messengers, and this is altering words from their places. So God confused them with what they had confused for themselves.

Qatada said: No people confused themselves without God confusing them.

al-Azhari recited "wa-la-labasna" with the doubled letter, indicating repetition. It is said: the Arabs "albasa" (confuse) "albasahu labsan," and "iltabasa 'alayhim al-amr" (the matter was confused for them), "albasahu labsan."

﴿And mocked were messengers before you﴾ (6:10), just as you were mocked, O Muhammad, consoling His Prophet ﷺ. ﴿So there surrounded﴾.

al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: "Tarak" (abandoned). 'Ata' said: "Ahal" (made lawful). Muqatil said: "Dar" (turned). al-Dahhak said: "Ihata" (encompassed).

al-Zajjaj said: "Al-hayq" in language is what overtakes a person of harm, which he has done. From it is: ﴿evil planning encompasses only its planners﴾ (35:43).

It was also said: "Wajaba" (became obligatory). "Al-hayq" and "al-hayuq" mean obligation.

﴿Those who mocked, they mocked them﴾ (6:10), ﴿what they used to mock﴾. So the punishment and the hastening of retribution surrounded those who mocked the messengers.

﴿Say, O Muhammad, to these deniers and mockers: Travel⁠ (sir), journey in the earth, taking heed; then look at how the end of the deniers was﴾ (6:11), that is, their final outcome, and how disbelief and falsehood brought them to destruction and punishment. He warns the disbelievers of Mecca of the punishment of past nations.

﴿Say: To whom belongs what is in the heavens and the earth?﴾ (6:12). If they answer you, well and good; otherwise, ﴿say: To God﴾ (6:12). He says: He will test you by the number of days, not [ ... ] and the idols. Then He said: ﴿Your Lord has prescribed for Himself mercy﴾ (6:12), that is, He decreed, out of grace and generosity, and made obligatory.

Mentioning "the self" (nafs) here is an expression of His existence and an emphasis of unity, and of the absence of intermediaries besides Him. This is an appeal from Him, exalted is He, to those who turn away from Him to turn toward Him, and an announcement that He is merciful to His servants, that He does not hasten to punish them, and that He accepts their repentance and return.

Hisham ibn Munabbih said: Abu 'Urwa related to us from Muhammad, the Messenger of God ﷺ, who said: "When God had decreed creation, He wrote in a book that is with Him above the Throne: 'Indeed My mercy precedes My wrath.'" [133]

'Umar said to Ka'b al-Ahbar: "What is the first thing God began of His creation?" Ka'b said: "God wrote a book, not with a pen or ink, but He wrote with His finger, recited by chrysolite, pearls and rubies: 'Indeed I am God, there is no god but I; My mercy has preceded My wrath.'"

Sulayman and 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar said: God, exalted is He, has a hundred mercies, each mercy of which covers what lies between the heaven and the earth. He sent down one mercy to the people of the world, and by it the humans, jinn, birds of the sky, fish of the sea, what lies between the air and the animals, and the creatures of the earth show mercy to one another. He keeps ninety-nine mercies with Himself. When the Day of Resurrection comes, He will add that mercy to what He has.

﴿He will surely gather you﴾ (6:12), the lam here is the lam of oath and the nun is the nun of emphasis. Its meaning: "By God, He will surely gather you ﴿to the Day of Resurrection﴾ (6:12)," meaning on the Day of Resurrection. "Ila" means "fi" (in). It was also said: the meaning is that He will surely gather you ﴿to the Day of Resurrection﴾ in [others], ﴿about which there is no doubt﴾ (6:12).

﴿Those who have lost themselves﴾ (6:12), meaning they were overcome by their own souls. The tanwin is in the place of the accusative, referring back to the kaf and the nun of His saying ﴿He will surely gather you﴾. It may also be nominative, as the subject, with its predicate: ﴿so they do not believe﴾ (6:12). So God, exalted is He, informed that the one who denies the Hereafter is ruined and a loser.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 6, verse 13–18:

﴿And to Him belongs whatever dwells in the night and the day.﴾ (the verse)

Al-Kalbi said: The disbelievers of Makkah said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "O Muhammad, we know that nothing moves you to what you call us to except need. So we will gather for you some of our wealth, so that you may be made rich, until you become the richest of us." So Allah the Exalted revealed His words: ﴿And to Him belongs whatever dwells (sakana, i.e., settles) in the night and the day﴾, meaning whatever is created.

Abu Rawh said: Among creation are things that settle by day and disperse by night, and among them are things that settle by night and disperse by day.

'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Yahya and Muhammad ibn Jarir said: Everything over which the sun rises and sets belongs to what dwells in the night and the day, and what is meant is all that is on the earth, because nothing of Allah's creation, the Mighty and Majestic, fails to dwell in the night and the day. It was also said: its meaning is ﴿whatever the night and the day pass over﴾.

The people of the meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: In the verse there are two readings, and its figurative sense (majaz) is abridged: ﴿And to Him belongs whatever dwells and moves (wa-shara) in the night and the day﴾, like His saying ﴿robes that protect you from the heat and the cold﴾ (16:81), meaning "and the cold." He intends "in everything." ﴿And He is the All-Hearing of their voices, the All-Knowing of their secrets.﴾

Al-Kalbi said: It means ﴿He is the All-Hearing of the speech of the Quraysh, the All-Knowing of who earns their provision.﴾ Say, O Muhammad: ﴿Shall I take as a protector (waliyy)﴾ other than Allah, a lord (rabb) worshipped, and a helper and supporter? ﴿Originator of the heavens and the earth﴾, meaning their Creator, their Innovator, and their Beginner. The root of fatr is splitting, from which comes "the camel's tooth split (fatara) when it cracks and begins to emerge."

Mujahid said: I heard Ibn 'Abbas say: "I did not know what ﴿Originator of the heavens and the earth﴾ meant until two Bedouins came to me disputing over a camel. One of them said to the other: 'I originated it (fatartuha), I brought it into being.'" ﴿And He feeds but is not fed﴾, meaning He provides sustenance and is not provided for. To this relates His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿I do not want provision from them, nor do I want them to feed Me﴾ (51:57).

'Ikrimah and al-A'mash recited: ﴿and He is not fed (wa-la yut'amu)﴾ with a fatha on the ya', meaning He provides sustenance and does not eat.

Ashhab al-'Uqayli recited: ﴿wa-huwa yut'imu wa-la yut'imu﴾, both with a damma on the ya' and a kasra on the 'ayn.

Al-Hasan ibn al-Fadl said: Its meaning is that He is able to feed and to refrain from feeding, like His saying ﴿He extends provision to whom He wills and restricts it﴾ (13:26).

I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi say: I heard Abu Mansur al-Azhari say in Harat: its meaning is ﴿and He feeds but is not sought to feed (wa-la yustat'im)﴾. The Arabs say: "I fed others," meaning "I asked them to feed me."

He recited:

"We feed whoever is in summer a feast,
and in winter when the gourds are not sought (for food)..."

Shihab ibn Harash narrated from 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Umayr from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: A mule was presented as a gift to the Prophet (ﷺ), one that Khosrow had sent him. Jahl ibn Shi'r mounted it, then seated me behind him and travelled with me for a while. Then he turned to me and said: "O boy." I said: "At your service, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Guard Allah and He will guard you. Guard Allah and you will find Him before you. Make yourself known to Allah in ease and He will know you in hardship. When you ask, ask Allah, and when you seek help, seek help from Allah. The pen has already run with what is to occur. If all creation were to try to benefit you with what Allah has not decreed for you, they could not do it; and if they strove to help you with what Allah has not written for you, they could not do it. If you are able to act with patience together with certainty, then do so; and if you are not able, then be patient, for in patience over what you dislike there is much good. Know that victory comes with patience, that with hardship comes ease, and that with difficulty comes ease."

﴿And He is the Subduer over His servants﴾, the Capable, the Dominant. In subjugation (qahr) there is a meaning beyond capability, which is preventing another from reaching his aim (Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 6/399).

﴿And He is the All-Wise in His command, the All-Aware of what comes from His servants.﴾

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 6, verse 13–18:

﴿And to Him belongs whatever dwells in the night and the day.﴾ (the verse)

Al-Kalbi said: The disbelievers of Makkah said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "O Muhammad, we know that nothing moves you to what you call us to except need. So we will gather for you some of our wealth, so that you may be made rich, until you become the richest of us." So Allah the Exalted revealed His words: ﴿And to Him belongs whatever dwells (sakana, i.e., settles) in the night and the day﴾, meaning whatever is created.

Abu Rawh said: Among creation are things that settle by day and disperse by night, and among them are things that settle by night and disperse by day.

'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Yahya and Muhammad ibn Jarir said: Everything over which the sun rises and sets belongs to what dwells in the night and the day, and what is meant is all that is on the earth, because nothing of Allah's creation, the Mighty and Majestic, fails to dwell in the night and the day. It was also said: its meaning is ﴿whatever the night and the day pass over﴾.

The people of the meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: In the verse there are two readings, and its figurative sense (majaz) is abridged: ﴿And to Him belongs whatever dwells and moves (wa-shara) in the night and the day﴾, like His saying ﴿robes that protect you from the heat and the cold﴾ (16:81), meaning "and the cold." He intends "in everything." ﴿And He is the All-Hearing of their voices, the All-Knowing of their secrets.﴾

Al-Kalbi said: It means ﴿He is the All-Hearing of the speech of the Quraysh, the All-Knowing of who earns their provision.﴾ Say, O Muhammad: ﴿Shall I take as a protector (waliyy)﴾ other than Allah, a lord (rabb) worshipped, and a helper and supporter? ﴿Originator of the heavens and the earth﴾, meaning their Creator, their Innovator, and their Beginner. The root of fatr is splitting, from which comes "the camel's tooth split (fatara) when it cracks and begins to emerge."

Mujahid said: I heard Ibn 'Abbas say: "I did not know what ﴿Originator of the heavens and the earth﴾ meant until two Bedouins came to me disputing over a camel. One of them said to the other: 'I originated it (fatartuha), I brought it into being.'" ﴿And He feeds but is not fed﴾, meaning He provides sustenance and is not provided for. To this relates His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿I do not want provision from them, nor do I want them to feed Me﴾ (51:57).

'Ikrimah and al-A'mash recited: ﴿and He is not fed (wa-la yut'amu)﴾ with a fatha on the ya', meaning He provides sustenance and does not eat.

Ashhab al-'Uqayli recited: ﴿wa-huwa yut'imu wa-la yut'imu﴾, both with a damma on the ya' and a kasra on the 'ayn.

Al-Hasan ibn al-Fadl said: Its meaning is that He is able to feed and to refrain from feeding, like His saying ﴿He extends provision to whom He wills and restricts it﴾ (13:26).

I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi say: I heard Abu Mansur al-Azhari say in Harat: its meaning is ﴿and He feeds but is not sought to feed (wa-la yustat'im)﴾. The Arabs say: "I fed others," meaning "I asked them to feed me."

He recited:

"We feed whoever is in summer a feast,
and in winter when the gourds are not sought (for food)..."

That is, "we ask for food." It was also said: its meaning is ﴿He feeds﴾, meaning Allah, ﴿and is not fed﴾, meaning the protector.

Say: ﴿I have been commanded to be the first to submit﴾, meaning to sincerely devote myself. ﴿And do not be among the polytheists.﴾ Say: ﴿I fear, if I disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous day﴾, meaning if I worship other than Him. It is the Day of Resurrection.

﴿Whoever is averted from it that day﴾, meaning whoever has the punishment averted from him.

The people of Kufa recited: ﴿yasrif﴾ with a fatha on the ya' and a kasra on the ra', in the sense of "whom Allah averts it from," and Abu 'Ubayd and Abu Hatim preferred this, because of His saying before it: ﴿Say: To whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth? Say: To Allah﴾ (6:12), and because of His saying after it ﴿He has had mercy on him﴾, and He did not say "then he has been shown mercy" in the passive form.

﴿Say, "What thing is greatest in testimony?"﴾ (the verse)

Al-Kalbi said: The people of Makkah came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "Allah has found no messenger other than you, and we do not see anyone who confirms what you say. If we asked the Jews and the Christians about you, they claim you have no mention among them. So show us who testifies that you are the Messenger of Allah, as you claim." So Allah revealed: ﴿Say, "What thing is greatest in testimony?"﴾. If they answer you, well and good; otherwise say: ﴿Allah is sufficient as a witness between me and you﴾ regarding what I say. ﴿And this Qur'an has been revealed to me that I may warn you therewith, O people of Makkah﴾, ﴿and whoever it reaches﴾, meaning whoever the Qur'an reaches among the non-Arabs and others.

Al-Farra' said: The Arabs omit the pronoun (hā', the "ha" of the object) after the relative forms *man* (who) and *mā* (what) in such constructions, as in *inna alladhī akhadhta mālaka* (indeed, the one who took your wealth), *wa-mālī akhadhtuhu* (and my wealth, I took it), and *man akramta* [abirru bihi] (whom you honored [I am kind to him]), meaning *akramtahu* (you honored him).

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "O people, convey from me, even if it is one verse from the Book of Allah. For whoever has been reached by a verse from the Book of Allah, the command of Allah has reached him; he may take it or leave it." [Jami' al-Bayan: 7/215.] [130]

Al-Hasan ibn Salih said: I asked Layth: "Is there anyone left to whom the call has not reached?"
He said: Mujahid used to say: "Wherever the Qur'an comes, there is a caller and a warner," and then he recited this verse.

Muqatil said: Whoever the Qur'an has reached, among jinn and humans, it is a warning to him.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: Whoever the Qur'an has reached, it is as if he saw Muhammad (peace be upon him) and heard from him.

﴿Do you indeed testify that with Allah there are other gods?﴾ He said "ukhra" (other) in the feminine rather than "akhar" (other, masculine), and "ālihah" (gods) is a plural, because the plural takes the feminine, as in His saying: ﴿What, then, is the state of the earlier generations?﴾ [Surah Ta-Ha: 51.]

﴿Say, O Muhammad: "If you testify, I will not testify. Say: He is only one God, and I am free of what you associate."﴾

﴿Those to whom We gave the Book﴾ means the Torah and the Gospel. ﴿Recognize him﴾ means Muhammad (ﷺ), his description and attributes, ﴿as they recognize their sons﴾, that is, the children.

Al-Kalbi said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) arrived in Madinah, 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) said to 'Abdullah ibn Salam: "Allah has revealed to His Prophet, ﴿Those to whom We gave the Book recognize him as they recognize their sons﴾. So what is this recognition?" 'Abdullah said: "O 'Umar, I recognized him among you when I saw him by his description and attributes, as I recognize my son when I see him playing with children. And I have a greater knowledge of Muhammad (ﷺ) than of my son." He said: "How so?" He said: "Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, described him in our Book, but I do not know what the women have done." 'Umar said: "May Allah grant you success, O Ibn Salam." [Zad al-Masir, with variation: 3/13; al-Durr al-Manthur: 1/147.]

﴿Those who have lost themselves﴾, meaning they were cheated of themselves, ﴿so they do not believe.﴾ This is because every servant has a place in Paradise and a place in Hell. When the Day of Resurrection comes, Allah makes the places of the people of Hell in Paradise to belong to the people of Paradise, and the places of the people of Paradise in Hell to belong to the people of Hell.

﴿And who is more unjust﴾, meaning more disbelieving,

al-Hasan said: "There is no one more unjust than the one who ﴿fabricates a lie against Allah﴾, by associating others with Him, ﴿or denies His signs﴾, meaning the Qur'an."

al-Hasan said: Everything in the Qur'an that says ﴿Our signs﴾ or ﴿His signs﴾ means by it the religion with what it contains.

﴿Surely the wrongdoers will not succeed,﴾ meaning the disbelievers.

﴿On the day We gather them all﴾, the worshippers and those worshipped, ﴿then We will say to those who associated others with Allah: "Where are your partners whom you claimed?"﴾ meaning: "They would intercede for you with your Lord." ﴿Then their trial will be nothing but﴾ meaning their answer and their reply. It was said: their excuse. And "fitnah" (trial) means testing. Since their questioning reveals what is in their hearts, it was called fitnah.

﴿Except that they will say: "By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists."﴾ This is because on the Day of Resurrection, when they see Allah's forgiveness and His pardoning of the people of Tawhid (monotheism), some of them say to others: "Come, let us conceal the shirk; perhaps we will be saved along with the people of Tawhid." So they say: ﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists.﴾ Then Allah, the Exalted, says to them: ﴿Where are your partners whom you claimed and called upon as My partners?﴾ Then ﴿We seal their mouths﴾, and their limbs testify against them with disbelief. This is His saying: ﴿See how they lied against themselves, and that which they used to fabricate has left them.﴾ "Dalla" means departed and perished, "anhum" (from them), ﴿what they used to fabricate﴾ concerning the idols.

﴿And among them are those who listen to you﴾, the verse...

He said: Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah, al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, 'Utbah and Shaybah the sons of Rabi'ah, Umayyah and Ubayy the sons of Khalaf, and al-Harith ibn 'Amir gathered and listened to the speech of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). They said to al-Nadr: "O Abu Futayla, what does Muhammad say?" He said, by the One who made it His house, meaning the Ka'bah: "I do not know what he says, except that he moves his tongue and says: ﴿They are only the myths of the ancients,﴾ just as I used to tell you about the past generations." al-Nadr had written down stories about the generations and their reports.

Abu Sufyan said: "I see that some of what he says is hidden." Abu Jahl said: "No!" Then Allah the Exalted revealed:

﴿And among them are those who listen to you﴾ and to your speech.

﴿And We have placed over their hearts coverings lest they understand it, and in their ears deafness﴾, meaning heaviness and deafness. ﴿And if they see every sign, they will not believe in it, until, when they come to you, they dispute with you. Those who disbelieve say: "This is nothing but the myths of the ancients."﴾ meaning their tales. "Usṭūrah" and "isṭārah" (both forms of "myth").

Some people of language said: They are trivialities, falsehoods, and nonsense, and their root is from "saṭṭartu," meaning "I wrote."

﴿And they forbid it and keep away from it.﴾

Muqatil said: It was revealed concerning Abu Talib, whose name was 'Abd Manaf. The Prophet (ﷺ) was with Abu Talib calling to Islam, and the Quraysh gathered before Abu Talib intending harm to the Prophet (ﷺ). Abu Talib said:

By Allah, they will not reach you with their gathering
until I am laid in the dust, buried.
So proclaim your command; no shame is upon you,
and rejoice in it, and let it cool your eyes.
You called me, and you claimed that you advise me,
and you have spoken the truth, and you were indeed my guide.
And you made known a religion that is undoubtedly
among the best religions of mankind.
Were it not for blame, or my fear of reproach,
you would have found me generous in declaring it openly.
[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 6/406.]

So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿And they forbid it and keep away from it﴾, meaning they prevent people from harming the Prophet (ﷺ), ﴿and keep away from it﴾, meaning they distance themselves from the guidance he brought, so they do not believe him.

This is the view of al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, 'Ata' ibn Dinar, one of two narrations from Ibn 'Abbas, and from Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah, al-Suddi and al-Dahhak. They said: It was revealed concerning a group of the disbelievers of Makkah, meaning that ﴿they forbid people﴾ from following Muhammad and believing in him, and they distance themselves from him.

Mujahid said: ﴿They forbid it﴾, meaning the Quraysh forbid the remembrance (of Allah) and distance themselves from it.

Qatadah said: They forbid the Qur'an and the Prophet (ﷺ) and distance themselves from him.

﴿And they destroy none but themselves, though they perceive it not.﴾ This is because the burdens of those whom they turn away fall upon them. ﴿Were you to see, O Muhammad, when they are made to stand﴾, meaning they are held back, ﴿over the Fire﴾, meaning in the Fire, as in His saying: ﴿And they followed what the devils recited over the kingdom of Solomon﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 102], meaning in the kingdom of Solomon.

The response of "law" (if) is omitted; its meaning is: if you saw them in that state, you would see a marvel.

﴿They will say: "Would that we were returned, and we would not deny the signs of our Lord, and we would be among the believers."﴾ The common readers recite ﴿wa-nakūna﴾ in the nominative, meaning: "Would that we were returned," and "we would not deny the signs of our Lord," and "we would be among the believers," whether we were returned or not.

Ibn Abi Ishaq and Hamzah recited ﴿wa-lā nukadhdhiba﴾ and ﴿wa-nakūna﴾ in the accusative, as an answer to a wish (tamannī). The Arabs put the answer to a wish in the accusative with the waw just as they do with the fa'.

Ibn 'Amir recited ﴿nuradd wa-lā nukadhdhiba﴾ in the nominative, and ﴿wa-nakūna﴾ in the accusative. He said: because they wished for the return and to be among the believers, and they informed that they would not deny the signs of their Lord if they were returned to the world.

This view is more pleasing to me than the first, because they did not conceal their disbelief in the world, unless the verse is applied to the hypocrites.

al-Mubarrad said: ﴿There has become apparent to them﴾ (is the requital for what they used to conceal before).

﴿But there has become apparent to them what they used to conceal﴾, meaning what they used to hide in the world of their disbelief and their disobedience.

al-Suddi said: They said: "By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists." That is their concealment "before." So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, made their limbs speak, and they testified against them with what they had hidden. This is His saying: ﴿But there has become apparent to them﴾. This view is more pleasing to me than the first, because they did not conceal their disbelief in the world, unless the verse is applied to the hypocrites.

al-Mubarrad said: ﴿There has become apparent to them﴾ (is the requital for what they used to conceal before).

al-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: Its meaning: "Rather, there has become apparent to them [their curse]." Then he said: ﴿And if they were returned to the world, they would return to what they were forbidden of disbelief. And indeed they are liars﴾ in their saying: "If you returned us to the world, we would not deny the signs of our Lord, and we would be among the believers."

﴿Say, "What thing is greatest in testimony?"﴾ (the verse)

Al-Kalbi said: The people of Makkah came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "Allah has found no messenger other than you, and we do not see anyone who confirms what you say. If we asked the Jews and the Christians about you, they claim you have no mention among them. So show us who testifies that you are the Messenger of Allah, as you claim." So Allah revealed: ﴿Say, "What thing is greatest in testimony?"﴾. If they answer you, well and good; otherwise say: ﴿Allah is sufficient as a witness between me and you﴾ regarding what I say. ﴿And this Qur'an has been revealed to me that I may warn you therewith, O people of Makkah﴾, ﴿and whoever it reaches﴾, meaning whoever the Qur'an reaches among the non-Arabs and others.

Al-Farra' said: The Arabs omit the pronoun (hā', the "ha" of the object) after the relative forms *man* (who) and *mā* (what) in such constructions, as in *inna alladhī akhadhta mālaka* (indeed, the one who took your wealth), *wa-mālī akhadhtuhu* (and my wealth, I took it), and *man akramta* [abirru bihi] (whom you honored [I am kind to him]), meaning *akramtahu* (you honored him).

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "O people, convey from me, even if it is one verse from the Book of Allah. For whoever has been reached by a verse from the Book of Allah, the command of Allah has reached him; he may take it or leave it." [Jami' al-Bayan: 7/215.] [130]

Al-Hasan ibn Salih said: I asked Layth: "Is there anyone left to whom the call has not reached?"
He said: Mujahid used to say: "Wherever the Qur'an comes, there is a caller and a warner," and then he recited this verse.

Muqatil said: Whoever the Qur'an has reached, among jinn and humans, it is a warning to him.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: Whoever the Qur'an has reached, it is as if he saw Muhammad (peace be upon him) and heard from him.

﴿Do you indeed testify that with Allah there are other gods?﴾ He said "ukhra" (other) in the feminine rather than "akhar" (other, masculine), and "ālihah" (gods) is a plural, because the plural takes the feminine, as in His saying: ﴿What, then, is the state of the earlier generations?﴾ [Surah Ta-Ha: 51.]

﴿Say, O Muhammad: "If you testify, I will not testify. Say: He is only one God, and I am free of what you associate."﴾

﴿Those to whom We gave the Book﴾ means the Torah and the Gospel. ﴿Recognize him﴾ means Muhammad (ﷺ), his description and attributes, ﴿as they recognize their sons﴾, that is, the children.

Al-Kalbi said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) arrived in Madinah, 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) said to 'Abdullah ibn Salam: "Allah has revealed to His Prophet, ﴿Those to whom We gave the Book recognize him as they recognize their sons﴾. So what is this recognition?" 'Abdullah said: "O 'Umar, I recognized him among you when I saw him by his description and attributes, as I recognize my son when I see him playing with children. And I have a greater knowledge of Muhammad (ﷺ) than of my son." He said: "How so?" He said: "Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, described him in our Book, but I do not know what the women have done." 'Umar said: "May Allah grant you success, O Ibn Salam." [Zad al-Masir, with variation: 3/13; al-Durr al-Manthur: 1/147.]

﴿Those who have lost themselves﴾, meaning they were cheated of themselves, ﴿so they do not believe.﴾ This is because every servant has a place in Paradise and a place in Hell. When the Day of Resurrection comes, Allah makes the places of the people of Hell in Paradise to belong to the people of Paradise, and the places of the people of Paradise in Hell to belong to the people of Hell.

﴿And who is more unjust﴾, meaning more disbelieving,

al-Hasan said: "There is no one more unjust than the one who ﴿fabricates a lie against Allah﴾, by associating others with Him, ﴿or denies His signs﴾, meaning the Qur'an."

al-Hasan said: Everything in the Qur'an that says ﴿Our signs﴾ or ﴿His signs﴾ means by it the religion with what it contains.

﴿Surely the wrongdoers will not succeed,﴾ meaning the disbelievers.

﴿On the day We gather them all﴾, the worshippers and those worshipped, ﴿then We will say to those who associated others with Allah: "Where are your partners whom you claimed?"﴾ meaning: "They would intercede for you with your Lord." ﴿Then their trial will be nothing but﴾ meaning their answer and their reply. It was said: their excuse. And "fitnah" (trial) means testing. Since their questioning reveals what is in their hearts, it was called fitnah.

﴿Except that they will say: "By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists."﴾ This is because on the Day of Resurrection, when they see Allah's forgiveness and His pardoning of the people of Tawhid (monotheism), some of them say to others: "Come, let us conceal the shirk; perhaps we will be saved along with the people of Tawhid." So they say: ﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists.﴾ Then Allah, the Exalted, says to them: ﴿Where are your partners whom you claimed and called upon as My partners?﴾ Then ﴿We seal their mouths﴾, and their limbs testify against them with disbelief. This is His saying: ﴿See how they lied against themselves, and that which they used to fabricate has left them.﴾ "Dalla" means departed and perished, "anhum" (from them), ﴿what they used to fabricate﴾ concerning the idols.

﴿And among them are those who listen to you﴾, the verse...

He said: Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah, al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, 'Utbah and Shaybah the sons of Rabi'ah, Umayyah and Ubayy the sons of Khalaf, and al-Harith ibn 'Amir gathered and listened to the speech of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). They said to al-Nadr: "O Abu Futayla, what does Muhammad say?" He said, by the One who made it His house, meaning the Ka'bah: "I do not know what he says, except that he moves his tongue and says: ﴿They are only the myths of the ancients,﴾ just as I used to tell you about the past generations." al-Nadr had written down stories about the generations and their reports.

Abu Sufyan said: "I see that some of what he says is hidden." Abu Jahl said: "No!" Then Allah the Exalted revealed:

﴿And among them are those who listen to you﴾ and to your speech.

﴿And We have placed over their hearts coverings lest they understand it, and in their ears deafness﴾, meaning heaviness and deafness. ﴿And if they see every sign, they will not believe in it, until, when they come to you, they dispute with you. Those who disbelieve say: "This is nothing but the myths of the ancients."﴾ meaning their tales. "Usṭūrah" and "isṭārah" (both forms of "myth").

Some people of language said: They are trivialities, falsehoods, and nonsense, and their root is from "saṭṭartu," meaning "I wrote."

﴿And they forbid it and keep away from it.﴾

Muqatil said: It was revealed concerning Abu Talib, whose name was 'Abd Manaf. The Prophet (ﷺ) was with Abu Talib calling to Islam, and the Quraysh gathered before Abu Talib intending harm to the Prophet (ﷺ). Abu Talib said:

By Allah, they will not reach you with their gathering
until I am laid in the dust, buried.
So proclaim your command; no shame is upon you,
and rejoice in it, and let it cool your eyes.
You called me, and you claimed that you advise me,
and you have spoken the truth, and you were indeed my guide.
And you made known a religion that is undoubtedly
among the best religions of mankind.
Were it not for blame, or my fear of reproach,
you would have found me generous in declaring it openly.
[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 6/406.]

So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿And they forbid it and keep away from it﴾, meaning they prevent people from harming the Prophet (ﷺ), ﴿and keep away from it﴾, meaning they distance themselves from the guidance he brought, so they do not believe him.

This is the view of al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, 'Ata' ibn Dinar, one of two narrations from Ibn 'Abbas, and from Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah, al-Suddi and al-Dahhak. They said: It was revealed concerning a group of the disbelievers of Makkah, meaning that ﴿they forbid people﴾ from following Muhammad and believing in him, and they distance themselves from him.

Mujahid said: ﴿They forbid it﴾, meaning the Quraysh forbid the remembrance (of Allah) and distance themselves from it.

Qatadah said: They forbid the Qur'an and the Prophet (ﷺ) and distance themselves from him.

﴿And they destroy none but themselves, though they perceive it not.﴾ This is because the burdens of those whom they turn away fall upon them. ﴿Were you to see, O Muhammad, when they are made to stand﴾, meaning they are held back, ﴿over the Fire﴾, meaning in the Fire, as in His saying: ﴿And they followed what the devils recited over the kingdom of Solomon﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 102], meaning in the kingdom of Solomon.

al-Sumayqa' recited ﴿idh waqafū﴾ with a fatha on the waw and the qaf, from the verb "waqafa" (to stand). The first reading is "wuqifū" (they were made to stand). He said: "waqaftu bi-nafsī wuqūfan" (I stood by myself), and "waqaftum waqfan" (you stood as a standing).

The response of "law" (if) is omitted; its meaning is: if you saw them in that state, you would see a marvel.

﴿They will say: "Would that we were returned, and we would not deny the signs of our Lord, and we would be among the believers."﴾ The common readers recite ﴿wa-nakūna﴾ in the nominative, meaning: "Would that we were returned," and "we would not deny the signs of our Lord," and "we would be among the believers," whether we were returned or not.

Ibn Abi Ishaq and Hamzah recited ﴿wa-lā nukadhdhiba﴾ and ﴿wa-nakūna﴾ in the accusative, as an answer to a wish (tamannī). The Arabs put the answer to a wish in the accusative with the waw just as they do with the fa'.

Ibn 'Amir recited ﴿nuradd wa-lā nukadhdhiba﴾ in the nominative, and ﴿wa-nakūna﴾ in the accusative. He said: because they wished for the return and to be among the believers, and they informed that they would not deny the signs of their Lord if they were returned to the world.

﴿But there has become apparent to them what they used to conceal﴾, meaning what they used to hide in the world of their disbelief and their disobedience.

al-Suddi said: They said: "By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists." That is their concealment "before." So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, made their limbs speak, and they testified against them with what they had hidden. This is His saying: ﴿But there has become apparent to them﴾. This view is more pleasing to me than the first, because they did not conceal their disbelief in the world, unless the verse is applied to the hypocrites.

al-Mubarrad said: ﴿There has become apparent to them﴾ (is the requital for what they used to conceal before).

al-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: Its meaning: "Rather, there has become apparent to them [their curse]." Then he said: ﴿And if they were returned to the world, they would return to what they were forbidden of disbelief. And indeed they are liars﴾ in their saying: "If you returned us to the world, we would not deny the signs of our Lord, and we would be among the believers."

And they say, "There is nothing but our life of this world." [Here there is inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir) in the wording.] 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam used to say: this is from their saying: "If they were returned, they would say: 'We are not to be resurrected after death.'"

﴿And if you could see when they are made to stand before their Lord.﴾ It was said: before the judgment of Allah [ ... ] [[Unreadable speech.]] they [and our hands speak] by the command of Allah. He will say, ﴿Is this not the truth?﴾ They will say, ﴿Yes, by our Lord, it is true.﴾ He will say, ﴿Then taste the punishment for what you used to disbelieve.﴾

That is, because of your disbelief.

﴿Those who denied the meeting with Allah have certainly lost,﴾ that is, they were ruined and perished, those who denied the meeting with Allah, that is, the resurrection after death, ﴿until, when the Hour comes upon them suddenly,﴾ the Resurrection, suddenly, unexpectedly, ﴿they will say, "Oh, our regret over what we neglected in it,"﴾ that is, our remorse over what we fell short of in it, in the great calamity. It was also said: over what we left behind in the world of the deeds of the Hereafter.

Muhammad ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) said: the pronoun refers to the transaction (al-safqah). That is because when the loss of their transaction became clear to them, the exchange of faith for disbelief and the world for the Hereafter, they said: ﴿Oh, our regret over what we neglected in it,﴾ meaning in the transaction; so the mention of the transaction was omitted, as in His saying, ﴿Those who denied the meeting with Allah have certainly lost,﴾ because loss occurs only in a sale transaction. [[Jami' al-Bayan: 7/236.]]

Al-Suddi said: it means over what we wasted of the deeds of Paradise. This is supported by what al-A'mash narrated from Abu Salih, from Abu Sa'id, from the Prophet (ﷺ) concerning this verse, that he said: "The people of the Fire will see their places in Paradise, and they will say: 'Oh, our regret!'"

[131] ﴿While they carry their burdens on their backs﴾, that is, their sins and their deeds.

Abu 'Ubayd said: it is said of a man who spreads out his garment and puts goods in it: "Carry your load (wizr) and your loads." Its derivation is from the wizr (support/refuge) that one relies upon, and for this reason it is called wizr, because it is as if it were that which the king or the prophet relies upon. From it is His saying, ﴿And appoint for me a minister from my family, Aaron, my brother﴾ [Surah Ta-Ha 20:29–30]. ﴿On their backs.﴾

Al-Suddi and 'Amr ibn Qays al-Mala'i said: when the believer comes out of his grave, he is met by the most beautiful form and the sweetest scent. He says, "Do you know me?" He says, "No, except that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has made your scent sweet and your form beautiful." He says, "Thus you were written in the world: I am your righteous deed. You used to ride me in the world, so ride me today." And he recited, ﴿The day We gather the righteous to the Most Merciful as a delegation﴾ [Maryam 19:85], that is, riding. But the disbeliever is met by the ugliest form and the most foul scent, and he says, "Do you know me?" He says, "No, except that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has made your form ugly and your scent foul." He says, "Because of your deeds in the world: I am your evil deed. You used to ride me in the evening, so today I ride you." This is His saying, ﴿While they carry their burdens on their backs. Unquestionably, evil is what they carry.﴾

Al-Zajjaj said: ﴿Unquestionably, evil is what they carry﴾ means: what they bear and what they do. ﴿And the life of this world is nothing but amusement and diversion,﴾ that is, falsehood and deception that does not endure. This is Allah's denial of the disbelievers in their saying, ﴿There is nothing but our life of this world,﴾ the verse. ﴿And the home of the Hereafter is better﴾ — the common reciters read it in the nominative as a description of the "wa" (i.e., as an attribute), and the people of the Levant read it with an idafah (genitive construction), because the two wordings differ, as in His saying: "Rabi' al-Awwal" and "Masjid al-Jami'," ﴿and the grain of the harvest﴾ [Qaf 50:9]. The world (al-dunya) was named for its nearness (dunuww), and it was said: for its lowliness (dana'ah). The Hereafter was named for being after the world. ﴿Better for those who fear Allah﴾ from shirk. ﴿Will you not reason?﴾ That is, the Hereafter is better than the world.

﴿We know that what they say grieves you,﴾ the verse.

Al-Suddi said: Al-Akhnas ibn Shariq met Abu Jahl ibn Hisham, and al-Akhnas said to Abu Jahl: "O Abu al-Hakam, tell me about Muhammad: is he truthful or a liar? For there is no one here who hears our conversation except me." Abu Jahl said to him: "By Allah, Muhammad is truthful, and Muhammad has never lied. But if the sons of Qusayy take the banner, the watering, the custodianship of the Ka'bah, the council house, and the prophethood, what will remain for the rest of Quraysh?" So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed this verse.

Abu Yazid al-Madani said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) met Abu Jahl and shook his hand. One of his devils met him and said to him: "You shake his hand?" He said: "By Allah, I know that he is truthful, but when have we ever followed the descendants of 'Abd Manaf?" So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed this verse.

Najiyah ibn Ka'b said: Abu Jahl said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "We do not accuse you, nor do we call you a liar, but we accuse what you have brought and we call it a lie." So Allah, Exalted, revealed this verse.

Muqatil said: It was revealed concerning al-Harith ibn 'Amir ibn Nawfal ibn 'Abd Manaf ibn Qusayy, who used to call the Prophet (ﷺ) a liar openly, but when he was alone with his household he would say: "Muhammad is not one of the people of lies; I do not think he is anything but truthful." And he said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "We know that what you have is true, and what prevents us from following the guidance with you is only our fear that the might of the Arabs will snatch us from our land. For we are a morsel for them, and we have no power against them." [132] So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed this verse:

﴿We know that what they say grieves you﴾, [that they say] you are a liar, a sorcerer, and a madman. ﴿But they do not call you a liar﴾, that is, they do not attribute lying to you, nor do they say to you, "You have lied."

Nafi' and al-Kisa'i read ﴿yukdhibunaka﴾ with the lightened form, and this is the reading of Ali (may Allah be pleased with him). It means: "they do not find you a liar." The Arabs say: "The land became barren (ajdabat) and fertile (akhsabat), and I made it fertile (ahyaytuha) and made it productive (ahyaytuha)," when they find it barren or fertile. Their saying also: the land is productive, bringing forth plants.

Ru'bah said:
"And I stirred the fertile lands of Dhat al-Barq"
That is, I found it bringing forth plants.

Al-Kisa'i said: The Arabs say, "akdhabtu al-rusul" when one informs that they told a lie, and "kadhdhabtuhu" when one judges that he is a liar.

﴿But the wrongdoers deny the signs of Allah.﴾

﴿And messengers were denied before you,﴾ [consolation to His Prophet]. They say: their people denied them, just as Quraysh denied you. ﴿So they were patient over what they were denied and harmed, until Our help came to them. And none can alter the words of Allah.﴾ Al-Kalbi said: that means the Qur'an.

'Ikrimah said: it means His saying, ﴿And We had already preceded Our word﴾, and ﴿none can alter the words of Allah﴾, up to His saying, ﴿victorious﴾ [al-Saffat 37:171–173]. And His saying: ﴿Indeed, We will surely support Our messengers and those who believe in the life of this world﴾ [Ghafir 40:51], and His saying, ﴿Allah has decreed, "I will surely prevail, I and My messengers"﴾ [al-Mujadila 58:21]. "Al-'adl" means: "I will certainly fulfill them for His punishment." ﴿And there has certainly come to you from the news of the messengers﴾, from before, as one says: "We were struck by rain," meaning: any rain.

﴿And if their aversion has been difficult for you﴾

Al-Kalbi said: al-Harith ibn 'Amir said: "O Muhammad, bring us a sign as the prophets used to bring. If you bring it, we will believe in you and confirm you." But Allah refused to bring it to them, so they turned away from him, and it was hard upon him (ﷺ).

So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And if their aversion has been difficult for you﴾, that is, it was great and burdensome, ﴿upon you﴾, their turning away from you. ﴿Then if you are able to seek a tunnel (nafaq) in the earth,﴾ that is, a passage, like the burrow of the jerboa (al-yarbu'), which is one of its holes, where it goes in; ﴿or a ladder (sullam) to the sky,﴾ a stairway and a means of ascent to Me in the sky, by which one climbs.

Al-Zajjaj said: "al-sullam" is from "al-salamah" (safety), and it is that which brings you safely to your place of ascent. ﴿And bring them a sign﴾, then do it. ﴿And if Allah had willed, He would have gathered them upon guidance﴾, so they would all believe. ﴿So never be among the ignorant﴾ — that some of them believe in you and not others. And indeed, if Allah had willed, He would have gathered them upon guidance; and whoever disbelieves, he disbelieves only through the whole of his knowledge in it.

And they say, "There is nothing but our life of this world." [Here there is inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir) in the wording.] 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam used to say: this is from their saying: "If they were returned, they would say: 'We are not to be resurrected after death.'"

﴿Why then, when Our punishment came upon them, did they not humble themselves?﴾ So that they believed and it was removed from them. ﴿But their hearts became hardened, and Satan made attractive to them what they were doing﴾ of disbelief and disobedience. ﴿So when they forgot what they had been reminded of,﴾ that is, they rejected what they had been admonished and commanded to do, ﴿We opened to them the gates of every thing﴾ that is, We replaced the trial and hardship with ease in living and health in their bodies. ﴿Until, when they rejoiced in what they had been given,﴾ were pleased with it, ﴿We seized them suddenly,﴾ unexpectedly, ﴿and at once they were in despair,﴾ hopeless of every good. Al-Suddi said: "destroyed." Ibn Kaysan said: "humbled." Al-Hasan said: "silent."

'Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami recited ﴿مُبْلَسُونَ﴾ (mublasun) with a fatha on the lam (mublasa), as an object, meaning "made despairing." The root of al-iblas is lowering the head out of sorrow and regret.

Mujahid said: al-iblas is disgrace. Ibn Zayd said: al-mublis is one upon whom an evil has descended that cannot be repelled.

Ja'far al-Sadiq said: ﴿When they forgot what they had been reminded of﴾ of the glorification [of God], ﴿We opened to them the gates of every thing﴾ of blessings, ﴿until, when they rejoiced in what they had been given﴾ of luxury and pleasure, ﴿they were suddenly seized, and to the evil of Hellfire [they were brought].

﴿So the last remnant of the people was cut off.﴾ Al-Suddi said: "the root of the people." Qutrub said: "Their seizure," meaning they were uprooted and destroyed. ﴿Those who did wrong.﴾ ﴿And praise be to God, Lord of the worlds,﴾ for their destruction.

'Uqba ibn 'Amir related from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "If you see that God gives His servants what they wish despite their disobedience, then that is indeed a gradual enticement from Him toward them." [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 6/426.]] [134] Then he recited this verse: ﴿So when they forgot what they had been reminded of﴾ to the end of the verse.

﴿Say, "Have you considered: if Allah were to take away your hearing and your sight and seal over your hearts, what deity other than Allah could bring them back to you?"﴾ That is, they would not comprehend speech or see the proof. ﴿Who could bring it to you?﴾ That is, bring back what He took from you. ﴿Observe how We vary the signs﴾ (nubayyin lahum al-ayat), that is, We make the signs clear to them, ﴿yet they turn away﴾ (yasdifun), that is, they turn aside from them, denying them.

﴿Say: "Have you considered: if the punishment of Allah comes upon you suddenly (baghtatan), or openly (jahratan), with visible sight and witness, [for what you associated with Him], will anyone be destroyed except the wrongdoing people?"﴾ The wrongdoers are the polytheists.

﴿We send the messengers only as bearers of good news and warners. So whoever believes and does righteous deeds, there will be no fear for them﴾ when those in the Fire fear, ﴿nor will they grieve﴾ when they grieve. ﴿But those who deny Our signs﴾, meaning Muhammad and the Qur'an, ﴿the punishment will touch them﴾, that is, afflict them, ﴿for what they used to defiantly do﴾, that is, commit.

﴿Say: "I do not tell you that I have the treasures of Allah﴾, meaning the provision of Allah, ﴿nor do I know the unseen﴾, that is, what is hidden from people, ﴿nor do I tell you that I am an angel﴾, so that you would reject my words and deny my command. ﴿I only follow what is revealed to me.﴾" That is not disallowed nor impossible by reason, given the existence of the evidences and the conclusive proof.

﴿Say: "Are the blind and the seeing alike? Will you not reflect?"﴾ The disbelievers and the believers, the misguided and the guided, are not alike.

﴿And warn with it﴾, that is, with the Qur'an, ﴿those who fear that they will be gathered﴾, that is, raised and brought to life, ﴿to their Lord.﴾ Ad-Dahhak said: "with it" refers to Allah. Another view: ﴿those who know that they will be gathered, because their fear is due to what their deeds have been.﴾ ﴿They will have no protector besides Him﴾, meaning no close one who benefits them, ﴿nor any intercessor﴾ to intercede for them, ﴿so that they may fear Him.﴾

﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening…﴾ Sulayman and Khabbab ibn al-Aratt said: this verse was revealed concerning us.

Al-Aqra' ibn Habis al-Tamimi and Uyayna ibn Hisn al-Fazari, who were among those whose hearts were to be softened (al-mu'allafa qulubuhum), came and found the Prophet (ﷺ) sitting with Bilal, Suhayb, Ammar and Khabbab, along with some weak Muslims. When they saw them around him, they belittled them and came to him and said: "O Messenger of Allah, if you sat at the head of the gathering and these people were away, and removed their woolen tunics, which were the only garments they had, we would sit with you, converse with you and take from you." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I am not one to drive away the believers." They said: "Then we wish you would make for us a gathering of your own, by which the Arabs would recognize our superiority, for the delegations of the Arabs come to you, and we are ashamed that the Arabs should see us with these slaves. When we come to you, let them be removed, and when we finish, sit with them if you wish." He said: "Yes." They said: "Write us a document to that effect." So he called for a sheet and called Ali to write.

He said: "While we were sitting in a corner, Jibril (peace be upon him) came down with the words: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening…﴾ [6:52], unless by something [else]." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) threw the sheet from his hand, then called us. We came to him while he was saying: ﴿Peace be upon you. Your Lord has prescribed for Himself mercy﴾ [6:54]. We would sit with him, and when he wished to rise, he rose and left us. Then Allah revealed this verse: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord…﴾. He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would sit with us patiently and we would draw close to him until our knees almost touched his knees. When the hour came for him to rise, we rose and left him until he stood up. He said: "Praise be to Allah who did not take me until He commanded me to keep myself patient with a people from my community: [your life is with you and your death is with you]." [135]

Al-Kalbi said: They said to him: "Make a day for us and a day for them." He said: "I will not do that." They said: "Then make the gathering one and come to us, and turn your back to them." So Allah revealed this verse.

Al-Ash'ath ibn Sawwar narrated from Idris, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: The chiefs of Quraysh passed by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), along with Suhayb, Khabbab, Bilal, Ammar and others of the weak Muslims. They said: "O Muhammad, are you pleased with these from your people? Shall we be followers of these? Are these the ones on whom Allah has bestowed favor from among us? Drive them away from you; perhaps if you drive them away, we will follow you." So Allah revealed: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord…﴾. He said: Quraysh had said: "Were it not for Bilal and Ibn Umm Abd, we would follow Muhammad." So Allah revealed this verse.

Ikrimah said: Utba ibn Rabi'a, Shayba ibn Umayya, Mut'im ibn Adi, al-Harith ibn Nawfal, Qurza ibn Abd and Amr ibn Nawfal, among the nobles of Banu Abd Manaf from the people of disbelief, came to Abu Talib and said: "O Abu Talib, if your nephew Muhammad would drive away our clients and allies, for they are our slaves, it would be greater in our hearts, more obedient to him among us, and closer to our following him and affirming him." Abu Talib came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and told him what they had concealed. Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "If you did that, we would see what they want and where they will end up." Then this verse was revealed concerning their statement. When it was revealed, Umar ibn al-Khattab came and apologized for his statement.

Jubayr ibn Nufayl said: The Quraysh came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "You sent for us, so drive these scum away from you, and we will be your companions." So Allah revealed: ﴿And do not drive away…﴾.

Ibn Abbas said: ﴿those who call upon their Lord﴾ means those who worship their Lord with the obligatory prayer, ﴿morning and evening﴾ means the dawn prayer and the afternoon prayer. This was because some poor people were with the Prophet (ﷺ), and some of the nobles said: "When we pray, let these be delayed, and let them pray behind us." So Allah revealed: ﴿And do not drive away those who…﴾.

Hamza ibn Isa said: I entered upon al-Hasan and said: "O Abu Sa'id, what do you say about the words of Allah: ﴿And do not drive away those who believe﴾?" He said: "No, rather they are those who guard the prayers in congregation."

Mujahid said: I prayed the dawn prayer with Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab (may Allah be pleased with him). When the imam finished the salam, the people hurried to the storyteller (al-qass). Sa'id said: "How quickly the people rush to this gathering!"

Mujahid said: I said: "They interpret the words of Allah: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening﴾." He meant that this refers only to the prayer we have just left, and we said they remember their Lord.

Abu Ja'far said: meaning they recite the Qur'an.

﴿seeking His face﴾ is the answer to His words ﴿You are not accountable for them in anything﴾ [6:52]. His words ﴿so you would be among the wrongdoers﴾ are the answer to His words ﴿and do not drive away﴾; ﴿no one﴾ is the answer to a negation, and ﴿Allah﴾ is the answer to the prohibition. ﴿Among the wrongdoers﴾, meaning those who harm themselves through disobedience. Driving away is misplaced when it is not in its proper place.

﴿And thus We tested some of them by others﴾ [6:53]: the lowly and the customary ranking with respect to the master and the wealthy. ﴿So that they say: "Are these the ones on whom Allah has bestowed favor from among us?"﴾ That is, the nobles, the rich, say: "these," meaning the poor and weak, "on whom Allah has bestowed favor from among us." Al-Kalbi said: When a noble saw a lowly person had embraced Islam before him, he would be too proud to accept Islam and say: "This one has preceded me in Islam," so he would not accept it. ﴿Is not Allah most knowing of the grateful?﴾, meaning the believers. This is the answer to their words "are these the ones on whom Allah has bestowed favor from among us?" It was also said: "Is not Allah most knowing of the grateful, those who give thanks for Islam when He guides them to it?"

Al-Ala' ibn Bashir, from Abu Bakr al-Naji, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, said: I was in a group among which were poor emigrants, some of whom covered others from nakedness. A reciter was reciting to us while we listened to his recitation. The Prophet (ﷺ) came upon us until he stood over us. When the reciter saw him, he fell silent. He greeted and said: "What were you doing?" We said: "O Messenger of Allah, a reciter was reciting to us and we were listening to his recitation." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Praise be to Allah who has placed among my community those with whom I have been commanded to keep myself patient." Then he sat in the midst of us to level himself among us, then he said, gesturing with his hand like this, and the people formed a circle and their faces became visible. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not recognize any of them, and they were the poor emigrants. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Rejoice, destitute emigrants, in complete success on the Day of Resurrection: you will enter Paradise before the wealthy believers by half a day, which is equal to five hundred years." [136]

Hisham ibn Sulayman, from Abu Yazid al-Raqqashi, from Anas, said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "O assembly of the poor, Allah has been pleased that I should take pattern from your gatherings, and that Allah is with us," and He said: ﴿And keep yourself patient with those who call upon their Lord morning and evening﴾. For these are the gatherings of the prophets before you and of the righteous." [137]

Mu'awiya ibn Murra, from A'idh ibn Amr: Salman, Suhayb and Bilal were sitting when Abu Sufyan passed by them. They said to him: "The swords of Allah have not yet taken from the neck of the enemy of Allah what they should." Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) said to them: "You say this to the elder of Quraysh and its master?" Then he came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and he said: "O Abu Bakr, perhaps you have angered them; if you have angered them, you have angered your Lord." Abu Bakr fell upon them and said: "Perhaps I have angered you?" They said: "No, O Abu Bakr, may Allah forgive you." [An-Nasa'i]

﴿When those who believe in Our signs come to you…﴾: the scholars differed about the occasion of revelation of this verse.

Ikrimah said: It was revealed concerning those whom Allah prohibited His Prophet (ﷺ) from driving away. Whenever the Prophet (ﷺ) saw them, he would greet them first and say: "Praise be to Allah who has placed among my community those whom I was commanded to greet first with peace." [138]

Al-Kalbi said: When the verse ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord﴾ was revealed, Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) came to the Prophet (ﷺ), apologized to him for his statement and sought forgiveness of Allah for it, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I intended nothing by it but good." So ﴿When those who believe in Our signs come to you, say: "Peace be upon you…"﴾ was revealed concerning Umar (may Allah be pleased with him).

Ata' said: It was revealed concerning Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, Ali, Bilal, Salim, Abu Ubayda, Suhayb ibn Sinan, Umar, Ja'far, Uthman ibn Maz'un, Ammar ibn Yasir, al-Arqam ibn al-Arqam and Abu Salama ibn Abd al-Asad (may Allah be pleased with them all).

Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Men came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "We have committed many great sins." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) remained silent about them, so Allah revealed concerning these men: ﴿those who believe in Our signs, say: "Peace be upon you. Your Lord has prescribed for Himself mercy: whoever of you does evil in ignorance﴾.

Mujahid said: [ignorance] means he does not know the lawful from the unlawful; and "from his ignorance" means your Lord's command, and everyone who commits a sin does so in ignorance. It was also said: ignorant of what that sin brings upon him. It is said: he became ignorant when he preferred disobedience over obedience. ﴿then repents after it and makes amends﴾, meaning he turns back from his error and sets his deed right.
