Al-Kalbi said: When a noble saw a lowly person had embraced Islam before him, he would be too proud to accept Islam and say: "This one has preceded me in Islam," so he would not accept it. ﴿Is not Allah most knowing of the grateful?﴾, meaning the believers. This is the answer to their words "are these the ones on whom Allah has bestowed favor from among us?" It was also said: "Is not Allah most knowing of the grateful, those who give thanks for Islam when He guides them to it?"

Al-Ala' ibn Bashir, from Abu Bakr al-Naji, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, said: I was in a group among which were poor emigrants, some of whom covered others from nakedness. A reciter was reciting to us while we listened to his recitation. The Prophet (ﷺ) came upon us until he stood over us. When the reciter saw him, he fell silent. He greeted and said: "What were you doing?" We said: "O Messenger of Allah, a reciter was reciting to us and we were listening to his recitation." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Praise be to Allah who has placed among my community those with whom I have been commanded to keep myself patient." Then he sat in the midst of us to level himself among us, then he said, gesturing with his hand like this, and the people formed a circle and their faces became visible. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not recognize any of them, and they were the poor emigrants. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Rejoice, destitute emigrants, in complete success on the Day of Resurrection: you will enter Paradise before the wealthy believers by half a day, which is equal to five hundred years." [136]

Hisham ibn Sulayman, from Abu Yazid al-Raqqashi, from Anas, said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "O assembly of the poor, Allah has been pleased that I should take pattern from your gatherings, and that Allah is with us," and He said: ﴿And keep yourself patient with those who call upon their Lord morning and evening﴾. For these are the gatherings of the prophets before you and of the righteous." [137]

Mu'awiya ibn Murra, from A'idh ibn Amr: Salman, Suhayb and Bilal were sitting when Abu Sufyan passed by them. They said to him: "The swords of Allah have not yet taken from the neck of the enemy of Allah what they should." Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) said to them: "You say this to the elder of Quraysh and its master?" Then he came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and he said: "O Abu Bakr, perhaps you have angered them; if you have angered them, you have angered your Lord." Abu Bakr fell upon them and said: "Perhaps I have angered you?" They said: "No, O Abu Bakr, may Allah forgive you." [An-Nasa'i]

﴿When those who believe in Our signs come to you…﴾: the scholars differed about the occasion of revelation of this verse.

Ikrimah said: It was revealed concerning those whom Allah prohibited His Prophet (ﷺ) from driving away. Whenever the Prophet (ﷺ) saw them, he would greet them first and say: "Praise be to Allah who has placed among my community those whom I was commanded to greet first with peace." [138]

Al-Kalbi said: When the verse ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord﴾ was revealed, Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) came to the Prophet (ﷺ), apologized to him for his statement and sought forgiveness of Allah for it, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I intended nothing by it but good." So ﴿When those who believe in Our signs come to you, say: "Peace be upon you…"﴾ was revealed concerning Umar (may Allah be pleased with him).

Ata' said: It was revealed concerning Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, Ali, Bilal, Salim, Abu Ubayda, Suhayb ibn Sinan, Umar, Ja'far, Uthman ibn Maz'un, Ammar ibn Yasir, al-Arqam ibn al-Arqam and Abu Salama ibn Abd al-Asad (may Allah be pleased with them all).

Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Men came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "We have committed many great sins." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) remained silent about them, so Allah revealed concerning these men: ﴿those who believe in Our signs, say: "Peace be upon you. Your Lord has prescribed for Himself mercy: whoever of you does evil in ignorance﴾.

Mujahid said: [ignorance] means he does not know the lawful from the unlawful; and "from his ignorance" means your Lord's command, and everyone who commits a sin does so in ignorance. It was also said: ignorant of what that sin brings upon him. It is said: he became ignorant when he preferred disobedience over obedience. ﴿then repents after it and makes amends﴾, meaning he turns back from his error and sets his deed right. It was also said: he makes his repentance sincere. ﴿indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ The reciters differed on the reading of ﴿annahu﴾. The Kufans [read it with a fatha on the alif in both places]. Ibn Kathir, al-A'mash, Ibn Umar, Hamza and al-Kisa'i read it as a fresh sentence (isti'naf) [with fatha in one place and kasra in the other]. Al-Hasan, Asim and Ya'qub read it in the accusative as a substitute for "mercy". The people of Medina read the first with a fatha, on the sense of "and He prescribed that he…", and read the second with a kasra as a fresh sentence, because what follows it is never reported. ﴿And thus﴾, that is, in this manner. It was also said: its meaning is "and We have explained to you in this surah and this verse."

And it came in the highest of what is explained concerning the deniers: ﴿Thus We detail the signs﴾, that is, We distinguish and make clear to you Our proof and Our evidences concerning everyone who denies, the people of falsehood. ﴿And that the way of the criminals may become evident﴾: the verb is raised, and its meaning is "that the path of the criminals may become manifest and clear." It is said: "the thing became clear (bana), made clear (abana), became clear in its explanation (tibyan) and became distinct (tabayyana) when it became apparent and plain." The word "sabil" (way) is masculine and feminine: Tamim treat it as masculine, while the people of the Hijaz treat it as feminine. The evidence for the masculine is His words: ﴿And if they see the way of right guidance, they will not adopt it as a way; but if they see the way of error, they will adopt it as a way﴾ [7:146]. The evidence for the feminine is His words: ﴿Why do you bar from the way of Allah those who believe, seeking to make it crooked?﴾ [7:86], and His words: ﴿Say, "This is my way; I invite to Allah with insight"﴾ [12:108]. Therefore one reading is "wa-litastabina" with the yā' and another with the tā', and the people of Medina read "wa-litastabina" with the tā' and "sabīla" in the accusative, addressing the Prophet (ﷺ): "and that you, O Muhammad, may learn the way of the criminals." It is said: "istabana al-shay'" and "tabayyanahu" when one knows it.

﴿Say: "Indeed I have been forbidden to worship those whom you invoke besides Allah."﴾ ﴿Say: "I will not follow your desires"﴾ in worshipping idols, and in driving away Bilal and Salman. ﴿Then I would have gone astray and would not be among the guided.﴾ That is, if I did that, I would have abandoned the path of truth and taken a way other than guidance.

Yahya ibn Wathhab [and Abu Raja'] read "qad dalilt" with a kasra on the lam. The two are dialects: "dalla yadullu" like "qalla yaqullu," and "dalla yadillu" like "malla yamillu." The first is more sound and more eloquent, because it is the dialect of the people of the Hijaz.

﴿Say: "Indeed I am upon clear evidence from my Lord"﴾: clarity, proof, insight and argument. ﴿and you have denied Him.﴾ That is, denied my Lord. ﴿What you seek to hasten is not with me﴾, meaning the punishment. It was revealed concerning al-Nadr ibn al-Harith. ﴿The decision is only Allah's; He relates the truth﴾. The people of the Hijaz and Asim read "yaqussu al-haqqa" with a doubled sad, meaning "He says the truth." They argued that it is written without a yā' in all the codices, and because it says "al-haqq," so one says "I judged by the truth." The rest read it with a dad, meaning "He decides by the truth," as evidenced by His words: ﴿And He is the best of deciders﴾ [7:87]. Al-fasl is the bringing of judgment. The reciters omitted the yā' for ease of pronunciation, then [...], as in His words ﴿burning of the Hellfire﴾ [37:163], ﴿Allah erases what He wills﴾ [13:39], ﴿Warnings will not avail﴾ [54:5], ﴿We will call the guards of Hell﴾ [96:18], and similar. They omitted the bā' from "al-haqq" because it is an adjective of the verbal noun, as if he judges the true judgment.

﴿Say: "If I had what you seek to hasten, within my power﴾, which is the punishment, ﴿the matter would have been decided between me and you﴾, that is, it would have been finished with the punishment and you would have been destroyed. ﴿And Allah is most knowing of the wrongdoers.﴾

﴿Say, "Have you considered: if Allah were to take away your hearing and your sight and seal over your hearts, what deity other than Allah could bring them back to you?"﴾ That is, they would not comprehend speech or see the proof. ﴿Who could bring it to you?﴾ That is, bring back what He took from you. ﴿Observe how We vary the signs﴾ (nubayyin lahum al-ayat), that is, We make the signs clear to them, ﴿yet they turn away﴾ (yasdifun), that is, they turn aside from them, denying them.

﴿Say: "Have you considered: if the punishment of Allah comes upon you suddenly (baghtatan), or openly (jahratan), with visible sight and witness, [for what you associated with Him], will anyone be destroyed except the wrongdoing people?"﴾ The wrongdoers are the polytheists.

﴿We send the messengers only as bearers of good news and warners. So whoever believes and does righteous deeds, there will be no fear for them﴾ when those in the Fire fear, ﴿nor will they grieve﴾ when they grieve. ﴿But those who deny Our signs﴾, meaning Muhammad and the Qur'an, ﴿the punishment will touch them﴾, that is, afflict them, ﴿for what they used to defiantly do﴾, that is, commit.

﴿Say: "I do not tell you that I have the treasures of Allah﴾, meaning the provision of Allah, ﴿nor do I know the unseen﴾, that is, what is hidden from people, ﴿nor do I tell you that I am an angel﴾, so that you would reject my words and deny my command. ﴿I only follow what is revealed to me.﴾" That is not disallowed nor impossible by reason, given the existence of the evidences and the conclusive proof.

﴿Say: "Are the blind and the seeing alike? Will you not reflect?"﴾ The disbelievers and the believers, the misguided and the guided, are not alike.

﴿And warn with it﴾, that is, with the Qur'an, ﴿those who fear that they will be gathered﴾, that is, raised and brought to life, ﴿to their Lord.﴾ Ad-Dahhak said: "with it" refers to Allah. Another view: ﴿those who know that they will be gathered, because their fear is due to what their deeds have been.﴾ ﴿They will have no protector besides Him﴾, meaning no close one who benefits them, ﴿nor any intercessor﴾ to intercede for them, ﴿so that they may fear Him.﴾

﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening…﴾ Sulayman and Khabbab ibn al-Aratt said: this verse was revealed concerning us.

Al-Aqra' ibn Habis al-Tamimi and Uyayna ibn Hisn al-Fazari, who were among those whose hearts were to be softened (al-mu'allafa qulubuhum), came and found the Prophet (ﷺ) sitting with Bilal, Suhayb, Ammar and Khabbab, along with some weak Muslims. When they saw them around him, they belittled them and came to him and said: "O Messenger of Allah, if you sat at the head of the gathering and these people were away, and removed their woolen tunics, which were the only garments they had, we would sit with you, converse with you and take from you." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I am not one to drive away the believers." They said: "Then we wish you would make for us a gathering of your own, by which the Arabs would recognize our superiority, for the delegations of the Arabs come to you, and we are ashamed that the Arabs should see us with these slaves. When we come to you, let them be removed, and when we finish, sit with them if you wish." He said: "Yes." They said: "Write us a document to that effect." So he called for a sheet and called Ali to write.

He said: "While we were sitting in a corner, Jibril (peace be upon him) came down with the words: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening…﴾ [6:52], unless by something [else]." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) threw the sheet from his hand, then called us. We came to him while he was saying: ﴿Peace be upon you. Your Lord has prescribed for Himself mercy﴾ [6:54]. We would sit with him, and when he wished to rise, he rose and left us. Then Allah revealed this verse: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord…﴾. He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would sit with us patiently and we would draw close to him until our knees almost touched his knees. When the hour came for him to rise, we rose and left him until he stood up. He said: "Praise be to Allah who did not take me until He commanded me to keep myself patient with a people from my community: [your life is with you and your death is with you]." [135]

Al-Kalbi said: They said to him: "Make a day for us and a day for them." He said: "I will not do that." They said: "Then make the gathering one and come to us, and turn your back to them." So Allah revealed this verse.

Al-Ash'ath ibn Sawwar narrated from Idris, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: The chiefs of Quraysh passed by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), along with Suhayb, Khabbab, Bilal, Ammar and others of the weak Muslims. They said: "O Muhammad, are you pleased with these from your people? Shall we be followers of these? Are these the ones on whom Allah has bestowed favor from among us? Drive them away from you; perhaps if you drive them away, we will follow you." So Allah revealed: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord…﴾. He said: Quraysh had said: "Were it not for Bilal and Ibn Umm Abd, we would follow Muhammad." So Allah revealed this verse.

Ikrimah said: Utba ibn Rabi'a, Shayba ibn Umayya, Mut'im ibn Adi, al-Harith ibn Nawfal, Qurza ibn Abd and Amr ibn Nawfal, among the nobles of Banu Abd Manaf from the people of disbelief, came to Abu Talib and said: "O Abu Talib, if your nephew Muhammad would drive away our clients and allies, for they are our slaves, it would be greater in our hearts, more obedient to him among us, and closer to our following him and affirming him." Abu Talib came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and told him what they had concealed. Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "If you did that, we would see what they want and where they will end up." Then this verse was revealed concerning their statement. When it was revealed, Umar ibn al-Khattab came and apologized for his statement.

Jubayr ibn Nufayl said: The Quraysh came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "You sent for us, so drive these scum away from you, and we will be your companions." So Allah revealed: ﴿And do not drive away…﴾.

Ibn Abbas said: ﴿those who call upon their Lord﴾ means those who worship their Lord with the obligatory prayer, ﴿morning and evening﴾ means the dawn prayer and the afternoon prayer. This was because some poor people were with the Prophet (ﷺ), and some of the nobles said: "When we pray, let these be delayed, and let them pray behind us." So Allah revealed: ﴿And do not drive away those who…﴾.

Hamza ibn Isa said: I entered upon al-Hasan and said: "O Abu Sa'id, what do you say about the words of Allah: ﴿And do not drive away those who believe﴾?" He said: "No, rather they are those who guard the prayers in congregation."

Mujahid said: I prayed the dawn prayer with Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab (may Allah be pleased with him). When the imam finished the salam, the people hurried to the storyteller (al-qass). Sa'id said: "How quickly the people rush to this gathering!"

Mujahid said: I said: "They interpret the words of Allah: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening﴾." He meant that this refers only to the prayer we have just left, and we said they remember their Lord.

Abu Ja'far said: meaning they recite the Qur'an.

﴿seeking His face﴾ is the answer to His words ﴿You are not accountable for them in anything﴾ [6:52]. His words ﴿so you would be among the wrongdoers﴾ are the answer to His words ﴿and do not drive away﴾; ﴿no one﴾ is the answer to a negation, and ﴿Allah﴾ is the answer to the prohibition. ﴿Among the wrongdoers﴾, meaning those who harm themselves through disobedience. Driving away is misplaced when it is not in its proper place.

﴿And thus We tested some of them by others﴾ [6:53]: the lowly and the customary ranking with respect to the master and the wealthy. ﴿So that they say: "Are these the ones on whom Allah has bestowed favor from among us?"﴾ That is, the nobles, the rich, say: "these," meaning the poor and weak, "on whom Allah has bestowed favor from among us." Al-Kalbi said: When a noble saw a lowly person had embraced Islam before him, he would be too proud to accept Islam and say: "This one has preceded me in Islam," so he would not accept it. ﴿Is not Allah most knowing of the grateful?﴾, meaning the believers. This is the answer to their words "are these the ones on whom Allah has bestowed favor from among us?" It was also said: "Is not Allah most knowing of the grateful, those who give thanks for Islam when He guides them to it?"

Al-Ala' ibn Bashir, from Abu Bakr al-Naji, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, said: I was in a group among which were poor emigrants, some of whom covered others from nakedness. A reciter was reciting to us while we listened to his recitation. The Prophet (ﷺ) came upon us until he stood over us. When the reciter saw him, he fell silent. He greeted and said: "What were you doing?" We said: "O Messenger of Allah, a reciter was reciting to us and we were listening to his recitation." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Praise be to Allah who has placed among my community those with whom I have been commanded to keep myself patient." Then he sat in the midst of us to level himself among us, then he said, gesturing with his hand like this, and the people formed a circle and their faces became visible. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not recognize any of them, and they were the poor emigrants. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Rejoice, destitute emigrants, in complete success on the Day of Resurrection: you will enter Paradise before the wealthy believers by half a day, which is equal to five hundred years." [136]

Hisham ibn Sulayman, from Abu Yazid al-Raqqashi, from Anas, said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "O assembly of the poor, Allah has been pleased that I should take pattern from your gatherings, and that Allah is with us," and He said: ﴿And keep yourself patient with those who call upon their Lord morning and evening﴾. For these are the gatherings of the prophets before you and of the righteous." [137]

Mu'awiya ibn Murra, from A'idh ibn Amr: Salman, Suhayb and Bilal were sitting when Abu Sufyan passed by them. They said to him: "The swords of Allah have not yet taken from the neck of the enemy of Allah what they should." Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) said to them: "You say this to the elder of Quraysh and its master?" Then he came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and he said: "O Abu Bakr, perhaps you have angered them; if you have angered them, you have angered your Lord." Abu Bakr fell upon them and said: "Perhaps I have angered you?" They said: "No, O Abu Bakr, may Allah forgive you." [An-Nasa'i]

﴿When those who believe in Our signs come to you…﴾: the scholars differed about the occasion of revelation of this verse.

Ikrimah said: It was revealed concerning those whom Allah prohibited His Prophet (ﷺ) from driving away. Whenever the Prophet (ﷺ) saw them, he would greet them first and say: "Praise be to Allah who has placed among my community those whom I was commanded to greet first with peace." [138]

Al-Kalbi said: When the verse ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord﴾ was revealed, Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) came to the Prophet (ﷺ), apologized to him for his statement and sought forgiveness of Allah for it, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I intended nothing by it but good." So ﴿When those who believe in Our signs come to you, say: "Peace be upon you…"﴾ was revealed concerning Umar (may Allah be pleased with him).

Ata' said: It was revealed concerning Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, Ali, Bilal, Salim, Abu Ubayda, Suhayb ibn Sinan, Umar, Ja'far, Uthman ibn Maz'un, Ammar ibn Yasir, al-Arqam ibn al-Arqam and Abu Salama ibn Abd al-Asad (may Allah be pleased with them all).

Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Men came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "We have committed many great sins." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) remained silent about them, so Allah revealed concerning these men: ﴿those who believe in Our signs, say: "Peace be upon you. Your Lord has prescribed for Himself mercy: whoever of you does evil in ignorance﴾.

Mujahid said: [ignorance] means he does not know the lawful from the unlawful; and "from his ignorance" means your Lord's command, and everyone who commits a sin does so in ignorance. It was also said: ignorant of what that sin brings upon him. It is said: he became ignorant when he preferred disobedience over obedience. ﴿then repents after it and makes amends﴾, meaning he turns back from his error and sets his deed right. It was also said: he makes his repentance sincere. ﴿indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ The reciters differed on the reading of ﴿annahu﴾. The Kufans [read it with a fatha on the alif in both places]. Ibn Kathir, al-A'mash, Ibn Umar, Hamza and al-Kisa'i read it as a fresh sentence (isti'naf) [with fatha in one place and kasra in the other]. Al-Hasan, Asim and Ya'qub read it in the accusative as a substitute for "mercy". The people of Medina read the first with a fatha, on the sense of "and He prescribed that he…", and read the second with a kasra as a fresh sentence, because what follows it is never reported. ﴿And thus﴾, that is, in this manner. It was also said: its meaning is "and We have explained to you in this surah and this verse."

And it came in the highest of what is explained concerning the deniers: ﴿Thus We detail the signs﴾, that is, We distinguish and make clear to you Our proof and Our evidences concerning everyone who denies, the people of falsehood. ﴿And that the way of the criminals may become evident﴾: the verb is raised, and its meaning is "that the path of the criminals may become manifest and clear." It is said: "the thing became clear (bana), made clear (abana), became clear in its explanation (tibyan) and became distinct (tabayyana) when it became apparent and plain." The word "sabil" (way) is masculine and feminine: Tamim treat it as masculine, while the people of the Hijaz treat it as feminine. The evidence for the masculine is His words: ﴿And if they see the way of right guidance, they will not adopt it as a way; but if they see the way of error, they will adopt it as a way﴾ [7:146]. The evidence for the feminine is His words: ﴿Why do you bar from the way of Allah those who believe, seeking to make it crooked?﴾ [7:86], and His words: ﴿Say, "This is my way; I invite to Allah with insight"﴾ [12:108]. Therefore one reading is "wa-litastabina" with the yā' and another with the tā', and the people of Medina read "wa-litastabina" with the tā' and "sabīla" in the accusative, addressing the Prophet (ﷺ): "and that you, O Muhammad, may learn the way of the criminals." It is said: "istabana al-shay'" and "tabayyanahu" when one knows it.

﴿Say: "Indeed I have been forbidden to worship those whom you invoke besides Allah."﴾ ﴿Say: "I will not follow your desires"﴾ in worshipping idols, and in driving away Bilal and Salman. ﴿Then I would have gone astray and would not be among the guided.﴾ That is, if I did that, I would have abandoned the path of truth and taken a way other than guidance.

Yahya ibn Wathhab [and Abu Raja'] read "qad dalilt" with a kasra on the lam. The two are dialects: "dalla yadullu" like "qalla yaqullu," and "dalla yadillu" like "malla yamillu." The first is more sound and more eloquent, because it is the dialect of the people of the Hijaz.

﴿Say: "Indeed I am upon clear evidence from my Lord"﴾: clarity, proof, insight and argument. ﴿and you have denied Him.﴾ That is, denied my Lord. ﴿What you seek to hasten is not with me﴾, meaning the punishment. It was revealed concerning al-Nadr ibn al-Harith. ﴿The decision is only Allah's; He relates the truth﴾. The people of the Hijaz and Asim read "yaqussu al-haqqa" with a doubled sad, meaning "He says the truth." They argued that it is written without a yā' in all the codices, and because it says "al-haqq," so one says "I judged by the truth." The rest read it with a dad, meaning "He decides by the truth," as evidenced by His words: ﴿And He is the best of deciders﴾ [7:87]. Al-fasl is the bringing of judgment. The reciters omitted the yā' for ease of pronunciation, then [...], as in His words ﴿burning of the Hellfire﴾ [37:163], ﴿Allah erases what He wills﴾ [13:39], ﴿Warnings will not avail﴾ [54:5], ﴿We will call the guards of Hell﴾ [96:18], and similar. They omitted the bā' from "al-haqq" because it is an adjective of the verbal noun, as if he judges the true judgment.

﴿Say: "If I had what you seek to hasten, within my power﴾, which is the punishment, ﴿the matter would have been decided between me and you﴾, that is, it would have been finished with the punishment and you would have been destroyed. ﴿And Allah is most knowing of the wrongdoers.﴾

﴿Say, "Have you considered: if Allah were to take away your hearing and your sight and seal over your hearts, what deity other than Allah could bring them back to you?"﴾ That is, they would not comprehend speech or see the proof. ﴿Who could bring it to you?﴾ That is, bring back what He took from you. ﴿Observe how We vary the signs﴾ (nubayyin lahum al-ayat), that is, We make the signs clear to them, ﴿yet they turn away﴾ (yasdifun), that is, they turn aside from them, denying them.

﴿Say: "Have you considered: if the punishment of Allah comes upon you suddenly (baghtatan), or openly (jahratan), with visible sight and witness, [for what you associated with Him], will anyone be destroyed except the wrongdoing people?"﴾ The wrongdoers are the polytheists.

﴿We send the messengers only as bearers of good news and warners. So whoever believes and does righteous deeds, there will be no fear for them﴾ when those in the Fire fear, ﴿nor will they grieve﴾ when they grieve. ﴿But those who deny Our signs﴾, meaning Muhammad and the Qur'an, ﴿the punishment will touch them﴾, that is, afflict them, ﴿for what they used to defiantly do﴾, that is, commit.

﴿Say: "I do not tell you that I have the treasures of Allah﴾, meaning the provision of Allah, ﴿nor do I know the unseen﴾, that is, what is hidden from people, ﴿nor do I tell you that I am an angel﴾, so that you would reject my words and deny my command. ﴿I only follow what is revealed to me.﴾" That is not disallowed nor impossible by reason, given the existence of the evidences and the conclusive proof.

﴿Say: "Are the blind and the seeing alike? Will you not reflect?"﴾ The disbelievers and the believers, the misguided and the guided, are not alike.

﴿And warn with it﴾, that is, with the Qur'an, ﴿those who fear that they will be gathered﴾, that is, raised and brought to life, ﴿to their Lord.﴾ Ad-Dahhak said: "with it" refers to Allah. Another view: ﴿those who know that they will be gathered, because their fear is due to what their deeds have been.﴾ ﴿They will have no protector besides Him﴾, meaning no close one who benefits them, ﴿nor any intercessor﴾ to intercede for them, ﴿so that they may fear Him.﴾

﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening…﴾ Sulayman and Khabbab ibn al-Aratt said: this verse was revealed concerning us.

Al-Aqra' ibn Habis al-Tamimi and Uyayna ibn Hisn al-Fazari, who were among those whose hearts were to be softened (al-mu'allafa qulubuhum), came and found the Prophet (ﷺ) sitting with Bilal, Suhayb, Ammar and Khabbab, along with some weak Muslims. When they saw them around him, they belittled them and came to him and said: "O Messenger of Allah, if you sat at the head of the gathering and these people were away, and removed their woolen tunics, which were the only garments they had, we would sit with you, converse with you and take from you." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I am not one to drive away the believers." They said: "Then we wish you would make for us a gathering of your own, by which the Arabs would recognize our superiority, for the delegations of the Arabs come to you, and we are ashamed that the Arabs should see us with these slaves. When we come to you, let them be removed, and when we finish, sit with them if you wish." He said: "Yes." They said: "Write us a document to that effect." So he called for a sheet and called Ali to write.

He said: "While we were sitting in a corner, Jibril (peace be upon him) came down with the words: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening…﴾ [6:52], unless by something [else]." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) threw the sheet from his hand, then called us. We came to him while he was saying: ﴿Peace be upon you. Your Lord has prescribed for Himself mercy﴾ [6:54]. We would sit with him, and when he wished to rise, he rose and left us. Then Allah revealed this verse: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord…﴾. He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would sit with us patiently and we would draw close to him until our knees almost touched his knees. When the hour came for him to rise, we rose and left him until he stood up. He said: "Praise be to Allah who did not take me until He commanded me to keep myself patient with a people from my community: [your life is with you and your death is with you]." [135]

Al-Kalbi said: They said to him: "Make a day for us and a day for them." He said: "I will not do that." They said: "Then make the gathering one and come to us, and turn your back to them." So Allah revealed this verse.

Al-Ash'ath ibn Sawwar narrated from Idris, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: The chiefs of Quraysh passed by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), along with Suhayb, Khabbab, Bilal, Ammar and others of the weak Muslims. They said: "O Muhammad, are you pleased with these from your people? Shall we be followers of these? Are these the ones on whom Allah has bestowed favor from among us? Drive them away from you; perhaps if you drive them away, we will follow you." So Allah revealed: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord…﴾. He said: Quraysh had said: "Were it not for Bilal and Ibn Umm Abd, we would follow Muhammad." So Allah revealed this verse.

Ikrimah said: Utba ibn Rabi'a, Shayba ibn Umayya, Mut'im ibn Adi, al-Harith ibn Nawfal, Qurza ibn Abd and Amr ibn Nawfal, among the nobles of Banu Abd Manaf from the people of disbelief, came to Abu Talib and said: "O Abu Talib, if your nephew Muhammad would drive away our clients and allies, for they are our slaves, it would be greater in our hearts, more obedient to him among us, and closer to our following him and affirming him." Abu Talib came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and told him what they had concealed. Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "If you did that, we would see what they want and where they will end up." Then this verse was revealed concerning their statement. When it was revealed, Umar ibn al-Khattab came and apologized for his statement.

Jubayr ibn Nufayl said: The Quraysh came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "You sent for us, so drive these scum away from you, and we will be your companions." So Allah revealed: ﴿And do not drive away…﴾.

Ibn Abbas said: ﴿those who call upon their Lord﴾ means those who worship their Lord with the obligatory prayer, ﴿morning and evening﴾ means the dawn prayer and the afternoon prayer. This was because some poor people were with the Prophet (ﷺ), and some of the nobles said: "When we pray, let these be delayed, and let them pray behind us." So Allah revealed: ﴿And do not drive away those who…﴾.

Hamza ibn Isa said: I entered upon al-Hasan and said: "O Abu Sa'id, what do you say about the words of Allah: ﴿And do not drive away those who believe﴾?" He said: "No, rather they are those who guard the prayers in congregation."

Mujahid said: I prayed the dawn prayer with Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab (may Allah be pleased with him). When the imam finished the salam, the people hurried to the storyteller (al-qass). Sa'id said: "How quickly the people rush to this gathering!"

Mujahid said: I said: "They interpret the words of Allah: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening﴾." He meant that this refers only to the prayer we have just left, and we said they remember their Lord.

Abu Ja'far said: meaning they recite the Qur'an.

﴿seeking His face﴾ is the answer to His words ﴿You are not accountable for them in anything﴾ [6:52]. His words ﴿so you would be among the wrongdoers﴾ are the answer to His words ﴿and do not drive away﴾; ﴿no one﴾ is the answer to a negation, and ﴿Allah﴾ is the answer to the prohibition. ﴿Among the wrongdoers﴾, meaning those who harm themselves through disobedience. Driving away is misplaced when it is not in its proper place.

﴿And thus We tested some of them by others﴾ [6:53]: the lowly and the customary ranking with respect to the master and the wealthy. ﴿So that they say: "Are these the ones on whom Allah has bestowed favor from among us?"﴾ That is, the nobles, the rich, say: "these," meaning the poor and weak, "on whom Allah has bestowed favor from among us." Al-Kalbi said: When a noble saw a lowly person had embraced Islam before him, he would be too proud to accept Islam and say: "This one has preceded me in Islam," so he would not accept it. ﴿Is not Allah most knowing of the grateful?﴾, meaning the believers. This is the answer to their words "are these the ones on whom Allah has bestowed favor from among us?" It was also said: "Is not Allah most knowing of the grateful, those who give thanks for Islam when He guides them to it?"

Al-Ala' ibn Bashir, from Abu Bakr al-Naji, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, said: I was in a group among which were poor emigrants, some of whom covered others from nakedness. A reciter was reciting to us while we listened to his recitation. The Prophet (ﷺ) came upon us until he stood over us. When the reciter saw him, he fell silent. He greeted and said: "What were you doing?" We said: "O Messenger of Allah, a reciter was reciting to us and we were listening to his recitation." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Praise be to Allah who has placed among my community those with whom I have been commanded to keep myself patient." Then he sat in the midst of us to level himself among us, then he said, gesturing with his hand like this, and the people formed a circle and their faces became visible. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not recognize any of them, and they were the poor emigrants. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Rejoice, destitute emigrants, in complete success on the Day of Resurrection: you will enter Paradise before the wealthy believers by half a day, which is equal to five hundred years." [136]

Hisham ibn Sulayman, from Abu Yazid al-Raqqashi, from Anas, said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "O assembly of the poor, Allah has been pleased that I should take pattern from your gatherings, and that Allah is with us," and He said: ﴿And keep yourself patient with those who call upon their Lord morning and evening﴾. For these are the gatherings of the prophets before you and of the righteous." [137]

Mu'awiya ibn Murra, from A'idh ibn Amr: Salman, Suhayb and Bilal were sitting when Abu Sufyan passed by them. They said to him: "The swords of Allah have not yet taken from the neck of the enemy of Allah what they should." Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) said to them: "You say this to the elder of Quraysh and its master?" Then he came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and he said: "O Abu Bakr, perhaps you have angered them; if you have angered them, you have angered your Lord." Abu Bakr fell upon them and said: "Perhaps I have angered you?" They said: "No, O Abu Bakr, may Allah forgive you." [An-Nasa'i]

﴿When those who believe in Our signs come to you…﴾: the scholars differed about the occasion of revelation of this verse.

Ikrimah said: It was revealed concerning those whom Allah prohibited His Prophet (ﷺ) from driving away. Whenever the Prophet (ﷺ) saw them, he would greet them first and say: "Praise be to Allah who has placed among my community those whom I was commanded to greet first with peace." [138]

Al-Kalbi said: When the verse ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord﴾ was revealed, Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) came to the Prophet (ﷺ), apologized to him for his statement and sought forgiveness of Allah for it, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I intended nothing by it but good." So ﴿When those who believe in Our signs come to you, say: "Peace be upon you…"﴾ was revealed concerning Umar (may Allah be pleased with him).

Ata' said: It was revealed concerning Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, Ali, Bilal, Salim, Abu Ubayda, Suhayb ibn Sinan, Umar, Ja'far, Uthman ibn Maz'un, Ammar ibn Yasir, al-Arqam ibn al-Arqam and Abu Salama ibn Abd al-Asad (may Allah be pleased with them all).

Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Men came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "We have committed many great sins." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) remained silent about them, so Allah revealed concerning these men: ﴿those who believe in Our signs, say: "Peace be upon you. Your Lord has prescribed for Himself mercy: whoever of you does evil in ignorance﴾.

Mujahid said: [ignorance] means he does not know the lawful from the unlawful; and "from his ignorance" means your Lord's command, and everyone who commits a sin does so in ignorance. It was also said: ignorant of what that sin brings upon him. It is said: he became ignorant when he preferred disobedience over obedience. ﴿then repents after it and makes amends﴾, meaning he turns back from his error and sets his deed right. It was also said: he makes his repentance sincere. ﴿indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ The reciters differed on the reading of ﴿annahu﴾. The Kufans [read it with a fatha on the alif in both places]. Ibn Kathir, al-A'mash, Ibn Umar, Hamza and al-Kisa'i read it as a fresh sentence (isti'naf) [with fatha in one place and kasra in the other]. Al-Hasan, Asim and Ya'qub read it in the accusative as a substitute for "mercy". The people of Medina read the first with a fatha, on the sense of "and He prescribed that he…", and read the second with a kasra as a fresh sentence, because what follows it is never reported. ﴿And thus﴾, that is, in this manner. It was also said: its meaning is "and We have explained to you in this surah and this verse."

And it came in the highest of what is explained concerning the deniers: ﴿Thus We detail the signs﴾, that is, We distinguish and make clear to you Our proof and Our evidences concerning everyone who denies, the people of falsehood. ﴿And that the way of the criminals may become evident﴾: the verb is raised, and its meaning is "that the path of the criminals may become manifest and clear." It is said: "the thing became clear (bana), made clear (abana), became clear in its explanation (tibyan) and became distinct (tabayyana) when it became apparent and plain." The word "sabil" (way) is masculine and feminine: Tamim treat it as masculine, while the people of the Hijaz treat it as feminine. The evidence for the masculine is His words: ﴿And if they see the way of right guidance, they will not adopt it as a way; but if they see the way of error, they will adopt it as a way﴾ [7:146]. The evidence for the feminine is His words: ﴿Why do you bar from the way of Allah those who believe, seeking to make it crooked?﴾ [7:86], and His words: ﴿Say, "This is my way; I invite to Allah with insight"﴾ [12:108]. Therefore one reading is "wa-litastabina" with the yā' and another with the tā', and the people of Medina read "wa-litastabina" with the tā' and "sabīla" in the accusative, addressing the Prophet (ﷺ): "and that you, O Muhammad, may learn the way of the criminals." It is said: "istabana al-shay'" and "tabayyanahu" when one knows it.

﴿Say: "Indeed I have been forbidden to worship those whom you invoke besides Allah."﴾ ﴿Say: "I will not follow your desires"﴾ in worshipping idols, and in driving away Bilal and Salman. ﴿Then I would have gone astray and would not be among the guided.﴾ That is, if I did that, I would have abandoned the path of truth and taken a way other than guidance.

Yahya ibn Wathhab [and Abu Raja'] read "qad dalilt" with a kasra on the lam. The two are dialects: "dalla yadullu" like "qalla yaqullu," and "dalla yadillu" like "malla yamillu." The first is more sound and more eloquent, because it is the dialect of the people of the Hijaz.

﴿Say: "Indeed I am upon clear evidence from my Lord"﴾: clarity, proof, insight and argument. ﴿and you have denied Him.﴾ That is, denied my Lord. ﴿What you seek to hasten is not with me﴾, meaning the punishment. It was revealed concerning al-Nadr ibn al-Harith. ﴿The decision is only Allah's; He relates the truth﴾. The people of the Hijaz and Asim read "yaqussu al-haqqa" with a doubled sad, meaning "He says the truth." They argued that it is written without a yā' in all the codices, and because it says "al-haqq," so one says "I judged by the truth." The rest read it with a dad, meaning "He decides by the truth," as evidenced by His words: ﴿And He is the best of deciders﴾ [7:87]. Al-fasl is the bringing of judgment. The reciters omitted the yā' for ease of pronunciation, then [...], as in His words ﴿burning of the Hellfire﴾ [37:163], ﴿Allah erases what He wills﴾ [13:39], ﴿Warnings will not avail﴾ [54:5], ﴿We will call the guards of Hell﴾ [96:18], and similar. They omitted the bā' from "al-haqq" because it is an adjective of the verbal noun, as if he judges the true judgment.

﴿Say: "If I had what you seek to hasten, within my power﴾, which is the punishment, ﴿the matter would have been decided between me and you﴾, that is, it would have been finished with the punishment and you would have been destroyed. ﴿And Allah is most knowing of the wrongdoers.﴾

﴿Say, "Have you considered: if Allah were to take away your hearing and your sight and seal over your hearts, what deity other than Allah could bring them back to you?"﴾ That is, they would not comprehend speech or see the proof. ﴿Who could bring it to you?﴾ That is, bring back what He took from you. ﴿Observe how We vary the signs﴾ (nubayyin lahum al-ayat), that is, We make the signs clear to them, ﴿yet they turn away﴾ (yasdifun), that is, they turn aside from them, denying them.

﴿Say: "Have you considered: if the punishment of Allah comes upon you suddenly (baghtatan), or openly (jahratan), with visible sight and witness, [for what you associated with Him], will anyone be destroyed except the wrongdoing people?"﴾ The wrongdoers are the polytheists.

﴿We send the messengers only as bearers of good news and warners. So whoever believes and does righteous deeds, there will be no fear for them﴾ when those in the Fire fear, ﴿nor will they grieve﴾ when they grieve. ﴿But those who deny Our signs﴾, meaning Muhammad and the Qur'an, ﴿the punishment will touch them﴾, that is, afflict them, ﴿for what they used to defiantly do﴾, that is, commit.

﴿Say: "I do not tell you that I have the treasures of Allah﴾, meaning the provision of Allah, ﴿nor do I know the unseen﴾, that is, what is hidden from people, ﴿nor do I tell you that I am an angel﴾, so that you would reject my words and deny my command. ﴿I only follow what is revealed to me.﴾" That is not disallowed nor impossible by reason, given the existence of the evidences and the conclusive proof.

﴿Say: "Are the blind and the seeing alike? Will you not reflect?"﴾ The disbelievers and the believers, the misguided and the guided, are not alike.

﴿And warn with it﴾, that is, with the Qur'an, ﴿those who fear that they will be gathered﴾, that is, raised and brought to life, ﴿to their Lord.﴾ Ad-Dahhak said: "with it" refers to Allah. Another view: ﴿those who know that they will be gathered, because their fear is due to what their deeds have been.﴾ ﴿They will have no protector besides Him﴾, meaning no close one who benefits them, ﴿nor any intercessor﴾ to intercede for them, ﴿so that they may fear Him.﴾

﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening…﴾ Sulayman and Khabbab ibn al-Aratt said: this verse was revealed concerning us.

Al-Aqra' ibn Habis al-Tamimi and Uyayna ibn Hisn al-Fazari, who were among those whose hearts were to be softened (al-mu'allafa qulubuhum), came and found the Prophet (ﷺ) sitting with Bilal, Suhayb, Ammar and Khabbab, along with some weak Muslims. When they saw them around him, they belittled them and came to him and said: "O Messenger of Allah, if you sat at the head of the gathering and these people were away, and removed their woolen tunics, which were the only garments they had, we would sit with you, converse with you and take from you." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I am not one to drive away the believers." They said: "Then we wish you would make for us a gathering of your own, by which the Arabs would recognize our superiority, for the delegations of the Arabs come to you, and we are ashamed that the Arabs should see us with these slaves. When we come to you, let them be removed, and when we finish, sit with them if you wish." He said: "Yes." They said: "Write us a document to that effect." So he called for a sheet and called Ali to write.

He said: "While we were sitting in a corner, Jibril (peace be upon him) came down with the words: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening…﴾ [6:52], unless by something [else]." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) threw the sheet from his hand, then called us. We came to him while he was saying: ﴿Peace be upon you. Your Lord has prescribed for Himself mercy﴾ [6:54]. We would sit with him, and when he wished to rise, he rose and left us. Then Allah revealed this verse: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord…﴾. He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would sit with us patiently and we would draw close to him until our knees almost touched his knees. When the hour came for him to rise, we rose and left him until he stood up. He said: "Praise be to Allah who did not take me until He commanded me to keep myself patient with a people from my community: [your life is with you and your death is with you]." [135]

Al-Kalbi said: They said to him: "Make a day for us and a day for them." He said: "I will not do that." They said: "Then make the gathering one and come to us, and turn your back to them." So Allah revealed this verse.

Al-Ash'ath ibn Sawwar narrated from Idris, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: The chiefs of Quraysh passed by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), along with Suhayb, Khabbab, Bilal, Ammar and others of the weak Muslims. They said: "O Muhammad, are you pleased with these from your people? Shall we be followers of these? Are these the ones on whom Allah has bestowed favor from among us? Drive them away from you; perhaps if you drive them away, we will follow you." So Allah revealed: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord…﴾. He said: Quraysh had said: "Were it not for Bilal and Ibn Umm Abd, we would follow Muhammad." So Allah revealed this verse.

Ikrimah said: Utba ibn Rabi'a, Shayba ibn Umayya, Mut'im ibn Adi, al-Harith ibn Nawfal, Qurza ibn Abd and Amr ibn Nawfal, among the nobles of Banu Abd Manaf from the people of disbelief, came to Abu Talib and said: "O Abu Talib, if your nephew Muhammad would drive away our clients and allies, for they are our slaves, it would be greater in our hearts, more obedient to him among us, and closer to our following him and affirming him." Abu Talib came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and told him what they had concealed. Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "If you did that, we would see what they want and where they will end up." Then this verse was revealed concerning their statement. When it was revealed, Umar ibn al-Khattab came and apologized for his statement.

Jubayr ibn Nufayl said: The Quraysh came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "You sent for us, so drive these scum away from you, and we will be your companions." So Allah revealed: ﴿And do not drive away…﴾.

Ibn Abbas said: ﴿those who call upon their Lord﴾ means those who worship their Lord with the obligatory prayer, ﴿morning and evening﴾ means the dawn prayer and the afternoon prayer. This was because some poor people were with the Prophet (ﷺ), and some of the nobles said: "When we pray, let these be delayed, and let them pray behind us." So Allah revealed: ﴿And do not drive away those who…﴾.

Hamza ibn Isa said: I entered upon al-Hasan and said: "O Abu Sa'id, what do you say about the words of Allah: ﴿And do not drive away those who believe﴾?" He said: "No, rather they are those who guard the prayers in congregation."

Mujahid said: I prayed the dawn prayer with Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab (may Allah be pleased with him). When the imam finished the salam, the people hurried to the storyteller (al-qass). Sa'id said: "How quickly the people rush to this gathering!"

Mujahid said: I said: "They interpret the words of Allah: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening﴾." He meant that this refers only to the prayer we have just left, and we said they remember their Lord.

Abu Ja'far said: meaning they recite the Qur'an.

﴿seeking His face﴾ is the answer to His words ﴿You are not accountable for them in anything﴾ [6:52]. His words ﴿so you would be among the wrongdoers﴾ are the answer to His words ﴿and do not drive away﴾; ﴿no one﴾ is the answer to a negation, and ﴿Allah﴾ is the answer to the prohibition. ﴿Among the wrongdoers﴾, meaning those who harm themselves through disobedience. Driving away is misplaced when it is not in its proper place.

﴿And thus We tested some of them by others﴾ [6:53]: the lowly and the customary ranking with respect to the master and the wealthy. ﴿So that they say: "Are these the ones on whom Allah has bestowed favor from among us?"﴾ That is, the nobles, the rich, say: "these," meaning the poor and weak, "on whom Allah has bestowed favor from among us." Al-Kalbi said: When a noble saw a lowly person had embraced Islam before him, he would be too proud to accept Islam and say: "This one has preceded me in Islam," so he would not accept it. ﴿Is not Allah most knowing of the grateful?﴾, meaning the believers. This is the answer to their words "are these the ones on whom Allah has bestowed favor from among us?" It was also said: "Is not Allah most knowing of the grateful, those who give thanks for Islam when He guides them to it?"

Al-Ala' ibn Bashir, from Abu Bakr al-Naji, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, said: I was in a group among which were poor emigrants, some of whom covered others from nakedness. A reciter was reciting to us while we listened to his recitation. The Prophet (ﷺ) came upon us until he stood over us. When the reciter saw him, he fell silent. He greeted and said: "What were you doing?" We said: "O Messenger of Allah, a reciter was reciting to us and we were listening to his recitation." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Praise be to Allah who has placed among my community those with whom I have been commanded to keep myself patient." Then he sat in the midst of us to level himself among us, then he said, gesturing with his hand like this, and the people formed a circle and their faces became visible. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not recognize any of them, and they were the poor emigrants. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Rejoice, destitute emigrants, in complete success on the Day of Resurrection: you will enter Paradise before the wealthy believers by half a day, which is equal to five hundred years." [136]

Hisham ibn Sulayman, from Abu Yazid al-Raqqashi, from Anas, said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "O assembly of the poor, Allah has been pleased that I should take pattern from your gatherings, and that Allah is with us," and He said: ﴿And keep yourself patient with those who call upon their Lord morning and evening﴾. For these are the gatherings of the prophets before you and of the righteous." [137]

Mu'awiya ibn Murra, from A'idh ibn Amr: Salman, Suhayb and Bilal were sitting when Abu Sufyan passed by them. They said to him: "The swords of Allah have not yet taken from the neck of the enemy of Allah what they should." Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) said to them: "You say this to the elder of Quraysh and its master?" Then he came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and he said: "O Abu Bakr, perhaps you have angered them; if you have angered them, you have angered your Lord." Abu Bakr fell upon them and said: "Perhaps I have angered you?" They said: "No, O Abu Bakr, may Allah forgive you." [An-Nasa'i]

﴿When those who believe in Our signs come to you…﴾: the scholars differed about the occasion of revelation of this verse.

Ikrimah said: It was revealed concerning those whom Allah prohibited His Prophet (ﷺ) from driving away. Whenever the Prophet (ﷺ) saw them, he would greet them first and say: "Praise be to Allah who has placed among my community those whom I was commanded to greet first with peace." [138]

Al-Kalbi said: When the verse ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord﴾ was revealed, Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) came to the Prophet (ﷺ), apologized to him for his statement and sought forgiveness of Allah for it, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I intended nothing by it but good." So ﴿When those who believe in Our signs come to you, say: "Peace be upon you…"﴾ was revealed concerning Umar (may Allah be pleased with him).

Ata' said: It was revealed concerning Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, Ali, Bilal, Salim, Abu Ubayda, Suhayb ibn Sinan, Umar, Ja'far, Uthman ibn Maz'un, Ammar ibn Yasir, al-Arqam ibn al-Arqam and Abu Salama ibn Abd al-Asad (may Allah be pleased with them all).

Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Men came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "We have committed many great sins." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) remained silent about them, so Allah revealed concerning these men: ﴿those who believe in Our signs, say: "Peace be upon you. Your Lord has prescribed for Himself mercy: whoever of you does evil in ignorance﴾.

Mujahid said: [ignorance] means he does not know the lawful from the unlawful; and "from his ignorance" means your Lord's command, and everyone who commits a sin does so in ignorance. It was also said: ignorant of what that sin brings upon him. It is said: he became ignorant when he preferred disobedience over obedience. ﴿then repents after it and makes amends﴾, meaning he turns back from his error and sets his deed right. It was also said: he makes his repentance sincere. ﴿indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ The reciters differed on the reading of ﴿annahu﴾. The Kufans [read it with a fatha on the alif in both places]. Ibn Kathir, al-A'mash, Ibn Umar, Hamza and al-Kisa'i read it as a fresh sentence (isti'naf) [with fatha in one place and kasra in the other]. Al-Hasan, Asim and Ya'qub read it in the accusative as a substitute for "mercy". The people of Medina read the first with a fatha, on the sense of "and He prescribed that he…", and read the second with a kasra as a fresh sentence, because what follows it is never reported. ﴿And thus﴾, that is, in this manner. It was also said: its meaning is "and We have explained to you in this surah and this verse."

And it came in the highest of what is explained concerning the deniers: ﴿Thus We detail the signs﴾, that is, We distinguish and make clear to you Our proof and Our evidences concerning everyone who denies, the people of falsehood. ﴿And that the way of the criminals may become evident﴾: the verb is raised, and its meaning is "that the path of the criminals may become manifest and clear." It is said: "the thing became clear (bana), made clear (abana), became clear in its explanation (tibyan) and became distinct (tabayyana) when it became apparent and plain." The word "sabil" (way) is masculine and feminine: Tamim treat it as masculine, while the people of the Hijaz treat it as feminine. The evidence for the masculine is His words: ﴿And if they see the way of right guidance, they will not adopt it as a way; but if they see the way of error, they will adopt it as a way﴾ [7:146]. The evidence for the feminine is His words: ﴿Why do you bar from the way of Allah those who believe, seeking to make it crooked?﴾ [7:86], and His words: ﴿Say, "This is my way; I invite to Allah with insight"﴾ [12:108]. Therefore one reading is "wa-litastabina" with the yā' and another with the tā', and the people of Medina read "wa-litastabina" with the tā' and "sabīla" in the accusative, addressing the Prophet (ﷺ): "and that you, O Muhammad, may learn the way of the criminals." It is said: "istabana al-shay'" and "tabayyanahu" when one knows it.

﴿Say: "Indeed I have been forbidden to worship those whom you invoke besides Allah."﴾ ﴿Say: "I will not follow your desires"﴾ in worshipping idols, and in driving away Bilal and Salman. ﴿Then I would have gone astray and would not be among the guided.﴾ That is, if I did that, I would have abandoned the path of truth and taken a way other than guidance.

Yahya ibn Wathhab [and Abu Raja'] read "qad dalilt" with a kasra on the lam. The two are dialects: "dalla yadullu" like "qalla yaqullu," and "dalla yadillu" like "malla yamillu." The first is more sound and more eloquent, because it is the dialect of the people of the Hijaz.

﴿Say: "Indeed I am upon clear evidence from my Lord"﴾: clarity, proof, insight and argument. ﴿and you have denied Him.﴾ That is, denied my Lord. ﴿What you seek to hasten is not with me﴾, meaning the punishment. It was revealed concerning al-Nadr ibn al-Harith. ﴿The decision is only Allah's; He relates the truth﴾. The people of the Hijaz and Asim read "yaqussu al-haqqa" with a doubled sad, meaning "He says the truth." They argued that it is written without a yā' in all the codices, and because it says "al-haqq," so one says "I judged by the truth." The rest read it with a dad, meaning "He decides by the truth," as evidenced by His words: ﴿And He is the best of deciders﴾ [7:87]. Al-fasl is the bringing of judgment. The reciters omitted the yā' for ease of pronunciation, then [...], as in His words ﴿burning of the Hellfire﴾ [37:163], ﴿Allah erases what He wills﴾ [13:39], ﴿Warnings will not avail﴾ [54:5], ﴿We will call the guards of Hell﴾ [96:18], and similar. They omitted the bā' from "al-haqq" because it is an adjective of the verbal noun, as if he judges the true judgment.

﴿Say: "If I had what you seek to hasten, within my power﴾, which is the punishment, ﴿the matter would have been decided between me and you﴾, that is, it would have been finished with the punishment and you would have been destroyed. ﴿And Allah is most knowing of the wrongdoers.﴾

﴿Say, "Have you considered: if Allah were to take away your hearing and your sight and seal over your hearts, what deity other than Allah could bring them back to you?"﴾ That is, they would not comprehend speech or see the proof. ﴿Who could bring it to you?﴾ That is, bring back what He took from you. ﴿Observe how We vary the signs﴾ (nubayyin lahum al-ayat), that is, We make the signs clear to them, ﴿yet they turn away﴾ (yasdifun), that is, they turn aside from them, denying them.

﴿Say: "Have you considered: if the punishment of Allah comes upon you suddenly (baghtatan), or openly (jahratan), with visible sight and witness, [for what you associated with Him], will anyone be destroyed except the wrongdoing people?"﴾ The wrongdoers are the polytheists.

﴿We send the messengers only as bearers of good news and warners. So whoever believes and does righteous deeds, there will be no fear for them﴾ when those in the Fire fear, ﴿nor will they grieve﴾ when they grieve. ﴿But those who deny Our signs﴾, meaning Muhammad and the Qur'an, ﴿the punishment will touch them﴾, that is, afflict them, ﴿for what they used to defiantly do﴾, that is, commit.

﴿Say: "I do not tell you that I have the treasures of Allah﴾, meaning the provision of Allah, ﴿nor do I know the unseen﴾, that is, what is hidden from people, ﴿nor do I tell you that I am an angel﴾, so that you would reject my words and deny my command. ﴿I only follow what is revealed to me.﴾" That is not disallowed nor impossible by reason, given the existence of the evidences and the conclusive proof.

﴿Say: "Are the blind and the seeing alike? Will you not reflect?"﴾ The disbelievers and the believers, the misguided and the guided, are not alike.

﴿And warn with it﴾, that is, with the Qur'an, ﴿those who fear that they will be gathered﴾, that is, raised and brought to life, ﴿to their Lord.﴾ Ad-Dahhak said: "with it" refers to Allah. Another view: ﴿those who know that they will be gathered, because their fear is due to what their deeds have been.﴾ ﴿They will have no protector besides Him﴾, meaning no close one who benefits them, ﴿nor any intercessor﴾ to intercede for them, ﴿so that they may fear Him.﴾

﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening…﴾ Sulayman and Khabbab ibn al-Aratt said: this verse was revealed concerning us.

Al-Aqra' ibn Habis al-Tamimi and Uyayna ibn Hisn al-Fazari, who were among those whose hearts were to be softened (al-mu'allafa qulubuhum), came and found the Prophet (ﷺ) sitting with Bilal, Suhayb, Ammar and Khabbab, along with some weak Muslims. When they saw them around him, they belittled them and came to him and said: "O Messenger of Allah, if you sat at the head of the gathering and these people were away, and removed their woolen tunics, which were the only garments they had, we would sit with you, converse with you and take from you." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I am not one to drive away the believers." They said: "Then we wish you would make for us a gathering of your own, by which the Arabs would recognize our superiority, for the delegations of the Arabs come to you, and we are ashamed that the Arabs should see us with these slaves. When we come to you, let them be removed, and when we finish, sit with them if you wish." He said: "Yes." They said: "Write us a document to that effect." So he called for a sheet and called Ali to write.

He said: "While we were sitting in a corner, Jibril (peace be upon him) came down with the words: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening…﴾ [6:52], unless by something [else]." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) threw the sheet from his hand, then called us. We came to him while he was saying: ﴿Peace be upon you. Your Lord has prescribed for Himself mercy﴾ [6:54]. We would sit with him, and when he wished to rise, he rose and left us. Then Allah revealed this verse: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord…﴾. He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would sit with us patiently and we would draw close to him until our knees almost touched his knees. When the hour came for him to rise, we rose and left him until he stood up. He said: "Praise be to Allah who did not take me until He commanded me to keep myself patient with a people from my community: [your life is with you and your death is with you]." [135]

Al-Kalbi said: They said to him: "Make a day for us and a day for them." He said: "I will not do that." They said: "Then make the gathering one and come to us, and turn your back to them." So Allah revealed this verse.

Al-Ash'ath ibn Sawwar narrated from Idris, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: The chiefs of Quraysh passed by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), along with Suhayb, Khabbab, Bilal, Ammar and others of the weak Muslims. They said: "O Muhammad, are you pleased with these from your people? Shall we be followers of these? Are these the ones on whom Allah has bestowed favor from among us? Drive them away from you; perhaps if you drive them away, we will follow you." So Allah revealed: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord…﴾. He said: Quraysh had said: "Were it not for Bilal and Ibn Umm Abd, we would follow Muhammad." So Allah revealed this verse.

Ikrimah said: Utba ibn Rabi'a, Shayba ibn Umayya, Mut'im ibn Adi, al-Harith ibn Nawfal, Qurza ibn Abd and Amr ibn Nawfal, among the nobles of Banu Abd Manaf from the people of disbelief, came to Abu Talib and said: "O Abu Talib, if your nephew Muhammad would drive away our clients and allies, for they are our slaves, it would be greater in our hearts, more obedient to him among us, and closer to our following him and affirming him." Abu Talib came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and told him what they had concealed. Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "If you did that, we would see what they want and where they will end up." Then this verse was revealed concerning their statement. When it was revealed, Umar ibn al-Khattab came and apologized for his statement.

Jubayr ibn Nufayl said: The Quraysh came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "You sent for us, so drive these scum away from you, and we will be your companions." So Allah revealed: ﴿And do not drive away…﴾.

Ibn Abbas said: ﴿those who call upon their Lord﴾ means those who worship their Lord with the obligatory prayer, ﴿morning and evening﴾ means the dawn prayer and the afternoon prayer. This was because some poor people were with the Prophet (ﷺ), and some of the nobles said: "When we pray, let these be delayed, and let them pray behind us." So Allah revealed: ﴿And do not drive away those who…﴾.

Hamza ibn Isa said: I entered upon al-Hasan and said: "O Abu Sa'id, what do you say about the words of Allah: ﴿And do not drive away those who believe﴾?" He said: "No, rather they are those who guard the prayers in congregation."

Mujahid said: I prayed the dawn prayer with Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab (may Allah be pleased with him). When the imam finished the salam, the people hurried to the storyteller (al-qass). Sa'id said: "How quickly the people rush to this gathering!"

Mujahid said: I said: "They interpret the words of Allah: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening﴾." He meant that this refers only to the prayer we have just left, and we said they remember their Lord.

Abu Ja'far said: meaning they recite the Qur'an.

﴿seeking His face﴾ is the answer to His words ﴿You are not accountable for them in anything﴾ [6:52]. His words ﴿so you would be among the wrongdoers﴾ are the answer to His words ﴿and do not drive away﴾; ﴿no one﴾ is the answer to a negation, and ﴿Allah﴾ is the answer to the prohibition. ﴿Among the wrongdoers﴾, meaning those who harm themselves through disobedience. Driving away is misplaced when it is not in its proper place.

﴿And thus We tested some of them by others﴾ [6:53]: the lowly and the customary ranking with respect to the master and the wealthy. ﴿So that they say: "Are these the ones on whom Allah has bestowed favor from among us?"﴾ That is, the nobles, the rich, say: "these," meaning the poor and weak, "on whom Allah has bestowed favor from among us." Al-Kalbi said: When a noble saw a lowly person had embraced Islam before him, he would be too proud to accept Islam and say: "This one has preceded me in Islam," so he would not accept it. ﴿Is not Allah most knowing of the grateful?﴾, meaning the believers. This is the answer to their words "are these the ones on whom Allah has bestowed favor from among us?" It was also said: "Is not Allah most knowing of the grateful, those who give thanks for Islam when He guides them to it?"

Al-Ala' ibn Bashir, from Abu Bakr al-Naji, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, said: I was in a group among which were poor emigrants, some of whom covered others from nakedness. A reciter was reciting to us while we listened to his recitation. The Prophet (ﷺ) came upon us until he stood over us. When the reciter saw him, he fell silent. He greeted and said: "What were you doing?" We said: "O Messenger of Allah, a reciter was reciting to us and we were listening to his recitation." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Praise be to Allah who has placed among my community those with whom I have been commanded to keep myself patient." Then he sat in the midst of us to level himself among us, then he said, gesturing with his hand like this, and the people formed a circle and their faces became visible. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not recognize any of them, and they were the poor emigrants. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Rejoice, destitute emigrants, in complete success on the Day of Resurrection: you will enter Paradise before the wealthy believers by half a day, which is equal to five hundred years." [136]

Hisham ibn Sulayman, from Abu Yazid al-Raqqashi, from Anas, said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "O assembly of the poor, Allah has been pleased that I should take pattern from your gatherings, and that Allah is with us," and He said: ﴿And keep yourself patient with those who call upon their Lord morning and evening﴾. For these are the gatherings of the prophets before you and of the righteous." [137]

Mu'awiya ibn Murra, from A'idh ibn Amr: Salman, Suhayb and Bilal were sitting when Abu Sufyan passed by them. They said to him: "The swords of Allah have not yet taken from the neck of the enemy of Allah what they should." Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) said to them: "You say this to the elder of Quraysh and its master?" Then he came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and he said: "O Abu Bakr, perhaps you have angered them; if you have angered them, you have angered your Lord." Abu Bakr fell upon them and said: "Perhaps I have angered you?" They said: "No, O Abu Bakr, may Allah forgive you." [An-Nasa'i]

﴿When those who believe in Our signs come to you…﴾: the scholars differed about the occasion of revelation of this verse.

Ikrimah said: It was revealed concerning those whom Allah prohibited His Prophet (ﷺ) from driving away. Whenever the Prophet (ﷺ) saw them, he would greet them first and say: "Praise be to Allah who has placed among my community those whom I was commanded to greet first with peace." [138]

Al-Kalbi said: When the verse ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord﴾ was revealed, Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) came to the Prophet (ﷺ), apologized to him for his statement and sought forgiveness of Allah for it, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I intended nothing by it but good." So ﴿When those who believe in Our signs come to you, say: "Peace be upon you…"﴾ was revealed concerning Umar (may Allah be pleased with him).

Ata' said: It was revealed concerning Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, Ali, Bilal, Salim, Abu Ubayda, Suhayb ibn Sinan, Umar, Ja'far, Uthman ibn Maz'un, Ammar ibn Yasir, al-Arqam ibn al-Arqam and Abu Salama ibn Abd al-Asad (may Allah be pleased with them all).

Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Men came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "We have committed many great sins." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) remained silent about them, so Allah revealed concerning these men: ﴿those who believe in Our signs, say: "Peace be upon you. Your Lord has prescribed for Himself mercy: whoever of you does evil in ignorance﴾.

Mujahid said: [ignorance] means he does not know the lawful from the unlawful; and "from his ignorance" means your Lord's command, and everyone who commits a sin does so in ignorance. It was also said: ignorant of what that sin brings upon him. It is said: he became ignorant when he preferred disobedience over obedience. ﴿then repents after it and makes amends﴾, meaning he turns back from his error and sets his deed right. It was also said: he makes his repentance sincere. ﴿indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ The reciters differed on the reading of ﴿annahu﴾. The Kufans [read it with a fatha on the alif in both places]. Ibn Kathir, al-A'mash, Ibn Umar, Hamza and al-Kisa'i read it as a fresh sentence (isti'naf) [with fatha in one place and kasra in the other]. Al-Hasan, Asim and Ya'qub read it in the accusative as a substitute for "mercy". The people of Medina read the first with a fatha, on the sense of "and He prescribed that he…", and read the second with a kasra as a fresh sentence, because what follows it is never reported. ﴿And thus﴾, that is, in this manner. It was also said: its meaning is "and We have explained to you in this surah and this verse."

And it came in the highest of what is explained concerning the deniers: ﴿Thus We detail the signs﴾, that is, We distinguish and make clear to you Our proof and Our evidences concerning everyone who denies, the people of falsehood. ﴿And that the way of the criminals may become evident﴾: the verb is raised, and its meaning is "that the path of the criminals may become manifest and clear." It is said: "the thing became clear (bana), made clear (abana), became clear in its explanation (tibyan) and became distinct (tabayyana) when it became apparent and plain." The word "sabil" (way) is masculine and feminine: Tamim treat it as masculine, while the people of the Hijaz treat it as feminine. The evidence for the masculine is His words: ﴿And if they see the way of right guidance, they will not adopt it as a way; but if they see the way of error, they will adopt it as a way﴾ [7:146]. The evidence for the feminine is His words: ﴿Why do you bar from the way of Allah those who believe, seeking to make it crooked?﴾ [7:86], and His words: ﴿Say, "This is my way; I invite to Allah with insight"﴾ [12:108]. Therefore one reading is "wa-litastabina" with the yā' and another with the tā', and the people of Medina read "wa-litastabina" with the tā' and "sabīla" in the accusative, addressing the Prophet (ﷺ): "and that you, O Muhammad, may learn the way of the criminals." It is said: "istabana al-shay'" and "tabayyanahu" when one knows it.

﴿Say: "Indeed I have been forbidden to worship those whom you invoke besides Allah."﴾ ﴿Say: "I will not follow your desires"﴾ in worshipping idols, and in driving away Bilal and Salman. ﴿Then I would have gone astray and would not be among the guided.﴾ That is, if I did that, I would have abandoned the path of truth and taken a way other than guidance.

Yahya ibn Wathhab [and Abu Raja'] read "qad dalilt" with a kasra on the lam. The two are dialects: "dalla yadullu" like "qalla yaqullu," and "dalla yadillu" like "malla yamillu." The first is more sound and more eloquent, because it is the dialect of the people of the Hijaz.

﴿Say: "Indeed I am upon clear evidence from my Lord"﴾: clarity, proof, insight and argument. ﴿and you have denied Him.﴾ That is, denied my Lord. ﴿What you seek to hasten is not with me﴾, meaning the punishment. It was revealed concerning al-Nadr ibn al-Harith. ﴿The decision is only Allah's; He relates the truth﴾. The people of the Hijaz and Asim read "yaqussu al-haqqa" with a doubled sad, meaning "He says the truth." They argued that it is written without a yā' in all the codices, and because it says "al-haqq," so one says "I judged by the truth." The rest read it with a dad, meaning "He decides by the truth," as evidenced by His words: ﴿And He is the best of deciders﴾ [7:87]. Al-fasl is the bringing of judgment. The reciters omitted the yā' for ease of pronunciation, then [...], as in His words ﴿burning of the Hellfire﴾ [37:163], ﴿Allah erases what He wills﴾ [13:39], ﴿Warnings will not avail﴾ [54:5], ﴿We will call the guards of Hell﴾ [96:18], and similar. They omitted the bā' from "al-haqq" because it is an adjective of the verbal noun, as if he judges the true judgment.

﴿Say: "If I had what you seek to hasten, within my power﴾, which is the punishment, ﴿the matter would have been decided between me and you﴾, that is, it would have been finished with the punishment and you would have been destroyed. ﴿And Allah is most knowing of the wrongdoers.﴾

﴿Say, "Have you considered: if Allah were to take away your hearing and your sight and seal over your hearts, what deity other than Allah could bring them back to you?"﴾ That is, they would not comprehend speech or see the proof. ﴿Who could bring it to you?﴾ That is, bring back what He took from you. ﴿Observe how We vary the signs﴾ (nubayyin lahum al-ayat), that is, We make the signs clear to them, ﴿yet they turn away﴾ (yasdifun), that is, they turn aside from them, denying them.

﴿Say: "Have you considered: if the punishment of Allah comes upon you suddenly (baghtatan), or openly (jahratan), with visible sight and witness, [for what you associated with Him], will anyone be destroyed except the wrongdoing people?"﴾ The wrongdoers are the polytheists.

﴿We send the messengers only as bearers of good news and warners. So whoever believes and does righteous deeds, there will be no fear for them﴾ when those in the Fire fear, ﴿nor will they grieve﴾ when they grieve. ﴿But those who deny Our signs﴾, meaning Muhammad and the Qur'an, ﴿the punishment will touch them﴾, that is, afflict them, ﴿for what they used to defiantly do﴾, that is, commit.

﴿Say: "I do not tell you that I have the treasures of Allah﴾, meaning the provision of Allah, ﴿nor do I know the unseen﴾, that is, what is hidden from people, ﴿nor do I tell you that I am an angel﴾, so that you would reject my words and deny my command. ﴿I only follow what is revealed to me.﴾" That is not disallowed nor impossible by reason, given the existence of the evidences and the conclusive proof.

﴿Say: "Are the blind and the seeing alike? Will you not reflect?"﴾ The disbelievers and the believers, the misguided and the guided, are not alike.

﴿And warn with it﴾, that is, with the Qur'an, ﴿those who fear that they will be gathered﴾, that is, raised and brought to life, ﴿to their Lord.﴾ Ad-Dahhak said: "with it" refers to Allah. Another view: ﴿those who know that they will be gathered, because their fear is due to what their deeds have been.﴾ ﴿They will have no protector besides Him﴾, meaning no close one who benefits them, ﴿nor any intercessor﴾ to intercede for them, ﴿so that they may fear Him.﴾

﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening…﴾ Sulayman and Khabbab ibn al-Aratt said: this verse was revealed concerning us.

Al-Aqra' ibn Habis al-Tamimi and Uyayna ibn Hisn al-Fazari, who were among those whose hearts were to be softened (al-mu'allafa qulubuhum), came and found the Prophet (ﷺ) sitting with Bilal, Suhayb, Ammar and Khabbab, along with some weak Muslims. When they saw them around him, they belittled them and came to him and said: "O Messenger of Allah, if you sat at the head of the gathering and these people were away, and removed their woolen tunics, which were the only garments they had, we would sit with you, converse with you and take from you." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I am not one to drive away the believers." They said: "Then we wish you would make for us a gathering of your own, by which the Arabs would recognize our superiority, for the delegations of the Arabs come to you, and we are ashamed that the Arabs should see us with these slaves. When we come to you, let them be removed, and when we finish, sit with them if you wish." He said: "Yes." They said: "Write us a document to that effect." So he called for a sheet and called Ali to write.

He said: "While we were sitting in a corner, Jibril (peace be upon him) came down with the words: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening…﴾ [6:52], unless by something [else]." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) threw the sheet from his hand, then called us. We came to him while he was saying: ﴿Peace be upon you. Your Lord has prescribed for Himself mercy﴾ [6:54].
