We would sit with him, and when he wished to rise, he rose and left us. Then Allah revealed this verse: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord…﴾. He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would sit with us patiently and we would draw close to him until our knees almost touched his knees. When the hour came for him to rise, we rose and left him until he stood up. He said: "Praise be to Allah who did not take me until He commanded me to keep myself patient with a people from my community: [your life is with you and your death is with you]." [135]

Al-Kalbi said: They said to him: "Make a day for us and a day for them." He said: "I will not do that." They said: "Then make the gathering one and come to us, and turn your back to them." So Allah revealed this verse.

Al-Ash'ath ibn Sawwar narrated from Idris, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: The chiefs of Quraysh passed by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), along with Suhayb, Khabbab, Bilal, Ammar and others of the weak Muslims. They said: "O Muhammad, are you pleased with these from your people? Shall we be followers of these? Are these the ones on whom Allah has bestowed favor from among us? Drive them away from you; perhaps if you drive them away, we will follow you." So Allah revealed: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord…﴾. He said: Quraysh had said: "Were it not for Bilal and Ibn Umm Abd, we would follow Muhammad." So Allah revealed this verse.

Ikrimah said: Utba ibn Rabi'a, Shayba ibn Umayya, Mut'im ibn Adi, al-Harith ibn Nawfal, Qurza ibn Abd and Amr ibn Nawfal, among the nobles of Banu Abd Manaf from the people of disbelief, came to Abu Talib and said: "O Abu Talib, if your nephew Muhammad would drive away our clients and allies, for they are our slaves, it would be greater in our hearts, more obedient to him among us, and closer to our following him and affirming him." Abu Talib came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and told him what they had concealed. Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "If you did that, we would see what they want and where they will end up." Then this verse was revealed concerning their statement. When it was revealed, Umar ibn al-Khattab came and apologized for his statement.

Jubayr ibn Nufayl said: The Quraysh came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "You sent for us, so drive these scum away from you, and we will be your companions." So Allah revealed: ﴿And do not drive away…﴾.

Ibn Abbas said: ﴿those who call upon their Lord﴾ means those who worship their Lord with the obligatory prayer, ﴿morning and evening﴾ means the dawn prayer and the afternoon prayer. This was because some poor people were with the Prophet (ﷺ), and some of the nobles said: "When we pray, let these be delayed, and let them pray behind us." So Allah revealed: ﴿And do not drive away those who…﴾.

Hamza ibn Isa said: I entered upon al-Hasan and said: "O Abu Sa'id, what do you say about the words of Allah: ﴿And do not drive away those who believe﴾?" He said: "No, rather they are those who guard the prayers in congregation."

Mujahid said: I prayed the dawn prayer with Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab (may Allah be pleased with him). When the imam finished the salam, the people hurried to the storyteller (al-qass). Sa'id said: "How quickly the people rush to this gathering!"

Mujahid said: I said: "They interpret the words of Allah: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening﴾." He meant that this refers only to the prayer we have just left, and we said they remember their Lord.

Abu Ja'far said: meaning they recite the Qur'an.

﴿seeking His face﴾ is the answer to His words ﴿You are not accountable for them in anything﴾ [6:52]. His words ﴿so you would be among the wrongdoers﴾ are the answer to His words ﴿and do not drive away﴾; ﴿no one﴾ is the answer to a negation, and ﴿Allah﴾ is the answer to the prohibition. ﴿Among the wrongdoers﴾, meaning those who harm themselves through disobedience. Driving away is misplaced when it is not in its proper place.

﴿And thus We tested some of them by others﴾ [6:53]: the lowly and the customary ranking with respect to the master and the wealthy. ﴿So that they say: "Are these the ones on whom Allah has bestowed favor from among us?"﴾ That is, the nobles, the rich, say: "these," meaning the poor and weak, "on whom Allah has bestowed favor from among us." Al-Kalbi said: When a noble saw a lowly person had embraced Islam before him, he would be too proud to accept Islam and say: "This one has preceded me in Islam," so he would not accept it. ﴿Is not Allah most knowing of the grateful?﴾, meaning the believers. This is the answer to their words "are these the ones on whom Allah has bestowed favor from among us?" It was also said: "Is not Allah most knowing of the grateful, those who give thanks for Islam when He guides them to it?"

Al-Ala' ibn Bashir, from Abu Bakr al-Naji, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, said: I was in a group among which were poor emigrants, some of whom covered others from nakedness. A reciter was reciting to us while we listened to his recitation. The Prophet (ﷺ) came upon us until he stood over us. When the reciter saw him, he fell silent. He greeted and said: "What were you doing?" We said: "O Messenger of Allah, a reciter was reciting to us and we were listening to his recitation." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Praise be to Allah who has placed among my community those with whom I have been commanded to keep myself patient." Then he sat in the midst of us to level himself among us, then he said, gesturing with his hand like this, and the people formed a circle and their faces became visible. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not recognize any of them, and they were the poor emigrants. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Rejoice, destitute emigrants, in complete success on the Day of Resurrection: you will enter Paradise before the wealthy believers by half a day, which is equal to five hundred years." [136]

Hisham ibn Sulayman, from Abu Yazid al-Raqqashi, from Anas, said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "O assembly of the poor, Allah has been pleased that I should take pattern from your gatherings, and that Allah is with us," and He said: ﴿And keep yourself patient with those who call upon their Lord morning and evening﴾. For these are the gatherings of the prophets before you and of the righteous." [137]

Mu'awiya ibn Murra, from A'idh ibn Amr: Salman, Suhayb and Bilal were sitting when Abu Sufyan passed by them. They said to him: "The swords of Allah have not yet taken from the neck of the enemy of Allah what they should." Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) said to them: "You say this to the elder of Quraysh and its master?" Then he came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and he said: "O Abu Bakr, perhaps you have angered them; if you have angered them, you have angered your Lord." Abu Bakr fell upon them and said: "Perhaps I have angered you?" They said: "No, O Abu Bakr, may Allah forgive you." [An-Nasa'i]

﴿When those who believe in Our signs come to you…﴾: the scholars differed about the occasion of revelation of this verse.

Ikrimah said: It was revealed concerning those whom Allah prohibited His Prophet (ﷺ) from driving away. Whenever the Prophet (ﷺ) saw them, he would greet them first and say: "Praise be to Allah who has placed among my community those whom I was commanded to greet first with peace." [138]

Al-Kalbi said: When the verse ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord﴾ was revealed, Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) came to the Prophet (ﷺ), apologized to him for his statement and sought forgiveness of Allah for it, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I intended nothing by it but good." So ﴿When those who believe in Our signs come to you, say: "Peace be upon you…"﴾ was revealed concerning Umar (may Allah be pleased with him).

Ata' said: It was revealed concerning Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, Ali, Bilal, Salim, Abu Ubayda, Suhayb ibn Sinan, Umar, Ja'far, Uthman ibn Maz'un, Ammar ibn Yasir, al-Arqam ibn al-Arqam and Abu Salama ibn Abd al-Asad (may Allah be pleased with them all).

Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Men came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "We have committed many great sins." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) remained silent about them, so Allah revealed concerning these men: ﴿those who believe in Our signs, say: "Peace be upon you. Your Lord has prescribed for Himself mercy: whoever of you does evil in ignorance﴾.

Mujahid said: [ignorance] means he does not know the lawful from the unlawful; and "from his ignorance" means your Lord's command, and everyone who commits a sin does so in ignorance. It was also said: ignorant of what that sin brings upon him. It is said: he became ignorant when he preferred disobedience over obedience. ﴿then repents after it and makes amends﴾, meaning he turns back from his error and sets his deed right. It was also said: he makes his repentance sincere. ﴿indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ The reciters differed on the reading of ﴿annahu﴾. The Kufans [read it with a fatha on the alif in both places]. Ibn Kathir, al-A'mash, Ibn Umar, Hamza and al-Kisa'i read it as a fresh sentence (isti'naf) [with fatha in one place and kasra in the other]. Al-Hasan, Asim and Ya'qub read it in the accusative as a substitute for "mercy". The people of Medina read the first with a fatha, on the sense of "and He prescribed that he…", and read the second with a kasra as a fresh sentence, because what follows it is never reported. ﴿And thus﴾, that is, in this manner. It was also said: its meaning is "and We have explained to you in this surah and this verse."

And it came in the highest of what is explained concerning the deniers: ﴿Thus We detail the signs﴾, that is, We distinguish and make clear to you Our proof and Our evidences concerning everyone who denies, the people of falsehood. ﴿And that the way of the criminals may become evident﴾: the verb is raised, and its meaning is "that the path of the criminals may become manifest and clear." It is said: "the thing became clear (bana), made clear (abana), became clear in its explanation (tibyan) and became distinct (tabayyana) when it became apparent and plain." The evidence for the masculine is His words: ﴿And if they see the way of right guidance, they will not adopt it as a way; but if they see the way of error, they will adopt it as a way﴾ [7:146]. The evidence for the feminine is His words: ﴿Why do you bar from the way of Allah those who believe, seeking to make it crooked?﴾ [7:86], and His words: ﴿Say, "This is my way; I invite to Allah with insight"﴾ [12:108]. ﴿Say: "Indeed I am upon clear evidence from my Lord"﴾: clarity, proof, insight and argument. ﴿and you have denied Him.﴾ That is, denied my Lord. ﴿What you seek to hasten is not with me﴾, meaning the punishment. It was revealed concerning al-Nadr ibn al-Harith. ﴿The decision is only Allah's; He relates the truth﴾. The people of the Hijaz and Asim read "yaqussu al-haqqa" with a doubled sad, meaning "He says the truth." They argued that it is written without a yā' in all the codices, and because it says "al-haqq," so one says "I judged by the truth." The rest read it with a dad, meaning "He decides by the truth," as evidenced by His words: ﴿And He is the best of deciders﴾ [7:87]. Al-fasl is the bringing of judgment. The reciters omitted the yā' for ease of pronunciation, then [...], as in His words ﴿burning of the Hellfire﴾ [37:163], ﴿Allah erases what He wills﴾ [13:39], ﴿Warnings will not avail﴾ [54:5], ﴿We will call the guards of Hell﴾ [96:18], and similar. They omitted the bā' from "al-haqq" because it is an adjective of the verbal noun, as if he judges the true judgment.

﴿Say: "If I had what you seek to hasten, within my power﴾, which is the punishment, ﴿the matter would have been decided between me and you﴾, that is, it would have been finished with the punishment and you would have been destroyed. ﴿And Allah is most knowing of the wrongdoers.﴾

﴿Say, "Have you considered: if Allah were to take away your hearing and your sight and seal over your hearts, what deity other than Allah could bring them back to you?"﴾ That is, they would not comprehend speech or see the proof. ﴿Who could bring it to you?﴾ That is, bring back what He took from you. ﴿Observe how We vary the signs﴾ (nubayyin lahum al-ayat), that is, We make the signs clear to them, ﴿yet they turn away﴾ (yasdifun), that is, they turn aside from them, denying them.

﴿Say: "Have you considered: if the punishment of Allah comes upon you suddenly (baghtatan), or openly (jahratan), with visible sight and witness, [for what you associated with Him], will anyone be destroyed except the wrongdoing people?"﴾ The wrongdoers are the polytheists.

﴿We send the messengers only as bearers of good news and warners. So whoever believes and does righteous deeds, there will be no fear for them﴾ when those in the Fire fear, ﴿nor will they grieve﴾ when they grieve. ﴿But those who deny Our signs﴾, meaning Muhammad and the Qur'an, ﴿the punishment will touch them﴾, that is, afflict them, ﴿for what they used to defiantly do﴾, that is, commit.

﴿Say: "I do not tell you that I have the treasures of Allah﴾, meaning the provision of Allah, ﴿nor do I know the unseen﴾, that is, what is hidden from people, ﴿nor do I tell you that I am an angel﴾, so that you would reject my words and deny my command. ﴿I only follow what is revealed to me.﴾" That is not disallowed nor impossible by reason, given the existence of the evidences and the conclusive proof.

﴿Say: "Are the blind and the seeing alike? Will you not reflect?"﴾ The disbelievers and the believers, the misguided and the guided, are not alike.

﴿And warn with it﴾, that is, with the Qur'an, ﴿those who fear that they will be gathered﴾, that is, raised and brought to life, ﴿to their Lord.﴾ Ad-Dahhak said: "with it" refers to Allah. Another view: ﴿those who know that they will be gathered, because their fear is due to what their deeds have been.﴾ ﴿They will have no protector besides Him﴾, meaning no close one who benefits them, ﴿nor any intercessor﴾ to intercede for them, ﴿so that they may fear Him.﴾

﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening…﴾ Sulayman and Khabbab ibn al-Aratt said: this verse was revealed concerning us.

Al-Aqra' ibn Habis al-Tamimi and Uyayna ibn Hisn al-Fazari, who were among those whose hearts were to be softened (al-mu'allafa qulubuhum), came and found the Prophet (ﷺ) sitting with Bilal, Suhayb, Ammar and Khabbab, along with some weak Muslims. When they saw them around him, they belittled them and came to him and said: "O Messenger of Allah, if you sat at the head of the gathering and these people were away, and removed their woolen tunics, which were the only garments they had, we would sit with you, converse with you and take from you." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I am not one to drive away the believers." They said: "Then we wish you would make for us a gathering of your own, by which the Arabs would recognize our superiority, for the delegations of the Arabs come to you, and we are ashamed that the Arabs should see us with these slaves. When we come to you, let them be removed, and when we finish, sit with them if you wish." He said: "Yes." They said: "Write us a document to that effect." So he called for a sheet and called Ali to write.

He said: "While we were sitting in a corner, Jibril (peace be upon him) came down with the words: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening…﴾ [6:52], unless by something [else]." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) threw the sheet from his hand, then called us. We came to him while he was saying: ﴿Peace be upon you. Your Lord has prescribed for Himself mercy﴾ [6:54]. We would sit with him, and when he wished to rise, he rose and left us. Then Allah revealed this verse: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord…﴾. He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would sit with us patiently and we would draw close to him until our knees almost touched his knees. When the hour came for him to rise, we rose and left him until he stood up. He said: "Praise be to Allah who did not take me until He commanded me to keep myself patient with a people from my community: [your life is with you and your death is with you]." [135]

Al-Kalbi said: They said to him: "Make a day for us and a day for them." He said: "I will not do that." They said: "Then make the gathering one and come to us, and turn your back to them." So Allah revealed this verse.

Al-Ash'ath ibn Sawwar narrated from Idris, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: The chiefs of Quraysh passed by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), along with Suhayb, Khabbab, Bilal, Ammar and others of the weak Muslims. They said: "O Muhammad, are you pleased with these from your people? Shall we be followers of these? Are these the ones on whom Allah has bestowed favor from among us? Drive them away from you; perhaps if you drive them away, we will follow you." So Allah revealed: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord…﴾. He said: Quraysh had said: "Were it not for Bilal and Ibn Umm Abd, we would follow Muhammad." So Allah revealed this verse.

Ikrimah said: Utba ibn Rabi'a, Shayba ibn Umayya, Mut'im ibn Adi, al-Harith ibn Nawfal, Qurza ibn Abd and Amr ibn Nawfal, among the nobles of Banu Abd Manaf from the people of disbelief, came to Abu Talib and said: "O Abu Talib, if your nephew Muhammad would drive away our clients and allies, for they are our slaves, it would be greater in our hearts, more obedient to him among us, and closer to our following him and affirming him." Abu Talib came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and told him what they had concealed. Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "If you did that, we would see what they want and where they will end up." Then this verse was revealed concerning their statement. When it was revealed, Umar ibn al-Khattab came and apologized for his statement.

Jubayr ibn Nufayl said: The Quraysh came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "You sent for us, so drive these scum away from you, and we will be your companions." So Allah revealed: ﴿And do not drive away…﴾.

Ibn Abbas said: ﴿those who call upon their Lord﴾ means those who worship their Lord with the obligatory prayer, ﴿morning and evening﴾ means the dawn prayer and the afternoon prayer. This was because some poor people were with the Prophet (ﷺ), and some of the nobles said: "When we pray, let these be delayed, and let them pray behind us." So Allah revealed: ﴿And do not drive away those who…﴾.

Hamza ibn Isa said: I entered upon al-Hasan and said: "O Abu Sa'id, what do you say about the words of Allah: ﴿And do not drive away those who believe﴾?" He said: "No, rather they are those who guard the prayers in congregation."

Mujahid said: I prayed the dawn prayer with Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab (may Allah be pleased with him). When the imam finished the salam, the people hurried to the storyteller (al-qass). Sa'id said: "How quickly the people rush to this gathering!"

Mujahid said: I said: "They interpret the words of Allah: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening﴾." He meant that this refers only to the prayer we have just left, and we said they remember their Lord.

Abu Ja'far said: meaning they recite the Qur'an.

﴿seeking His face﴾ is the answer to His words ﴿You are not accountable for them in anything﴾ [6:52]. His words ﴿so you would be among the wrongdoers﴾ are the answer to His words ﴿and do not drive away﴾; ﴿no one﴾ is the answer to a negation, and ﴿Allah﴾ is the answer to the prohibition. ﴿Among the wrongdoers﴾, meaning those who harm themselves through disobedience. Driving away is misplaced when it is not in its proper place.

﴿And thus We tested some of them by others﴾ [6:53]: the lowly and the customary ranking with respect to the master and the wealthy. ﴿So that they say: "Are these the ones on whom Allah has bestowed favor from among us?"﴾ That is, the nobles, the rich, say: "these," meaning the poor and weak, "on whom Allah has bestowed favor from among us." Al-Kalbi said: When a noble saw a lowly person had embraced Islam before him, he would be too proud to accept Islam and say: "This one has preceded me in Islam," so he would not accept it. ﴿Is not Allah most knowing of the grateful?﴾, meaning the believers. This is the answer to their words "are these the ones on whom Allah has bestowed favor from among us?" It was also said: "Is not Allah most knowing of the grateful, those who give thanks for Islam when He guides them to it?"

Al-Ala' ibn Bashir, from Abu Bakr al-Naji, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, said: I was in a group among which were poor emigrants, some of whom covered others from nakedness. A reciter was reciting to us while we listened to his recitation. The Prophet (ﷺ) came upon us until he stood over us. When the reciter saw him, he fell silent. He greeted and said: "What were you doing?" We said: "O Messenger of Allah, a reciter was reciting to us and we were listening to his recitation." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Praise be to Allah who has placed among my community those with whom I have been commanded to keep myself patient." Then he sat in the midst of us to level himself among us, then he said, gesturing with his hand like this, and the people formed a circle and their faces became visible. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not recognize any of them, and they were the poor emigrants. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Rejoice, destitute emigrants, in complete success on the Day of Resurrection: you will enter Paradise before the wealthy believers by half a day, which is equal to five hundred years." [136]

Hisham ibn Sulayman, from Abu Yazid al-Raqqashi, from Anas, said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "O assembly of the poor, Allah has been pleased that I should take pattern from your gatherings, and that Allah is with us," and He said: ﴿And keep yourself patient with those who call upon their Lord morning and evening﴾. For these are the gatherings of the prophets before you and of the righteous." [137]

Mu'awiya ibn Murra, from A'idh ibn Amr: Salman, Suhayb and Bilal were sitting when Abu Sufyan passed by them. They said to him: "The swords of Allah have not yet taken from the neck of the enemy of Allah what they should." Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) said to them: "You say this to the elder of Quraysh and its master?" Then he came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and he said: "O Abu Bakr, perhaps you have angered them; if you have angered them, you have angered your Lord." Abu Bakr fell upon them and said: "Perhaps I have angered you?" They said: "No, O Abu Bakr, may Allah forgive you." [An-Nasa'i]

﴿When those who believe in Our signs come to you…﴾: the scholars differed about the occasion of revelation of this verse.

Ikrimah said: It was revealed concerning those whom Allah prohibited His Prophet (ﷺ) from driving away. Whenever the Prophet (ﷺ) saw them, he would greet them first and say: "Praise be to Allah who has placed among my community those whom I was commanded to greet first with peace." [138]

Al-Kalbi said: When the verse ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord﴾ was revealed, Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) came to the Prophet (ﷺ), apologized to him for his statement and sought forgiveness of Allah for it, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I intended nothing by it but good." So ﴿When those who believe in Our signs come to you, say: "Peace be upon you…"﴾ was revealed concerning Umar (may Allah be pleased with him).

Ata' said: It was revealed concerning Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, Ali, Bilal, Salim, Abu Ubayda, Suhayb ibn Sinan, Umar, Ja'far, Uthman ibn Maz'un, Ammar ibn Yasir, al-Arqam ibn al-Arqam and Abu Salama ibn Abd al-Asad (may Allah be pleased with them all).

Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Men came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "We have committed many great sins." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) remained silent about them, so Allah revealed concerning these men: ﴿those who believe in Our signs, say: "Peace be upon you. Your Lord has prescribed for Himself mercy: whoever of you does evil in ignorance﴾.

Mujahid said: [ignorance] means he does not know the lawful from the unlawful; and "from his ignorance" means your Lord's command, and everyone who commits a sin does so in ignorance. It was also said: ignorant of what that sin brings upon him. It is said: he became ignorant when he preferred disobedience over obedience. ﴿then repents after it and makes amends﴾, meaning he turns back from his error and sets his deed right. It was also said: he makes his repentance sincere. ﴿indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ The reciters differed on the reading of ﴿annahu﴾. The Kufans [read it with a fatha on the alif in both places]. Ibn Kathir, al-A'mash, Ibn Umar, Hamza and al-Kisa'i read it as a fresh sentence (isti'naf) [with fatha in one place and kasra in the other]. Al-Hasan, Asim and Ya'qub read it in the accusative as a substitute for "mercy". The people of Medina read the first with a fatha, on the sense of "and He prescribed that he…", and read the second with a kasra as a fresh sentence, because what follows it is never reported. ﴿And thus﴾, that is, in this manner. It was also said: its meaning is "and We have explained to you in this surah and this verse."

And it came in the highest of what is explained concerning the deniers: ﴿Thus We detail the signs﴾, that is, We distinguish and make clear to you Our proof and Our evidences concerning everyone who denies, the people of falsehood. ﴿And that the way of the criminals may become evident﴾: the verb is raised, and its meaning is "that the path of the criminals may become manifest and clear." It is said: "the thing became clear (bana), made clear (abana), became clear in its explanation (tibyan) and became distinct (tabayyana) when it became apparent and plain." The word "sabil" (way) is masculine and feminine: Tamim treat it as masculine, while the people of the Hijaz treat it as feminine. The evidence for the masculine is His words: ﴿And if they see the way of right guidance, they will not adopt it as a way; but if they see the way of error, they will adopt it as a way﴾ [7:146]. The evidence for the feminine is His words: ﴿Why do you bar from the way of Allah those who believe, seeking to make it crooked?﴾ [7:86], and His words: ﴿Say, "This is my way; I invite to Allah with insight"﴾ [12:108]. Therefore one reading is "wa-litastabina" with the yā' and another with the tā', and the people of Medina read "wa-litastabina" with the tā' and "sabīla" in the accusative, addressing the Prophet (ﷺ): "and that you, O Muhammad, may learn the way of the criminals." It is said: "istabana al-shay'" and "tabayyanahu" when one knows it.

﴿Say: "Indeed I have been forbidden to worship those whom you invoke besides Allah."﴾ ﴿Say: "I will not follow your desires"﴾ in worshipping idols, and in driving away Bilal and Salman. ﴿Then I would have gone astray and would not be among the guided.﴾ That is, if I did that, I would have abandoned the path of truth and taken a way other than guidance.

Yahya ibn Wathhab [and Abu Raja'] read "qad dalilt" with a kasra on the lam. The two are dialects: "dalla yadullu" like "qalla yaqullu," and "dalla yadillu" like "malla yamillu." The first is more sound and more eloquent, because it is the dialect of the people of the Hijaz.

﴿Say: "Indeed I am upon clear evidence from my Lord"﴾: clarity, proof, insight and argument. ﴿and you have denied Him.﴾ That is, denied my Lord. ﴿What you seek to hasten is not with me﴾, meaning the punishment. It was revealed concerning al-Nadr ibn al-Harith. ﴿The decision is only Allah's; He relates the truth﴾. The people of the Hijaz and Asim read "yaqussu al-haqqa" with a doubled sad, meaning "He says the truth." They argued that it is written without a yā' in all the codices, and because it says "al-haqq," so one says "I judged by the truth." The rest read it with a dad, meaning "He decides by the truth," as evidenced by His words: ﴿And He is the best of deciders﴾ [7:87]. Al-fasl is the bringing of judgment. The reciters omitted the yā' for ease of pronunciation, then [...], as in His words ﴿burning of the Hellfire﴾ [37:163], ﴿Allah erases what He wills﴾ [13:39], ﴿Warnings will not avail﴾ [54:5], ﴿We will call the guards of Hell﴾ [96:18], and similar. They omitted the bā' from "al-haqq" because it is an adjective of the verbal noun, as if he judges the true judgment.

﴿Say: "If I had what you seek to hasten, within my power﴾, which is the punishment, ﴿the matter would have been decided between me and you﴾, that is, it would have been finished with the punishment and you would have been destroyed. ﴿And Allah is most knowing of the wrongdoers.﴾

﴿Say, "Have you considered: if Allah were to take away your hearing and your sight and seal over your hearts, what deity other than Allah could bring them back to you?"﴾ That is, they would not comprehend speech or see the proof. ﴿Who could bring it to you?﴾ That is, bring back what He took from you. ﴿Observe how We vary the signs﴾ (nubayyin lahum al-ayat), that is, We make the signs clear to them, ﴿yet they turn away﴾ (yasdifun), that is, they turn aside from them, denying them.

﴿Say: "Have you considered: if the punishment of Allah comes upon you suddenly (baghtatan), or openly (jahratan), with visible sight and witness, [for what you associated with Him], will anyone be destroyed except the wrongdoing people?"﴾ The wrongdoers are the polytheists.

﴿We send the messengers only as bearers of good news and warners. So whoever believes and does righteous deeds, there will be no fear for them﴾ when those in the Fire fear, ﴿nor will they grieve﴾ when they grieve. ﴿But those who deny Our signs﴾, meaning Muhammad and the Qur'an, ﴿the punishment will touch them﴾, that is, afflict them, ﴿for what they used to defiantly do﴾, that is, commit.

﴿Say: "I do not tell you that I have the treasures of Allah﴾, meaning the provision of Allah, ﴿nor do I know the unseen﴾, that is, what is hidden from people, ﴿nor do I tell you that I am an angel﴾, so that you would reject my words and deny my command. ﴿I only follow what is revealed to me.﴾" That is not disallowed nor impossible by reason, given the existence of the evidences and the conclusive proof.

﴿Say: "Are the blind and the seeing alike? Will you not reflect?"﴾ The disbelievers and the believers, the misguided and the guided, are not alike.

﴿And warn with it﴾, that is, with the Qur'an, ﴿those who fear that they will be gathered﴾, that is, raised and brought to life, ﴿to their Lord.﴾ Ad-Dahhak said: "with it" refers to Allah. Another view: ﴿those who know that they will be gathered, because their fear is due to what their deeds have been.﴾ ﴿They will have no protector besides Him﴾, meaning no close one who benefits them, ﴿nor any intercessor﴾ to intercede for them, ﴿so that they may fear Him.﴾

﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening…﴾ Sulayman and Khabbab ibn al-Aratt said: this verse was revealed concerning us.

Al-Aqra' ibn Habis al-Tamimi and Uyayna ibn Hisn al-Fazari, who were among those whose hearts were to be softened (al-mu'allafa qulubuhum), came and found the Prophet (ﷺ) sitting with Bilal, Suhayb, Ammar and Khabbab, along with some weak Muslims. When they saw them around him, they belittled them and came to him and said: "O Messenger of Allah, if you sat at the head of the gathering and these people were away, and removed their woolen tunics, which were the only garments they had, we would sit with you, converse with you and take from you." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I am not one to drive away the believers." They said: "Then we wish you would make for us a gathering of your own, by which the Arabs would recognize our superiority, for the delegations of the Arabs come to you, and we are ashamed that the Arabs should see us with these slaves. When we come to you, let them be removed, and when we finish, sit with them if you wish." He said: "Yes." They said: "Write us a document to that effect." So he called for a sheet and called Ali to write.

He said: "While we were sitting in a corner, Jibril (peace be upon him) came down with the words: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening…﴾ [6:52], unless by something [else]." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) threw the sheet from his hand, then called us. We came to him while he was saying: ﴿Peace be upon you. Your Lord has prescribed for Himself mercy﴾ [6:54]. We would sit with him, and when he wished to rise, he rose and left us. Then Allah revealed this verse: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord…﴾. He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would sit with us patiently and we would draw close to him until our knees almost touched his knees. When the hour came for him to rise, we rose and left him until he stood up. He said: "Praise be to Allah who did not take me until He commanded me to keep myself patient with a people from my community: [your life is with you and your death is with you]." [135]

Al-Kalbi said: They said to him: "Make a day for us and a day for them." He said: "I will not do that." They said: "Then make the gathering one and come to us, and turn your back to them." So Allah revealed this verse.

Al-Ash'ath ibn Sawwar narrated from Idris, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: The chiefs of Quraysh passed by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), along with Suhayb, Khabbab, Bilal, Ammar and others of the weak Muslims. They said: "O Muhammad, are you pleased with these from your people? Shall we be followers of these? Are these the ones on whom Allah has bestowed favor from among us? Drive them away from you; perhaps if you drive them away, we will follow you." So Allah revealed: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord…﴾. He said: Quraysh had said: "Were it not for Bilal and Ibn Umm Abd, we would follow Muhammad." So Allah revealed this verse.

Ikrimah said: Utba ibn Rabi'a, Shayba ibn Umayya, Mut'im ibn Adi, al-Harith ibn Nawfal, Qurza ibn Abd and Amr ibn Nawfal, among the nobles of Banu Abd Manaf from the people of disbelief, came to Abu Talib and said: "O Abu Talib, if your nephew Muhammad would drive away our clients and allies, for they are our slaves, it would be greater in our hearts, more obedient to him among us, and closer to our following him and affirming him." Abu Talib came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and told him what they had concealed. Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "If you did that, we would see what they want and where they will end up." Then this verse was revealed concerning their statement. When it was revealed, Umar ibn al-Khattab came and apologized for his statement.

Jubayr ibn Nufayl said: The Quraysh came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "You sent for us, so drive these scum away from you, and we will be your companions." So Allah revealed: ﴿And do not drive away…﴾.

Ibn Abbas said: ﴿those who call upon their Lord﴾ means those who worship their Lord with the obligatory prayer, ﴿morning and evening﴾ means the dawn prayer and the afternoon prayer. This was because some poor people were with the Prophet (ﷺ), and some of the nobles said: "When we pray, let these be delayed, and let them pray behind us." So Allah revealed: ﴿And do not drive away those who…﴾.

Hamza ibn Isa said: I entered upon al-Hasan and said: "O Abu Sa'id, what do you say about the words of Allah: ﴿And do not drive away those who believe﴾?" He said: "No, rather they are those who guard the prayers in congregation."

Mujahid said: I prayed the dawn prayer with Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab (may Allah be pleased with him). When the imam finished the salam, the people hurried to the storyteller (al-qass). Sa'id said: "How quickly the people rush to this gathering!"

Mujahid said: I said: "They interpret the words of Allah: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening﴾." He meant that this refers only to the prayer we have just left, and we said they remember their Lord.

Abu Ja'far said: meaning they recite the Qur'an.

﴿seeking His face﴾ is the answer to His words ﴿You are not accountable for them in anything﴾ [6:52]. His words ﴿so you would be among the wrongdoers﴾ are the answer to His words ﴿and do not drive away﴾; ﴿no one﴾ is the answer to a negation, and ﴿Allah﴾ is the answer to the prohibition. ﴿Among the wrongdoers﴾, meaning those who harm themselves through disobedience. Driving away is misplaced when it is not in its proper place.

﴿And thus We tested some of them by others﴾ [6:53]: the lowly and the customary ranking with respect to the master and the wealthy. ﴿So that they say: "Are these the ones on whom Allah has bestowed favor from among us?"﴾ That is, the nobles, the rich, say: "these," meaning the poor and weak, "on whom Allah has bestowed favor from among us." Al-Kalbi said: When a noble saw a lowly person had embraced Islam before him, he would be too proud to accept Islam and say: "This one has preceded me in Islam," so he would not accept it. ﴿Is not Allah most knowing of the grateful?﴾, meaning the believers. This is the answer to their words "are these the ones on whom Allah has bestowed favor from among us?" It was also said: "Is not Allah most knowing of the grateful, those who give thanks for Islam when He guides them to it?"

Al-Ala' ibn Bashir, from Abu Bakr al-Naji, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, said: I was in a group among which were poor emigrants, some of whom covered others from nakedness. A reciter was reciting to us while we listened to his recitation. The Prophet (ﷺ) came upon us until he stood over us. When the reciter saw him, he fell silent. He greeted and said: "What were you doing?" We said: "O Messenger of Allah, a reciter was reciting to us and we were listening to his recitation." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Praise be to Allah who has placed among my community those with whom I have been commanded to keep myself patient." Then he sat in the midst of us to level himself among us, then he said, gesturing with his hand like this, and the people formed a circle and their faces became visible. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not recognize any of them, and they were the poor emigrants. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Rejoice, destitute emigrants, in complete success on the Day of Resurrection: you will enter Paradise before the wealthy believers by half a day, which is equal to five hundred years." [136]

Hisham ibn Sulayman, from Abu Yazid al-Raqqashi, from Anas, said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "O assembly of the poor, Allah has been pleased that I should take pattern from your gatherings, and that Allah is with us," and He said: ﴿And keep yourself patient with those who call upon their Lord morning and evening﴾. For these are the gatherings of the prophets before you and of the righteous." [137]

Mu'awiya ibn Murra, from A'idh ibn Amr: Salman, Suhayb and Bilal were sitting when Abu Sufyan passed by them. They said to him: "The swords of Allah have not yet taken from the neck of the enemy of Allah what they should." Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) said to them: "You say this to the elder of Quraysh and its master?" Then he came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and he said: "O Abu Bakr, perhaps you have angered them; if you have angered them, you have angered your Lord." Abu Bakr fell upon them and said: "Perhaps I have angered you?" They said: "No, O Abu Bakr, may Allah forgive you." [An-Nasa'i]

﴿When those who believe in Our signs come to you…﴾: the scholars differed about the occasion of revelation of this verse.

Ikrimah said: It was revealed concerning those whom Allah prohibited His Prophet (ﷺ) from driving away. Whenever the Prophet (ﷺ) saw them, he would greet them first and say: "Praise be to Allah who has placed among my community those whom I was commanded to greet first with peace." [138]

Al-Kalbi said: When the verse ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord﴾ was revealed, Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) came to the Prophet (ﷺ), apologized to him for his statement and sought forgiveness of Allah for it, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I intended nothing by it but good." So ﴿When those who believe in Our signs come to you, say: "Peace be upon you…"﴾ was revealed concerning Umar (may Allah be pleased with him).

Ata' said: It was revealed concerning Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, Ali, Bilal, Salim, Abu Ubayda, Suhayb ibn Sinan, Umar, Ja'far, Uthman ibn Maz'un, Ammar ibn Yasir, al-Arqam ibn al-Arqam and Abu Salama ibn Abd al-Asad (may Allah be pleased with them all).

Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Men came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "We have committed many great sins." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) remained silent about them, so Allah revealed concerning these men: ﴿those who believe in Our signs, say: "Peace be upon you. Your Lord has prescribed for Himself mercy: whoever of you does evil in ignorance﴾.

Mujahid said: [ignorance] means he does not know the lawful from the unlawful; and "from his ignorance" means your Lord's command, and everyone who commits a sin does so in ignorance. It was also said: ignorant of what that sin brings upon him. It is said: he became ignorant when he preferred disobedience over obedience. ﴿then repents after it and makes amends﴾, meaning he turns back from his error and sets his deed right. It was also said: he makes his repentance sincere. ﴿indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ The reciters differed on the reading of ﴿annahu﴾. The Kufans [read it with a fatha on the alif in both places]. Ibn Kathir, al-A'mash, Ibn Umar, Hamza and al-Kisa'i read it as a fresh sentence (isti'naf) [with fatha in one place and kasra in the other]. Al-Hasan, Asim and Ya'qub read it in the accusative as a substitute for "mercy". The people of Medina read the first with a fatha, on the sense of "and He prescribed that he…", and read the second with a kasra as a fresh sentence, because what follows it is never reported. ﴿And thus﴾, that is, in this manner. It was also said: its meaning is "and We have explained to you in this surah and this verse."

And it came in the highest of what is explained concerning the deniers: ﴿Thus We detail the signs﴾, that is, We distinguish and make clear to you Our proof and Our evidences concerning everyone who denies, the people of falsehood. ﴿And that the way of the criminals may become evident﴾: the verb is raised, and its meaning is "that the path of the criminals may become manifest and clear." It is said: "the thing became clear (bana), made clear (abana), became clear in its explanation (tibyan) and became distinct (tabayyana) when it became apparent and plain." The word "sabil" (way) is masculine and feminine: Tamim treat it as masculine, while the people of the Hijaz treat it as feminine. The evidence for the masculine is His words: ﴿And if they see the way of right guidance, they will not adopt it as a way; but if they see the way of error, they will adopt it as a way﴾ [7:146]. The evidence for the feminine is His words: ﴿Why do you bar from the way of Allah those who believe, seeking to make it crooked?﴾ [7:86], and His words: ﴿Say, "This is my way; I invite to Allah with insight"﴾ [12:108]. Therefore one reading is "wa-litastabina" with the yā' and another with the tā', and the people of Medina read "wa-litastabina" with the tā' and "sabīla" in the accusative, addressing the Prophet (ﷺ): "and that you, O Muhammad, may learn the way of the criminals." It is said: "istabana al-shay'" and "tabayyanahu" when one knows it.

﴿Say: "Indeed I have been forbidden to worship those whom you invoke besides Allah."﴾ ﴿Say: "I will not follow your desires"﴾ in worshipping idols, and in driving away Bilal and Salman. ﴿Then I would have gone astray and would not be among the guided.﴾ That is, if I did that, I would have abandoned the path of truth and taken a way other than guidance.

Yahya ibn Wathhab [and Abu Raja'] read "qad dalilt" with a kasra on the lam. The two are dialects: "dalla yadullu" like "qalla yaqullu," and "dalla yadillu" like "malla yamillu." The first is more sound and more eloquent, because it is the dialect of the people of the Hijaz.

﴿Say: "Indeed I am upon clear evidence from my Lord"﴾: clarity, proof, insight and argument. ﴿and you have denied Him.﴾ That is, denied my Lord. ﴿What you seek to hasten is not with me﴾, meaning the punishment. It was revealed concerning al-Nadr ibn al-Harith. ﴿The decision is only Allah's; He relates the truth﴾. The people of the Hijaz and Asim read "yaqussu al-haqqa" with a doubled sad, meaning "He says the truth." They argued that it is written without a yā' in all the codices, and because it says "al-haqq," so one says "I judged by the truth." The rest read it with a dad, meaning "He decides by the truth," as evidenced by His words: ﴿And He is the best of deciders﴾ [7:87]. Al-fasl is the bringing of judgment. The reciters omitted the yā' for ease of pronunciation, then [...], as in His words ﴿burning of the Hellfire﴾ [37:163], ﴿Allah erases what He wills﴾ [13:39], ﴿Warnings will not avail﴾ [54:5], ﴿We will call the guards of Hell﴾ [96:18], and similar. They omitted the bā' from "al-haqq" because it is an adjective of the verbal noun, as if he judges the true judgment.

﴿Say: "If I had what you seek to hasten, within my power﴾, which is the punishment, ﴿the matter would have been decided between me and you﴾, that is, it would have been finished with the punishment and you would have been destroyed. ﴿And Allah is most knowing of the wrongdoers.﴾

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 6, verse 59–67:

﴿And with Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them but He.﴾ Al-mafatih is the plural of al-mafkah (key).

Ibn al-Sumayta' recited mafatih (with a yā'), as the plural of al-miftah (key). The meaning: whoever has knowledge of the unseen, and He opens that by His subtle kindness. The scholars differed concerning mafatih al-ghayb (the keys of the unseen).

ʿAbdullah ibn ʿUmar narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The keys of the unseen are five ... Indeed Allah has with Him the knowledge of the Hour, He sends down the rain, He knows what is in the wombs, no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow, and no soul knows in what land it will die. Indeed Allah is All-Knowing, All-Aware." [[al-Sunan al-Kubra: 4/411.]] [139]

al-Suddi said: mafatih al-ghayb means the treasuries of the unseen. Muqatil and al-Dahhak said: it means the treasuries of the earth.

And [it means] knowledge of when the punishment will descend upon you.

ʿAta': It means what is hidden from you of reward and punishment, and what my affair and your affair will come to. It was also said: they are the terms of life and the time of their ending. It was said: the states of the servants, of happiness and misery. It was said: the outcomes of lifespans and the conclusions of deeds. It was said: they are what has not yet occurred, whether it will occur or not, how what will occur will occur, and how what will not occur would have occurred had it occurred.

Ibn Masʿud said: Your Prophet was given knowledge of everything except the keys of the unseen.

﴿And He knows what is on the land and in the sea.﴾

Mujahid said: al-barr is the deserts, and al-bahr is every town that has water.

﴿And not a leaf falls but He knows it.﴾ Ibn ʿAbbas said: There is no tree on land or sea but that there is an angel with it, and each knows who eats from it and what falls of its leaves. And [He knows] how many of you [remain] of the leaves on the tree and what has fallen from it.

Abu al-Qasim ibn Habib said: I heard Abu Bakr ibn ʿAbdus say: its meaning is that He knows it as it turns from back to front until it falls on the ground.

﴿Nor a grain in the darknesses of the earth﴾, that is, in the bellies of the earth. It was also said: beneath the rock, in the lowest of the earths.

﴿Nor anything fresh or dry﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: The fresh is water, and the dry is the desert. ʿAta' said: it means what grows and what does not grow.

al-Hasan said: God records it as fresh and records it as dry, so that you may know, son of Adam, that your deed is more worthy of [repairing] that garden.

And he said: The fresh is the tongue of the believer, moist with the remembrance of God; the dry is the tongue of the disbeliever, which does not move with the remembrance of God.

And [it means] what pleases Allah, Mighty and Majestic. It was also said: they are trees and plants.

al-Aʿmash narrated from Abu Ziyad from ʿAbdullah ibn al-Harith, who said: There is no tree on earth, nor a spot the size of the eye of a needle, but upon it is an angel, and each brings to God its knowledge, its dryness when it dries and its moisture when it is moist.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated from Nafiʿ from Ibn ʿUmar from the Prophet (ﷺ): "There is no crop on the earth nor fruit on trees [and not a grain in the darknesses of the earth] [[So in the source.]] but on it is written: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate, the provision of so-and-so son of so-and-so. And that is His saying, exalted be He, in His decisive Book: ﴿And not a leaf falls but He knows it, nor a grain in the darknesses of the earth, nor anything fresh or dry, but it is in a clear Record.﴾" [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 7/4.]] [140]

﴿...but it is in a clear Record.﴾ ﴿And He is the One who takes you in death by night﴾, that is, He seizes your souls in your sleep. ﴿And He knows what you commit by day﴾; its origin is from the "jarihah" (limb) of the hand.

Then it was said of every limb of a person that it is his jarihah, meaning a member of his body through which he acts; from this comes "al-zarʿ al-jayyid" (good crop). It is also said: may Allah not leave him any jarihah, meaning no servant or maidservant who earns for him.

﴿Then He resurrects you therein﴾, that is, He raises you up and awakens you ﴿that a term appointed may be fulfilled﴾ in the Fire, meaning the appointed term of life until death, until its trace and its provision are finished.

Abu Talha and Abu Raja' recited li-yuqdaya with a fathah on the nūn and ajalan in the accusative. In this there is an establishment of proof against those who deny resurrection, meaning: as He has power over this, so He is able to resurrect you after death.

And he said: It is written in the Torah: O son of Adam, as you sleep so you die, and as He wakes you so He resurrects you.

﴿Then to Him is your return﴾ in the Hereafter. ﴿Then He will inform you﴾, that is, tell you and recompense you ﴿of what you used to do.﴾

﴿And He is the Subduer over His servants, and He sends over you guardians﴾, meaning the angels who guard the deeds of the children of Adam; it is the plural of ḥāfiẓ (guard). Its parallel is His saying: ﴿And indeed over you are guardians﴾ [[Surat al-Infitar: 10.]]. ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Among people is one who lives wretched, heart ignorant, heedless in wakefulness. But when he is faithful and sees the danger of death and fears the guardians, [he is saved]. People are only a departing one and a remaining one; he who departs is an admonition to he who remains.

﴿Until, when death comes to one of you, Our messengers take him﴾, meaning the assistants of the Angel of Death, who seize him, then hand him over to the Angel of Death. ﴿And they do not fail﴾, that is, they do not disobey and do not neglect.

ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmar recited lā yufrituna with the lightened form, meaning they do not exceed the limit.

﴿Then they are returned to Allah﴾, meaning the angels; it was also said: meaning the servants. ﴿Their true Master. Unquestionably, to Him is the judgment﴾, the decree concerning His creation. ﴿And He is the swiftest of reckoners﴾, meaning He does not need deliberation or calculation.

﴿Say: Who rescues you from the darknesses of the land and the sea﴾ when you lose the way and fear destruction, ﴿calling upon Him humbly and secretly﴾. ʿAsim recited wa-khufyah, and both are dialects. al-Aʿmash recited wa-khīfah, from fear, like the one in al-Aʿraf. ﴿"If He rescues us from this"﴾, that is, they say: if You rescue us from this, meaning these darknesses, ﴿we will surely be among the thankful﴾, among the believers.

﴿Say: Allah rescues you from them and from every distress﴾, meaning sorrow. ﴿Yet you associate partners [with Him].﴾

﴿Say: He is able to send upon you punishment from above you﴾, meaning the cry, the stones, the wind, and the flood, as He did to ʿAd, Thamud, the people of Shuʿayb, the people of Lut, and the people of Nuh. ﴿Or from beneath your feet﴾, meaning the sinking into the earth, as He did to Qarun.

Mujahid said: ﴿punishment from above you﴾ refers to the wicked rulers, and ﴿from beneath your feet﴾ to the evil slaves.

al-Dahhak: ﴿punishment from above you﴾ means from the side of your elders; ﴿or from beneath your feet﴾ means from below you. ﴿Or confuse you into sects﴾, or create you and divide and scatter among you desires and disagreements. ﴿And make you taste the violence of one another﴾, meaning the various swords, by killing one another, as was done to the Children of Israel.

When this verse was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Jibril, what will become of my community in this?" Jibril said to him: "I am only a servant like you. Ask your Lord." So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood, performed ablution, prayed, and asked his Lord; he was given two of the three requests and denied one. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I asked Him that He not send upon my community a punishment from above them or from beneath their feet, and He granted me that. I asked Him that He not make their violence among themselves, and He denied me. And Jibril (peace be upon him) informed me that the destruction of my community will be by the sword." [[With variation, in Tafsir al-Tabari: 7/292.]] [141]

al-Zuhri said: Khabbab ibn al-Aratt observed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) one night praying. When he finished, he said: At dawn, I saw you pray a prayer such as I had never seen you pray. He said: Yes, it was a prayer of desire and fear. I asked my Lord three things in it and He gave me two and withheld one. I asked Him not to let an enemy from other than them dominate my community, and He gave it to me. I asked Him not to send upon them a famine that would destroy them, and He gave it to me. I asked Him not to make their violence among themselves, and He withheld it from me.

﴿Behold how We vary the signs, that perhaps they may understand.﴾ ﴿But your people denied it﴾; Ibrahim ibn ʿUbalah recited kadhabat with the taʾ, [referring to the Qurʾan]. ﴿And it is the truth.﴾ It was also said: [it refers] to the punishment. ﴿Say: I am not a guardian over you﴾, that is, a keeper or watcher; it was also said: one given power over you. ﴿I am only a messenger.﴾

﴿For every news there is a settled time﴾, the place of its completion, its reality and its end, at which it becomes evident who is truthful and who is a liar, what is right and what is false.

Muqatil said: For every report that Allah the Exalted gives, there is a time and a place in which it occurs, without failure or delay.

al-Kalbi said: For every saying or deed there is a reality. What of it was in this world, you will come to know; what of it was in the Hereafter, it will become manifest to them. ﴿And you will surely know it.﴾

al-Hasan said: For every deed there is a recompense. Whoever does a good deed is recompensed with Paradise, and whoever does an evil deed is recompensed with the Fire. ﴿And you will surely know it, O people of Makkah.﴾

al-Suddi said: ﴿For every news there is a settled time﴾, that is, an appointed time which you conceal, and it will come to you until you recognize it.

ʿAta' said: ﴿For every news there is a settled time﴾: He delays its punishment so that he may commit his sin; when he has committed his sin, He punishes him.

al-Tha'labi said: I saw in some tafsirs that this verse is beneficial for toothache: if it is written on paper and placed upon the tooth.

﴿Then He resurrects you therein﴾, that is, He raises you up and awakens you ﴿that a term appointed may be fulfilled﴾ in the Fire, meaning the appointed term of life until death, until its trace and its provision are finished.

Abu Talha and Abu Raja' recited li-yuqdaya with a fathah on the nūn and ajalan in the accusative. In this there is an establishment of proof against those who deny resurrection, meaning: as He has power over this, so He is able to resurrect you after death.

And he said: It is written in the Torah: O son of Adam, as you sleep so you die, and as He wakes you so He resurrects you.

﴿Then to Him is your return﴾ in the Hereafter. ﴿Then He will inform you﴾, that is, tell you and recompense you ﴿of what you used to do.﴾

﴿And He is the Subduer over His servants, and He sends over you guardians﴾, meaning the angels who guard the deeds of the children of Adam; it is the plural of ḥāfiẓ (guard). Its parallel is His saying: ﴿And indeed over you are guardians﴾ [[Surat al-Infitar: 10.]]. ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Among people is one who lives wretched, heart ignorant, heedless in wakefulness. But when he is faithful and sees the danger of death and fears the guardians, [he is saved]. People are only a departing one and a remaining one; he who departs is an admonition to he who remains.

﴿Until, when death comes to one of you, Our messengers take him﴾, meaning the assistants of the Angel of Death, who seize him, then hand him over to the Angel of Death. ﴿And they do not fail﴾, that is, they do not disobey and do not neglect.

ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmar recited lā yufrituna with the lightened form, meaning they do not exceed the limit.

﴿Then they are returned to Allah﴾, meaning the angels; it was also said: meaning the servants. ﴿Their true Master. Unquestionably, to Him is the judgment﴾, the decree concerning His creation. ﴿And He is the swiftest of reckoners﴾, meaning He does not need deliberation or calculation.

﴿Say: Who rescues you from the darknesses of the land and the sea﴾ when you lose the way and fear destruction, ﴿calling upon Him humbly and secretly﴾. ʿAsim recited wa-khufyah, and both are dialects. al-Aʿmash recited wa-khīfah, from fear, like the one in al-Aʿraf. ﴿"If He rescues us from this"﴾, that is, they say: if You rescue us from this, meaning these darknesses, ﴿we will surely be among the thankful﴾, among the believers.

﴿Say: Allah rescues you from them and from every distress﴾, meaning sorrow. ﴿Yet you associate partners [with Him].﴾

﴿Say: He is able to send upon you punishment from above you﴾, meaning the cry, the stones, the wind, and the flood, as He did to ʿAd, Thamud, the people of Shuʿayb, the people of Lut, and the people of Nuh. ﴿Or from beneath your feet﴾, meaning the sinking into the earth, as He did to Qarun.

Mujahid said: ﴿punishment from above you﴾ refers to the wicked rulers, and ﴿from beneath your feet﴾ to the evil slaves.

al-Dahhak: ﴿punishment from above you﴾ means from the side of your elders; ﴿or from beneath your feet﴾ means from below you. ﴿Or confuse you into sects﴾, or create you and divide and scatter among you desires and disagreements. ﴿And make you taste the violence of one another﴾, meaning the various swords, by killing one another, as was done to the Children of Israel.

When this verse was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Jibril, what will become of my community in this?" Jibril said to him: "I am only a servant like you. Ask your Lord." So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood, performed ablution, prayed, and asked his Lord; he was given two of the three requests and denied one. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I asked Him that He not send upon my community a punishment from above them or from beneath their feet, and He granted me that. I asked Him that He not make their violence among themselves, and He denied me. And Jibril (peace be upon him) informed me that the destruction of my community will be by the sword." [[With variation, in Tafsir al-Tabari: 7/292.]] [141]

al-Zuhri said: Khabbab ibn al-Aratt observed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) one night praying. When he finished, he said: At dawn, I saw you pray a prayer such as I had never seen you pray. He said: Yes, it was a prayer of desire and fear. I asked my Lord three things in it and He gave me two and withheld one. I asked Him not to let an enemy from other than them dominate my community, and He gave it to me. I asked Him not to send upon them a famine that would destroy them, and He gave it to me. I asked Him not to make their violence among themselves, and He withheld it from me.

﴿Behold how We vary the signs, that perhaps they may understand.﴾ ﴿But your people denied it﴾; Ibrahim ibn ʿUbalah recited kadhabat with the taʾ, [referring to the Qurʾan]. ﴿And it is the truth.﴾ It was also said: [it refers] to the punishment. ﴿Say: I am not a guardian over you﴾, that is, a keeper or watcher; it was also said: one given power over you. ﴿I am only a messenger.﴾

﴿For every news there is a settled time﴾, the place of its completion, its reality and its end, at which it becomes evident who is truthful and who is a liar, what is right and what is false.

Muqatil said: For every report that Allah the Exalted gives, there is a time and a place in which it occurs, without failure or delay.

al-Kalbi said: For every saying or deed there is a reality. What of it was in this world, you will come to know; what of it was in the Hereafter, it will become manifest to them. ﴿And you will surely know it.﴾

al-Hasan said: For every deed there is a recompense. Whoever does a good deed is recompensed with Paradise, and whoever does an evil deed is recompensed with the Fire. ﴿And you will surely know it, O people of Makkah.﴾

al-Suddi said: ﴿For every news there is a settled time﴾, that is, an appointed time which you conceal, and it will come to you until you recognize it.

ʿAta' said: ﴿For every news there is a settled time﴾: He delays its punishment so that he may commit his sin; when he has committed his sin, He punishes him.

al-Tha'labi said: I saw in some tafsirs that this verse is beneficial for toothache: if it is written on paper and placed upon the tooth.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 6, verse 59–67:

﴿And with Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them but He.﴾ Al-mafatih is the plural of al-mafkah (key).

Ibn al-Sumayta' recited mafatih (with a yā'), as the plural of al-miftah (key). The meaning: whoever has knowledge of the unseen, and He opens that by His subtle kindness. The scholars differed concerning mafatih al-ghayb (the keys of the unseen).

ʿAbdullah ibn ʿUmar narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The keys of the unseen are five ... Indeed Allah has with Him the knowledge of the Hour, He sends down the rain, He knows what is in the wombs, no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow, and no soul knows in what land it will die. Indeed Allah is All-Knowing, All-Aware." [[al-Sunan al-Kubra: 4/411.]] [139]

al-Suddi said: mafatih al-ghayb means the treasuries of the unseen. Muqatil and al-Dahhak said: it means the treasuries of the earth.

And [it means] knowledge of when the punishment will descend upon you.

ʿAta': It means what is hidden from you of reward and punishment, and what my affair and your affair will come to. It was also said: they are the terms of life and the time of their ending. It was said: the states of the servants, of happiness and misery. It was said: the outcomes of lifespans and the conclusions of deeds. It was said: they are what has not yet occurred, whether it will occur or not, how what will occur will occur, and how what will not occur would have occurred had it occurred.

Ibn Masʿud said: Your Prophet was given knowledge of everything except the keys of the unseen.

﴿And He knows what is on the land and in the sea.﴾

Mujahid said: al-barr is the deserts, and al-bahr is every town that has water.

﴿And not a leaf falls but He knows it.﴾ Ibn ʿAbbas said: There is no tree on land or sea but that there is an angel with it, and each knows who eats from it and what falls of its leaves. And [He knows] how many of you [remain] of the leaves on the tree and what has fallen from it.

Abu al-Qasim ibn Habib said: I heard Abu Bakr ibn ʿAbdus say: its meaning is that He knows it as it turns from back to front until it falls on the ground.

﴿Nor a grain in the darknesses of the earth﴾, that is, in the bellies of the earth. It was also said: beneath the rock, in the lowest of the earths.

And he said: The fresh is the tongue of the believer, moist with the remembrance of God; the dry is the tongue of the disbeliever, which does not move with the remembrance of God.

And [it means] what pleases Allah, Mighty and Majestic. It was also said: they are trees and plants.

﴿And when you see those who engage in vain talk about Our verses﴾, meaning the Qur'an, with mockery and falsehood, ﴿turn away from them﴾, meaning leave them and do not sit with them, ﴿until they engage in another discourse﴾, meaning enter into a conversation other than the Qur'an. That was because:

The polytheists, when they sat with the believers, would revile the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), speak abusively, and mock the Qur'an. So Allah forbade the believers from sitting with them.

﴿And if Satan causes you to forget﴾.

Ibn 'Abbas and Ibn 'Amir read it as ﴿yunsawnaka﴾ with emphasis (tashdid, gemination of the letter nun), ﴿Satan, then do not sit after the reminder with the wrongdoing people﴾. So get up from their company after you have remembered. Then He said: ﴿Nor is there any accountability for those who fear Allah upon them from their reckoning﴾, meaning from the sins of those who engage in such talk, ﴿anything﴾.

Ibn 'Abbas said: The Muslims said, "We fear sin when we leave them and do not forbid them." So Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed this verse.

Ibn 'Abbas said in another report: The Muslims said, "If whenever the polytheists mock the Qur'an and engage in vain talk about it we rise and leave them, we will not be able to sit in the Sacred Mosque or circumambulate the House." So it was revealed: ﴿Nor is there any accountability for those who fear Allah upon them from their reckoning anything, but a reminder﴾, meaning remind them and admonish them. It is in the accusative position as a verbal noun (maṣdar, a noun derived from the verb), meaning "remind them a reminder." The words dhikr and dhikrā are one and the same. It may also be in the nominative position, meaning "it is a reminder." ﴿That perhaps they may fear Allah﴾, meaning to refrain from vain talk, when you admonish them. It was also said: "And when you rise," it is sufficient for them in that case, from mockery and vain talk. It was also said: "That perhaps they may feel shame."

﴿And leave those who have taken their religion as amusement and play﴾, meaning as falsehood and frivolity, ﴿and whom the worldly life has deceived﴾. That is because Allah, the Exalted, made for you a people's festival which they exalt and in which they pray. Some people made their festival a source of amusement and play, except the community of Muhammad (ﷺ), who made their festival a prayer to Allah.

It also refers to the days such as Friday, the Fitr, and the Nahr. ﴿And remind by it﴾, meaning admonish with the Qur'an, ﴿lest a soul be given over to destruction for what it has earned﴾. The meaning is "lest a soul be ruined," as in His saying, ﴿Allah makes clear to you lest you go astray﴾, meaning so that you do not go astray. The meaning of the verse is: remind them so that they may believe, so that no soul is given over to destruction for what it has earned.

Ibn 'Abbas said: "destroyed." Qatada said: "held back." Al-Hasan, Mujahid, 'Ikrima, and al-Suddi said: "delivered to ruin." Ibn Abi Talha reported from Ibn 'Abbas: "disgraced."

Al-Dahhak said: "disgraced and burned." Al-Mu'arrikh and Ibn Zayd said: "seized."

The poet said:

"And my handing over of the sons of Bi'ly without crime,
regarding their wrongdoing and without blood shed."

Al-'Awf ibn al-Ahwas said: He had mortgaged his house and bore the burden of a wealthy man, for the sons of Qushayr, the blood money of al-Suhqiyya. They said, "We are not satisfied with you," so they handed him over as a pledge. The word ﴿bi'un﴾ means a crime, and al-bi'w means an offence.

Al-Akhfash said: ﴿tubsala﴾ means "be recompensed." Al-Farra' said: "be held as a pledge."

He also recited al-Nabigha al-Ja'di:

"We are pledged for the sake of the one who regains consciousness, 'Amir,
for what was pledged in al-Darda', and so he was given over."

'Atiyya al-'Awfi said: "delivered into the disgrace of Hell."

The people of language said: The original sense of al-ibsāl is prohibition. It is said: "I forbade the thing (absaltu al-shay')" when you forbid it, and al-basl means the forbidden.

The poet said:

"She rose early blaming you after weakness in generosity,
the forbidden (basl) is my blame and my reproach upon you."

He said: "We recited basl," meaning a brave man whose death is not reckoned, as if he has forbidden himself. Then this was made a description for every stern person. It also means "left behind" and "remaining." It is said: "a drink that is basl," meaning abandoned.

Al-Shanfara said:

"There I do not hope for a life that pleases me,
the night-companion of the nights, forbidden by its offences."

His saying ﴿for them there is no protector besides Allah﴾, meaning for those souls, ﴿no intimate friend or companion﴾, ﴿nor intercessor who will intercede for them in the Hereafter. And if they offer every compensation, it will not be accepted from them﴾. Abu 'Ubayda said: "And if they offer every kind of ransom, it will not be accepted from them, because repentance is only in life."

﴿Those are the ones who have been given over to destruction for what they earned. For them is a drink of boiling water and a painful punishment because they used to disbelieve.﴾

﴿Say: Shall we call upon, besides Allah, that which neither benefits us nor harms us, and be turned back on our heels after Allah has guided us?﴾ It was revealed concerning 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr when he invited his father to disbelief, so Allah, the Exalted, revealed: ﴿Say: Shall we call upon, besides Allah, that which does not benefit us if we worship it, nor harm us if we abandon it, and be turned back on our heels to polytheism after Allah has guided us?﴾

The Arabs say of every returning failure who did not achieve his need: "He was turned back on his heels" and "he drew back on his heels," so it is like one who is seized by the devils, meaning misled.

Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "Like one whom the ghouls have enticed in the wilderness, and they have misled him, while he is bewildered and lost." ﴿In the earth, bewildered﴾, and "bewildered" (ḥayrān) is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (ḥāl).

Al-A'mash and Hamza read ﴿istahwā bihi﴾ with a ba' (preposition bi). Talha read ﴿istahwāhu﴾ with an alif.

Al-Hasan read ﴿istahwathu al-shayāṭūn﴾. In the codex of 'Abdullah and Ubayy it is ﴿istahwāhu al-shaytān﴾ in the singular. ﴿He has companions who call him to guidance, "Come to us,"﴾ meaning they brought him. It was also said: the companions of Muhammad (ﷺ).

﴿Say: Indeed, the guidance of Allah is the guidance, and we have been commanded to submit to the Lord of the worlds﴾, meaning so that we submit to the Lord of the worlds. ﴿And to establish prayer and fear Him; and He it is to whom you will be gathered﴾, up to His saying ﴿when the Trumpet is blown﴾.

Abu 'Ubayda said: "It is the plural of ṣūrah, like sūrah and sūr."

Al-'Ajjaj said:

"And many a one with a closed-off enclosure,
I traveled toward it through the high walls."

Others said: It is an oven in which something is blown, in the dialect of the people of Yemen.

Al-'Ajjaj recited:

"We struck them on the day of the two gatherings,
with the panting horses in the dust of the two clouds,
a fierce striking, not like the striking of the two horns (ṣūrayn)."

This is supported by the report narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ): "How can I be at ease when the one who holds the horn has put the horn to his mouth, [and bent its curve], and has lowered his ear, watching for when he will be commanded, and then blows?"

Then He said: ﴿Knower of the unseen and the visible, and He is the Wise, the All-Aware.﴾
