﴿Say: Indeed, the guidance of Allah is the guidance, and we have been commanded to submit to the Lord of the worlds﴾, meaning so that we submit to the Lord of the worlds. ﴿And to establish prayer and fear Him; and He it is to whom you will be gathered﴾, up to His saying ﴿when the Trumpet is blown﴾.

Abu 'Ubayda said: "It is the plural of ṣūrah, like sūrah and sūr."

Al-'Ajjaj said:

"And many a one with a closed-off enclosure,
I traveled toward it through the high walls."

Others said: It is an oven in which something is blown, in the dialect of the people of Yemen.

Al-'Ajjaj recited:

"We struck them on the day of the two gatherings,
with the panting horses in the dust of the two clouds,
a fierce striking, not like the striking of the two horns (ṣūrayn)."

This is supported by the report narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ): "How can I be at ease when the one who holds the horn has put the horn to his mouth, [and bent its curve], and has lowered his ear, watching for when he will be commanded, and then blows?"

Then He said: ﴿Knower of the unseen and the visible, and He is the Wise, the All-Aware.﴾

﴿And when you see those who engage in vain talk about Our verses﴾, meaning the Qur'an, with mockery and falsehood, ﴿turn away from them﴾, meaning leave them and do not sit with them, ﴿until they engage in another discourse﴾, meaning enter into a conversation other than the Qur'an. That was because:

The polytheists, when they sat with the believers, would revile the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), speak abusively, and mock the Qur'an. So Allah forbade the believers from sitting with them.

﴿And if Satan causes you to forget﴾.

Ibn 'Abbas and Ibn 'Amir read it as ﴿yunsawnaka﴾ with emphasis (tashdid, gemination of the letter nun), ﴿Satan, then do not sit after the reminder with the wrongdoing people﴾. So get up from their company after you have remembered. Then He said: ﴿Nor is there any accountability for those who fear Allah upon them from their reckoning﴾, meaning from the sins of those who engage in such talk, ﴿anything﴾.

Ibn 'Abbas said: The Muslims said, "We fear sin when we leave them and do not forbid them." So Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed this verse.

Ibn 'Abbas said in another report: The Muslims said, "If whenever the polytheists mock the Qur'an and engage in vain talk about it we rise and leave them, we will not be able to sit in the Sacred Mosque or circumambulate the House." So it was revealed: ﴿Nor is there any accountability for those who fear Allah upon them from their reckoning anything, but a reminder﴾, meaning remind them and admonish them. It is in the accusative position as a verbal noun (maṣdar, a noun derived from the verb), meaning "remind them a reminder." The words dhikr and dhikrā are one and the same. It may also be in the nominative position, meaning "it is a reminder." ﴿That perhaps they may fear Allah﴾, meaning to refrain from vain talk, when you admonish them. It was also said: "And when you rise," it is sufficient for them in that case, from mockery and vain talk. It was also said: "That perhaps they may feel shame."

﴿And leave those who have taken their religion as amusement and play﴾, meaning as falsehood and frivolity, ﴿and whom the worldly life has deceived﴾. That is because Allah, the Exalted, made for you a people's festival which they exalt and in which they pray. Some people made their festival a source of amusement and play, except the community of Muhammad (ﷺ), who made their festival a prayer to Allah.

It also refers to the days such as Friday, the Fitr, and the Nahr. ﴿And remind by it﴾, meaning admonish with the Qur'an, ﴿lest a soul be given over to destruction for what it has earned﴾. The meaning is "lest a soul be ruined," as in His saying, ﴿Allah makes clear to you lest you go astray﴾, meaning so that you do not go astray. The meaning of the verse is: remind them so that they may believe, so that no soul is given over to destruction for what it has earned.

Ibn 'Abbas said: "destroyed." Qatada said: "held back." Al-Hasan, Mujahid, 'Ikrima, and al-Suddi said: "delivered to ruin." Ibn Abi Talha reported from Ibn 'Abbas: "disgraced."

Al-Dahhak said: "disgraced and burned." Al-Mu'arrikh and Ibn Zayd said: "seized."

The poet said:

"And my handing over of the sons of Bi'ly without crime,
regarding their wrongdoing and without blood shed."

Al-'Awf ibn al-Ahwas said: He had mortgaged his house and bore the burden of a wealthy man, for the sons of Qushayr, the blood money of al-Suhqiyya. They said, "We are not satisfied with you," so they handed him over as a pledge. The word ﴿bi'un﴾ means a crime, and al-bi'w means an offence.

Al-Akhfash said: ﴿tubsala﴾ means "be recompensed." Al-Farra' said: "be held as a pledge."

He also recited al-Nabigha al-Ja'di:

"We are pledged for the sake of the one who regains consciousness, 'Amir,
for what was pledged in al-Darda', and so he was given over."

'Atiyya al-'Awfi said: "delivered into the disgrace of Hell."

The people of language said: The original sense of al-ibsāl is prohibition. It is said: "I forbade the thing (absaltu al-shay')" when you forbid it, and al-basl means the forbidden.

The poet said:

"She rose early blaming you after weakness in generosity,
the forbidden (basl) is my blame and my reproach upon you."

He said: "We recited basl," meaning a brave man whose death is not reckoned, as if he has forbidden himself. Then this was made a description for every stern person. It also means "left behind" and "remaining." It is said: "a drink that is basl," meaning abandoned.

Al-Shanfara said:

"There I do not hope for a life that pleases me,
the night-companion of the nights, forbidden by its offences."

His saying ﴿for them there is no protector besides Allah﴾, meaning for those souls, ﴿no intimate friend or companion﴾, ﴿nor intercessor who will intercede for them in the Hereafter. And if they offer every compensation, it will not be accepted from them﴾. Abu 'Ubayda said: "And if they offer every kind of ransom, it will not be accepted from them, because repentance is only in life."

﴿Those are the ones who have been given over to destruction for what they earned. For them is a drink of boiling water and a painful punishment because they used to disbelieve.﴾

﴿Say: Shall we call upon, besides Allah, that which neither benefits us nor harms us, and be turned back on our heels after Allah has guided us?﴾ It was revealed concerning 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr when he invited his father to disbelief, so Allah, the Exalted, revealed: ﴿Say: Shall we call upon, besides Allah, that which does not benefit us if we worship it, nor harm us if we abandon it, and be turned back on our heels to polytheism after Allah has guided us?﴾

The Arabs say of every returning failure who did not achieve his need: "He was turned back on his heels" and "he drew back on his heels," so it is like one who is seized by the devils, meaning misled.

Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "Like one whom the ghouls have enticed in the wilderness, and they have misled him, while he is bewildered and lost." ﴿In the earth, bewildered﴾, and "bewildered" (ḥayrān) is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (ḥāl).

Al-A'mash and Hamza read ﴿istahwā bihi﴾ with a ba' (preposition bi). Talha read ﴿istahwāhu﴾ with an alif.

Al-Hasan read ﴿istahwathu al-shayāṭūn﴾. In the codex of 'Abdullah and Ubayy it is ﴿istahwāhu al-shaytān﴾ in the singular. ﴿He has companions who call him to guidance, "Come to us,"﴾ meaning they brought him. It was also said: the companions of Muhammad (ﷺ).

﴿Say: Indeed, the guidance of Allah is the guidance, and we have been commanded to submit to the Lord of the worlds﴾, meaning so that we submit to the Lord of the worlds. ﴿And to establish prayer and fear Him; and He it is to whom you will be gathered﴾, up to His saying ﴿when the Trumpet is blown﴾.

Abu 'Ubayda said: "It is the plural of ṣūrah, like sūrah and sūr."

Al-'Ajjaj said:

"And many a one with a closed-off enclosure,
I traveled toward it through the high walls."

Others said: It is an oven in which something is blown, in the dialect of the people of Yemen.

Al-'Ajjaj recited:

"We struck them on the day of the two gatherings,
with the panting horses in the dust of the two clouds,
a fierce striking, not like the striking of the two horns (ṣūrayn)."

This is supported by the report narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ): "How can I be at ease when the one who holds the horn has put the horn to his mouth, [and bent its curve], and has lowered his ear, watching for when he will be commanded, and then blows?"

Then He said: ﴿Knower of the unseen and the visible, and He is the Wise, the All-Aware.﴾

And when Abraham said to his father Azar, ﴿Do you take idols as gods?﴾

Muhammad ibn Ishaq, al-Dahhak and al-Kalbi said: Azar was the father of Abraham. He is a name like Israel and Jacob. He was from the people of Kutha, a village in the outskirts of Kufa [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 7/316.]].

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: "He was the father of Abraham."

Sulayman [al-Taymi] said: "It is an insult and a defect. In their speech it means 'the crooked one.'" It was also said that its meaning is "the old man" in Persian, *al-Hanam*. According to these opinions, it is in the genitive position as an apposition (*badal*) or a qualifier (*sifa*), but it is in the accusative form because it is *la yanṣarif* (a diptote, which does not take nunation).

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, Mujahid and Yaman said: "Azar is the name of an idol." According to this interpretation, it is in the accusative position.

In the speech there is an inversion of order. Its sense is: "Do you take Azar as idols and gods?"

Al-Hasan, Abu Yazid al-Madani and Ya'qub al-Hadrami read *Azaru* with a *damma* (in the vocative), meaning: "O Azar, do you take idols as gods besides God," up to His words ﴿And thus We showed Abraham the dominion of the heavens and the earth﴾.

This means: just as We gave him insight into his religion and the truth in opposition to his people, so We showed him *malakut al-samawat wal-ard*, that is, their dominion. *Al-malakut* means *al-mulk* (sovereignty). The *ta'* in it is added to show intensity, as in *al-jabarut* and *al-rahamut* (the ta' indicates the feminine, or an intensifier, as in these words).

It is reported from the Arabs: "*Sarra'an lahu malakut al-Yaman wal-Iraq*" (a rapid [ruler] whose sovereignty is Yemen and Iraq).

Al-Kisa'i said: "The *ta'* was added to it for emphasis," and he recited:
"And the worst of men is the cheat, the deceiver [*al-khalbut*]" [[Kitab al-'Ayn: 4/271.]].

'Ikrimah said: "It is the sovereignty, except that in Nabataean it is *malkuta*." He read it with a dotted *ya'* as *maliyyan* (meaning sovereignty).

Ibn 'Abbas said: "It means the creation of the heavens and the earth."

Mujahid and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "It means the signs of the heavens and the earth. That is because he was raised up on a rock, and the heavens and the earth were uncovered for him, even the Throne and the lowest part of the earth, and he looked at his place in Paradise."

This is the meaning of His words ﴿And We gave him his reward in this world﴾ [al-'Ankabut 27]: that is, We showed him his place in Paradise.

Qatadah said: Abraham (peace be upon him) said to himself that he was the most merciful of creation. So God, the Mighty and Majestic, raised him until he overlooked the people of the earth and saw their deeds. When he saw them committing acts of disobedience, he said to God: "Destroy them!" and he began to curse them. His Lord said to him: "I am more merciful to My servants than you. Descend, perhaps they will repent."

Qays ibn Abi Hazim narrated from 'Ali, may God honor his face, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "When God, the Exalted, showed Abraham the dominion of the heavens and the earth, he overlooked a man committing one of the sins against God, so he invoked God against him and he perished. Then he overlooked another and invoked God against him and he perished. Then he overlooked another, and when he wanted to invoke against him, God, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed to him: 'O Abraham, you are a man whose supplication is answered. So do not invoke against My servants, for they are in relation to Me in three situations: either they repent to Me and I accept their repentance, or I bring forth from them a soul that glorifies Me, or they [return] to Me. If I wish, I pardon him, and if I wish, I punish him.'"

Al-Dahhak said: "*Malakut al-samawat wal-ard*" is the sun, the moon and the stars. Qatadah said: Abraham (peace be upon him) was hidden from one of the tyrants, and provision was made for him in his fingers: whenever he sucked one of his fingers, he found provision in it. When he came out, God showed him *malakut al-samawat wal-ard*. The *malakut* of the heavens is the sun, the moon and the stars, and the *malakut* of the earth is the mountains, the trees and the seas.

﴿And that he might be among the certain ones.﴾ ﴿So when the night covered him, he saw a star...﴾ up to the end of the verse.

The exegetes said: Abraham (peace be upon him) was born in the time of Nimrod ibn Kan'an. Nimrod was the first to place a crown on his head and to put a crown on himself, and he called the people [...]. He had soothsayers and astrologers.

They said: "In this year a boy will be born in your city who will change the religion of the people of the earth, and your destruction and the end of your rule will be at his hands." It is said that they found this in the books of the prophets, peace be upon them.

Al-Suddi said: Nimrod saw in his dream as if a star had risen and taken away the light of the sun and the moon until neither of them had any light. He was terrified by this, a great terror. He summoned the sorcerers, the soothsayers, the magicians and the physiognomists, and asked them about it. They said: "A child will be born in your region this year who will bring about the ruin of your kingdom and your household at his hands."

So he ordered that every boy born in his region that year be slain, and he ordered that men be separated from women, and he appointed a man over every ten [women]. Whenever a woman menstruated, he allowed her to be with him, and when she became pure, he separated her from him. Then Azar, the father of Abraham, returned and found his wife had become pure from menstruation, so he lay with her in her purity, and she conceived Abraham (peace be upon him).

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Nimrod sent to every pregnant woman in his town and detained her with him, except the mother of Abraham, for he did not know of her pregnancy, because she was a young girl who did not recognize pregnancy in her womb.

Al-Suddi said: Nimrod took the men out to the encampment and kept them away from the women, out of fear of that child who might be. He remained in this state as long as God willed. Then he had a need in the city, and he did not trust anyone among his people except Azar, so he sent for him and summoned him. He said: "I have a need of you, and I want to advise you concerning it. I am sending you only because I trust you. I swear to you that you must not approach your wife or lie with her." Azar said: "I am more protective of my religion than that." So he advised him concerning his need, then sent him. He entered the city and fulfilled his need. Then he said: "I entered upon my family and looked at him [the child]." When he looked at the mother of Abraham, he could not restrain himself until he lay with her, and she conceived Abraham.

Ibn 'Abbas said: When the mother of Abraham became pregnant, the soothsayers said to Nimrod: "The boy we told you about has been conceived by his mother tonight." So Nimrod ordered the slaying of the boys. When the mother of Abraham's delivery drew near and her labor pains seized her, she went out fleeing, fearing that someone would see her and kill her child. She placed him in a dry river, then wrapped him in a cloth and placed him among reeds. She returned and reported that she had given birth, and that the child was in such and such a place. Azar went to take him from that place. He dug a tunnel for him beside a river and hid him in it, and sealed its entrance with a rock out of fear of wild beasts. His mother used to visit him and nurse him.

Al-Suddi said: When the belly of the mother of Abraham grew large, Azar feared that [the child] would be slaughtered, so he took her to a land between Kufa and Basra called Urmah. He lodged her in a tunnel in the earth and put water beside them both. He used to visit her secretly, hiding that from his companions. She gave birth in that tunnel, and he grew up. When he was one year old, he was like a three-year-old, and he became a youth, out of fear that [he would fall into] the greed of the slaughterers. Then Azar mentioned to his companions that he had a grown son, and he took him out to them.

Ibn Ishaq said: When the mother of Abraham felt the pains of labor, she went out at night to a cave near her and gave birth to Abraham in it. She tended to his needs as is done for a newborn, then sealed the cave and returned to her house. Then she would look in on him in the cave to see what had happened, and she would find him alive, sucking his thumb.

Abu Rawq said: Whenever the mother of Abraham entered upon Abraham, she found him sucking his fingers. One day she said: "I will look at his fingers." She found him sucking from one finger water, from another honey, from another milk, from another dates, and from another ghee.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Azar had asked the mother of Abraham what had happened with her pregnancy. She said: "I gave birth to a boy, and he died." So he believed her and remained silent about it. A day for Abraham in youth was like a month, and a month like a year. Abraham did not remain in the cave except for fifteen months. Then he returned to his father Azar, and he told him that he was his son, and his mother told him that he was his son, and she informed him of what she had done during his absence. Azar was delighted by that and rejoiced greatly.

They said: Abraham grew up while he was in the tunnel, after he had said to his mother: "Who is my Lord?" She said: "I am." He said: "Then who is your lord?" She said: "Your father." He said: "Then who is the lord of my father?" She said to him: "Be quiet." So he was quiet. When she returned to her husband, she said: "Did you see the boy about whom we used to talk, that he would be of a religion other than that of the people of the earth? He is your son." Then she told him what [Abraham] had said to her. Then his father Azar came to him, and Abraham said to him: "O my father, who is my Lord?" He said: "Your mother." He said: "Then who is my mother's lord?" He said: "I am." He said: "Then who is your lord?" He said: "Nimrod." He said: "Then who is the lord of Nimrod?" So [Azar] slapped him a slap and said: "Be quiet and get up!" He said to his parents: "Take me out." So they took him out of the tunnel. They set out with him when the sun had set. Abraham looked at the camels, the horses and the sheep, and said: "Father, what are these?" He said: "Camels, horses and sheep." He said: "These must have a lord and a creator." Then he looked and reflected on the creation of the heavens and the earth. He said: "The One who created me, provided for me, fed me and gave me drink, He is my Lord; I have no god besides Him." Then he looked, and behold, Jupiter had risen, and it is said Venus; that night was at the end of the month, so he saw the star before the moon. He said: ﴿This is my lord.﴾

That is His words, mighty and majestic: ﴿So when the night covered him﴾, that is, it entered. It is said: *janna al-layl* and *ajanna*, and *janahu al-layl* and *ajannahu*, and *janna 'alayhi al-layl yajunnu junuunan wa jinanan* when it grew dark and everything passed away. The jinn are so called because they are hidden [*ijtinan*], so they are not seen.

Abu 'Ubaydah said: *junun al-layl* is its blackness. He recited:
"Had it not been for the darkness of night, the pursuit of our riders would have overtaken him, at Dhu al-Ramth and al-Arta, 'Iyad ibn Nashib" [[al-Sihah: 5/2094, where it reads "rikabuna" (our riders); Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 7/25. *Al-Ramth* with a kasra is the pasture of camels, and *al-Arta* is a tree that grows in sand.]].

﴿And he saw a star, [and] said, "This is my lord."﴾ They differed concerning it. Some of them took it according to its apparent meaning and said: Abraham (peace be upon him) was not one who sought guidance, bewildered, seeking success, until God granted him success and gave him his rectitude. This statement of his was made in his childhood, before the proof was established against him. In that condition one would say that neither disbelief nor faith exists.

Evidence for this is what 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "When ﴿the night covered him, he saw a star, [and] said, 'This is my lord.'﴾ He worshipped it until it set. When it set, he said, ﴿'I do not like those that set.'﴾ When he saw the moon rising, he said, ﴿'This is my lord,'﴾ and worshipped it until it set. When it set, ﴿'If my Lord does not guide me, I will surely be among the people who are astray.'﴾ When he saw the sun rising, he said, ﴿'This is my lord; this is greater,'﴾ and worshipped it until the sun set. When it set, he said: ﴿'O my people, indeed I am free from what you associate.'﴾"

Others rejected this view and said: It is not permissible that a messenger of God should come upon a time when he was not monotheistic, knowing, and free from every worshipped other than Him.

They said: How could they accuse him of this, when God protected and purified him in his place of rest and his place of storage, and granted him his rectitude beforehand, and showed him His dominion, and He said: ﴿when he came to his Lord with a sound heart﴾ [al-Saffat 84], and He said: ﴿And thus We showed Abraham the dominion of the heavens and the earth, that he might be among the certain﴾ [al-An'am 75]? "He saw a star and said, 'This is my lord,'" based on belief and reality? This is something that could never happen.

Then four interpretations were given of it. The first interpretation: Abraham (peace be upon him) wanted to lead them step by step with this statement, to make them recognize their error and ignorance in exalting what they exalted, and to establish the proof against them, and to show them that he exalted what they exalted, and sought guidance from where they sought it. When [the star] set, he showed them the deficiency inherent in the stars, so they would see the error of what they claimed. They used to exalt the stars, worship them, and treat them as judges.

They said: The likeness of this is like the disciple (*al-hawari*) who came to a people who worshipped their idol, and he showed them its greatness, and they were guided by his opinion in many matters, until an enemy of theirs, whom the king feared for his kingdom, reproached them, and the king consulted the disciple about his affair.

They said [to the disciple]: "Our opinion is that you should call upon our god so that what has misled us may be removed, for we are gathered for such a day." So they gathered around it, crying out and supplicating, while their enemy hurried and relied [on that]. When it became clear to them that their lord neither benefits nor harms, he said to them, in the form of a question and a reproach for their action: ﴿This is my lord?﴾ And could such a thing be a lord? That is, this is not my lord, like God's words ﴿'Or you will be among the immortals'﴾ [al-A'raf 20], meaning that they are the immortals.

And like Moses' words to Pharaoh: ﴿And is it a favor of which you remind me that you have enslaved the children of Israel?﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 22], meaning: "Or is it a favor that you have granted?"

Al-Hudhali said:
"They raised me up and said, 'O Khuwaylid, do not be alarmed,'
so I said, and I denied the faces, 'They, they [are the ones]'" [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 7/325; al-Sihah: 3/1223; the verse is by Abu Khirash.]].

Another said:
"By your life, I do not know, though I am knowledgeable,
whether [he is] Shu'ayth ibn Sahm or Shu'ayth ibn Munqir" [[Same source.]].

The third interpretation: Abraham (peace be upon him) said this as an argument against his people, not in the sense of doubt about his Lord, as if he said: "This is my lord according to you." ﴿When it set, he said—and it was the crescent—﴾ he said: "This is greater than it," so he looked at what you were devoted to here, meaning with you. His words ﴿'Taste! Indeed you are the mighty, the noble'﴾ [al-Dukhan 49], with his saying to Abu Jahl [the trial in the fire]: "You are such in your own estimation, but in our view you are neither mighty nor noble." There is abbreviation and implication in the verse, and its meaning is: he said, "They say, 'This is my lord,'" like His words ﴿And when Abraham was raising the foundations of the House, and Ishmael [said], "Our Lord..."﴾ [al-Baqarah 127], meaning they say: "Our Lord, accept from us." ﴿When it set, that is, disappeared and vanished, he said: "I do not like those that set"﴾ as lords, for they do not last. ﴿When he saw the moon rising, that is, ascending, he said, "This is my lord." When it set, he said, "If my Lord does not guide me, I will surely be among the people who are astray,"﴾ from guidance. ﴿When he saw the sun rising, he said, "This is my lord."﴾

Muhammad ibn Muqatil al-Razi said: He said "This" [masculine] and not "This" [feminine] because he saw the light of the sun and did not see the sun itself, so he returned it to the ray.

Al-Akhfash said: He meant: "This one who rises is my lord," or "This one who comes, I see him as my lord." "This is greater," because he saw it as brighter and greater. When it set, he said: ﴿"O my people, indeed I am free from what you associate. Indeed I have turned my face toward..."﴾ up to the end of the verse.

Azar used to make idols. When Abraham was taken into his care, he began to make idols and give them to Abraham to sell. Abraham would take them and call out: "Who will buy what harms him and does not benefit him?" No one would buy them. When they became too many for him, he took them to a river, struck their heads in it, and said: "Drink!" mocking his people and the error they were in, until his disparagement of them and his mockery of them became widespread among his people and the people of his town.

﴿And his people disputed with him,﴾ that is, argued with him about his religion. ﴿He said, "Do you argue with me about God, when He has guided me?"﴾ that is, He informed me of monotheism and the truth. ﴿And I do not fear what you associate with Him﴾. That is because they said to him: "Are you not afraid that our gods will afflict you with harm, such as leprosy or madness, because of your disparagement of them?" He said to them: ﴿"And I do not fear what you associate with Him," that is, the idols, "except that my Lord wills something." Everything is in accordance with what He wills, ﴿"My Lord encompasses all things in knowledge"﴾, that is, His knowledge encompasses everything. ﴿"Will you not then remember? And how should I fear what you have associated, when you do not fear that you have associated with God that for which He has sent down no authority to you?"﴾ That is, the idols, which do not see, do not hear, do not harm and do not benefit. ﴿"Then which of the two parties has more right to security, if you know?"﴾ That is, more worthy of security [are we, or whoever follows my religion?]. Then God, the Mighty and Majestic, said, judging and deciding between them: ﴿Those who believed and did not mix their belief with wrongdoing [zulm]—for them is security, and they are guided.﴾ That is, they did not mix their faith with shirk: ﴿for them is security, and they are guided﴾.

'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud said: When this verse was revealed, the companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) took it to apply to themselves and said: "We have not wronged ourselves." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "It is not as you think; rather, it is as Luqman said to his son: ﴿'O my son, do not associate anything with God. Indeed, association is a great wrong'﴾ [Luqman 13]" [142] (It is only shirk).

﴿And that was Our argument, which We gave to Abraham against his people﴾, that is, to overcome their argument and defeat them with proof. He said: it is His words ﴿Those who believed and did not mix their belief with wrongdoing﴾; he said: "with worship of idols." ﴿We raise by degrees whom We will﴾, by knowledge.

The people of Kufa, Yahya ibn Ya'mur and Ibn Mahisin read *darajatin* with tanwin, meaning: "We raise whom We will by degrees." Its like is in Surah Yusuf: ﴿Indeed your Lord is Wise, Knowing﴾.

And when Abraham said to his father Azar, ﴿Do you take idols as gods?﴾

Muhammad ibn Ishaq, al-Dahhak and al-Kalbi said: Azar was the father of Abraham. He is a name like Israel and Jacob. He was from the people of Kutha, a village in the outskirts of Kufa [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 7/316.]].

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: "He was the father of Abraham."

Sulayman [al-Taymi] said: "It is an insult and a defect. In their speech it means 'the crooked one.'" It was also said that its meaning is "the old man" in Persian, *al-Hanam*. According to these opinions, it is in the genitive position as an apposition (*badal*) or a qualifier (*sifa*), but it is in the accusative form because it is *la yanṣarif* (a diptote, which does not take nunation).

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, Mujahid and Yaman said: "Azar is the name of an idol." According to this interpretation, it is in the accusative position.

In the speech there is an inversion of order. Its sense is: "Do you take Azar as idols and gods?"

Al-Hasan, Abu Yazid al-Madani and Ya'qub al-Hadrami read *Azaru* with a *damma* (in the vocative), meaning: "O Azar, do you take idols as gods besides God," up to His words ﴿And thus We showed Abraham the dominion of the heavens and the earth﴾.

This means: just as We gave him insight into his religion and the truth in opposition to his people, so We showed him *malakut al-samawat wal-ard*, that is, their dominion. *Al-malakut* means *al-mulk* (sovereignty). The *ta'* in it is added to show intensity, as in *al-jabarut* and *al-rahamut* (the ta' indicates the feminine, or an intensifier, as in these words).

It is reported from the Arabs: "*Sarra'an lahu malakut al-Yaman wal-Iraq*" (a rapid [ruler] whose sovereignty is Yemen and Iraq).

Al-Kisa'i said: "The *ta'* was added to it for emphasis," and he recited:
"And the worst of men is the cheat, the deceiver [*al-khalbut*]" [[Kitab al-'Ayn: 4/271.]].

'Ikrimah said: "It is the sovereignty, except that in Nabataean it is *malkuta*." He read it with a dotted *ya'* as *maliyyan* (meaning sovereignty).

Ibn 'Abbas said: "It means the creation of the heavens and the earth."

Mujahid and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "It means the signs of the heavens and the earth. That is because he was raised up on a rock, and the heavens and the earth were uncovered for him, even the Throne and the lowest part of the earth, and he looked at his place in Paradise."

This is the meaning of His words ﴿And We gave him his reward in this world﴾ [al-'Ankabut 27]: that is, We showed him his place in Paradise.

Qatadah said: Abraham (peace be upon him) said to himself that he was the most merciful of creation. So God, the Mighty and Majestic, raised him until he overlooked the people of the earth and saw their deeds. When he saw them committing acts of disobedience, he said to God: "Destroy them!" and he began to curse them. His Lord said to him: "I am more merciful to My servants than you. Descend, perhaps they will repent."

Qays ibn Abi Hazim narrated from 'Ali, may God honor his face, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "When God, the Exalted, showed Abraham the dominion of the heavens and the earth, he overlooked a man committing one of the sins against God, so he invoked God against him and he perished. Then he overlooked another and invoked God against him and he perished. Then he overlooked another, and when he wanted to invoke against him, God, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed to him: 'O Abraham, you are a man whose supplication is answered. So do not invoke against My servants, for they are in relation to Me in three situations: either they repent to Me and I accept their repentance, or I bring forth from them a soul that glorifies Me, or they [return] to Me. If I wish, I pardon him, and if I wish, I punish him.'"

Al-Dahhak said: "*Malakut al-samawat wal-ard*" is the sun, the moon and the stars. Qatadah said: Abraham (peace be upon him) was hidden from one of the tyrants, and provision was made for him in his fingers: whenever he sucked one of his fingers, he found provision in it. When he came out, God showed him *malakut al-samawat wal-ard*. The *malakut* of the heavens is the sun, the moon and the stars, and the *malakut* of the earth is the mountains, the trees and the seas.

﴿And that he might be among the certain ones.﴾ ﴿So when the night covered him, he saw a star...﴾ up to the end of the verse.

The exegetes said: Abraham (peace be upon him) was born in the time of Nimrod ibn Kan'an. Nimrod was the first to place a crown on his head and to put a crown on himself, and he called the people [...]. He had soothsayers and astrologers.

They said: "In this year a boy will be born in your city who will change the religion of the people of the earth, and your destruction and the end of your rule will be at his hands." It is said that they found this in the books of the prophets, peace be upon them.

Al-Suddi said: Nimrod saw in his dream as if a star had risen and taken away the light of the sun and the moon until neither of them had any light. He was terrified by this, a great terror. He summoned the sorcerers, the soothsayers, the magicians and the physiognomists, and asked them about it. They said: "A child will be born in your region this year who will bring about the ruin of your kingdom and your household at his hands."

So he ordered that every boy born in his region that year be slain, and he ordered that men be separated from women, and he appointed a man over every ten [women]. Whenever a woman menstruated, he allowed her to be with him, and when she became pure, he separated her from him. Then Azar, the father of Abraham, returned and found his wife had become pure from menstruation, so he lay with her in her purity, and she conceived Abraham (peace be upon him).

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Nimrod sent to every pregnant woman in his town and detained her with him, except the mother of Abraham, for he did not know of her pregnancy, because she was a young girl who did not recognize pregnancy in her womb.

Al-Suddi said: Nimrod took the men out to the encampment and kept them away from the women, out of fear of that child who might be. He remained in this state as long as God willed. Then he had a need in the city, and he did not trust anyone among his people except Azar, so he sent for him and summoned him. He said: "I have a need of you, and I want to advise you concerning it. I am sending you only because I trust you. I swear to you that you must not approach your wife or lie with her." Azar said: "I am more protective of my religion than that." So he advised him concerning his need, then sent him. He entered the city and fulfilled his need. Then he said: "I entered upon my family and looked at him [the child]." When he looked at the mother of Abraham, he could not restrain himself until he lay with her, and she conceived Abraham.

Ibn 'Abbas said: When the mother of Abraham became pregnant, the soothsayers said to Nimrod: "The boy we told you about has been conceived by his mother tonight." So Nimrod ordered the slaying of the boys. When the mother of Abraham's delivery drew near and her labor pains seized her, she went out fleeing, fearing that someone would see her and kill her child. She placed him in a dry river, then wrapped him in a cloth and placed him among reeds. She returned and reported that she had given birth, and that the child was in such and such a place. Azar went to take him from that place. He dug a tunnel for him beside a river and hid him in it, and sealed its entrance with a rock out of fear of wild beasts. His mother used to visit him and nurse him.

Al-Suddi said: When the belly of the mother of Abraham grew large, Azar feared that [the child] would be slaughtered, so he took her to a land between Kufa and Basra called Urmah. He lodged her in a tunnel in the earth and put water beside them both. He used to visit her secretly, hiding that from his companions. She gave birth in that tunnel, and he grew up. When he was one year old, he was like a three-year-old, and he became a youth, out of fear that [he would fall into] the greed of the slaughterers. Then Azar mentioned to his companions that he had a grown son, and he took him out to them.

Ibn Ishaq said: When the mother of Abraham felt the pains of labor, she went out at night to a cave near her and gave birth to Abraham in it. She tended to his needs as is done for a newborn, then sealed the cave and returned to her house. Then she would look in on him in the cave to see what had happened, and she would find him alive, sucking his thumb.

Abu Rawq said: Whenever the mother of Abraham entered upon Abraham, she found him sucking his fingers. One day she said: "I will look at his fingers." She found him sucking from one finger water, from another honey, from another milk, from another dates, and from another ghee.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Azar had asked the mother of Abraham what had happened with her pregnancy. She said: "I gave birth to a boy, and he died." So he believed her and remained silent about it. A day for Abraham in youth was like a month, and a month like a year. Abraham did not remain in the cave except for fifteen months. Then he returned to his father Azar, and he told him that he was his son, and his mother told him that he was his son, and she informed him of what she had done during his absence. Azar was delighted by that and rejoiced greatly.

They said: Abraham grew up while he was in the tunnel, after he had said to his mother: "Who is my Lord?" She said: "I am." He said: "Then who is your lord?" She said: "Your father." He said: "Then who is the lord of my father?" She said to him: "Be quiet." So he was quiet. When she returned to her husband, she said: "Did you see the boy about whom we used to talk, that he would be of a religion other than that of the people of the earth? He is your son." Then she told him what [Abraham] had said to her. Then his father Azar came to him, and Abraham said to him: "O my father, who is my Lord?" He said: "Your mother." He said: "Then who is my mother's lord?" He said: "I am." He said: "Then who is your lord?" He said: "Nimrod." He said: "Then who is the lord of Nimrod?" So [Azar] slapped him a slap and said: "Be quiet and get up!" He said to his parents: "Take me out." So they took him out of the tunnel. They set out with him when the sun had set. Abraham looked at the camels, the horses and the sheep, and said: "Father, what are these?" He said: "Camels, horses and sheep." He said: "These must have a lord and a creator." Then he looked and reflected on the creation of the heavens and the earth. He said: "The One who created me, provided for me, fed me and gave me drink, He is my Lord; I have no god besides Him." Then he looked, and behold, Jupiter had risen, and it is said Venus; that night was at the end of the month, so he saw the star before the moon. He said: ﴿This is my lord.﴾

That is His words, mighty and majestic: ﴿So when the night covered him﴾, that is, it entered. It is said: *janna al-layl* and *ajanna*, and *janahu al-layl* and *ajannahu*, and *janna 'alayhi al-layl yajunnu junuunan wa jinanan* when it grew dark and everything passed away. The jinn are so called because they are hidden [*ijtinan*], so they are not seen.

Abu 'Ubaydah said: *junun al-layl* is its blackness. He recited:
"Had it not been for the darkness of night, the pursuit of our riders would have overtaken him, at Dhu al-Ramth and al-Arta, 'Iyad ibn Nashib" [[al-Sihah: 5/2094, where it reads "rikabuna" (our riders); Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 7/25. *Al-Ramth* with a kasra is the pasture of camels, and *al-Arta* is a tree that grows in sand.]].

﴿And he saw a star, [and] said, "This is my lord."﴾ They differed concerning it. Some of them took it according to its apparent meaning and said: Abraham (peace be upon him) was not one who sought guidance, bewildered, seeking success, until God granted him success and gave him his rectitude. This statement of his was made in his childhood, before the proof was established against him. In that condition one would say that neither disbelief nor faith exists.

Evidence for this is what 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "When ﴿the night covered him, he saw a star, [and] said, 'This is my lord.'﴾ He worshipped it until it set. When it set, he said, ﴿'I do not like those that set.'﴾ When he saw the moon rising, he said, ﴿'This is my lord,'﴾ and worshipped it until it set. When it set, ﴿'If my Lord does not guide me, I will surely be among the people who are astray.'﴾ When he saw the sun rising, he said, ﴿'This is my lord; this is greater,'﴾ and worshipped it until the sun set. When it set, he said: ﴿'O my people, indeed I am free from what you associate.'﴾"

Others rejected this view and said: It is not permissible that a messenger of God should come upon a time when he was not monotheistic, knowing, and free from every worshipped other than Him.

They said: How could they accuse him of this, when God protected and purified him in his place of rest and his place of storage, and granted him his rectitude beforehand, and showed him His dominion, and He said: ﴿when he came to his Lord with a sound heart﴾ [al-Saffat 84], and He said: ﴿And thus We showed Abraham the dominion of the heavens and the earth, that he might be among the certain﴾ [al-An'am 75]? "He saw a star and said, 'This is my lord,'" based on belief and reality? This is something that could never happen.

Then four interpretations were given of it. The first interpretation: Abraham (peace be upon him) wanted to lead them step by step with this statement, to make them recognize their error and ignorance in exalting what they exalted, and to establish the proof against them, and to show them that he exalted what they exalted, and sought guidance from where they sought it. When [the star] set, he showed them the deficiency inherent in the stars, so they would see the error of what they claimed. They used to exalt the stars, worship them, and treat them as judges.

They said: The likeness of this is like the disciple (*al-hawari*) who came to a people who worshipped their idol, and he showed them its greatness, and they were guided by his opinion in many matters, until an enemy of theirs, whom the king feared for his kingdom, reproached them, and the king consulted the disciple about his affair.

They said [to the disciple]: "Our opinion is that you should call upon our god so that what has misled us may be removed, for we are gathered for such a day." So they gathered around it, crying out and supplicating, while their enemy hurried and relied [on that]. When it became clear to them that their lord neither benefits nor harms, he said to them, in the form of a question and a reproach for their action: ﴿This is my lord?﴾ And could such a thing be a lord? That is, this is not my lord, like God's words ﴿'Or you will be among the immortals'﴾ [al-A'raf 20], meaning that they are the immortals.

And like Moses' words to Pharaoh: ﴿And is it a favor of which you remind me that you have enslaved the children of Israel?﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 22], meaning: "Or is it a favor that you have granted?"

Al-Hudhali said:
"They raised me up and said, 'O Khuwaylid, do not be alarmed,'
so I said, and I denied the faces, 'They, they [are the ones]'" [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 7/325; al-Sihah: 3/1223; the verse is by Abu Khirash.]].

Another said:
"By your life, I do not know, though I am knowledgeable,
whether [he is] Shu'ayth ibn Sahm or Shu'ayth ibn Munqir" [[Same source.]].

The third interpretation: Abraham (peace be upon him) said this as an argument against his people, not in the sense of doubt about his Lord, as if he said: "This is my lord according to you." ﴿When it set, he said—and it was the crescent—﴾ he said: "This is greater than it," so he looked at what you were devoted to here, meaning with you. His words ﴿'Taste! Indeed you are the mighty, the noble'﴾ [al-Dukhan 49], with his saying to Abu Jahl [the trial in the fire]: "You are such in your own estimation, but in our view you are neither mighty nor noble." There is abbreviation and implication in the verse, and its meaning is: he said, "They say, 'This is my lord,'" like His words ﴿And when Abraham was raising the foundations of the House, and Ishmael [said], "Our Lord..."﴾ [al-Baqarah 127], meaning they say: "Our Lord, accept from us." ﴿When it set, that is, disappeared and vanished, he said: "I do not like those that set"﴾ as lords, for they do not last. ﴿When he saw the moon rising, that is, ascending, he said, "This is my lord." When it set, he said, "If my Lord does not guide me, I will surely be among the people who are astray,"﴾ from guidance. ﴿When he saw the sun rising, he said, "This is my lord."﴾

Muhammad ibn Muqatil al-Razi said: He said "This" [masculine] and not "This" [feminine] because he saw the light of the sun and did not see the sun itself, so he returned it to the ray.

Al-Akhfash said: He meant: "This one who rises is my lord," or "This one who comes, I see him as my lord." "This is greater," because he saw it as brighter and greater. When it set, he said: ﴿"O my people, indeed I am free from what you associate. Indeed I have turned my face toward..."﴾ up to the end of the verse.

Azar used to make idols. When Abraham was taken into his care, he began to make idols and give them to Abraham to sell. Abraham would take them and call out: "Who will buy what harms him and does not benefit him?" No one would buy them. When they became too many for him, he took them to a river, struck their heads in it, and said: "Drink!" mocking his people and the error they were in, until his disparagement of them and his mockery of them became widespread among his people and the people of his town.

﴿And his people disputed with him,﴾ that is, argued with him about his religion. ﴿He said, "Do you argue with me about God, when He has guided me?"﴾ that is, He informed me of monotheism and the truth. ﴿And I do not fear what you associate with Him﴾. That is because they said to him: "Are you not afraid that our gods will afflict you with harm, such as leprosy or madness, because of your disparagement of them?" He said to them: ﴿"And I do not fear what you associate with Him," that is, the idols, "except that my Lord wills something." Everything is in accordance with what He wills, ﴿"My Lord encompasses all things in knowledge"﴾, that is, His knowledge encompasses everything. ﴿"Will you not then remember? And how should I fear what you have associated, when you do not fear that you have associated with God that for which He has sent down no authority to you?"﴾ That is, the idols, which do not see, do not hear, do not harm and do not benefit. ﴿"Then which of the two parties has more right to security, if you know?"﴾ That is, more worthy of security [are we, or whoever follows my religion?]. Then God, the Mighty and Majestic, said, judging and deciding between them: ﴿Those who believed and did not mix their belief with wrongdoing [zulm]—for them is security, and they are guided.﴾ That is, they did not mix their faith with shirk: ﴿for them is security, and they are guided﴾.

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "It is not as you think; rather, it is as Luqman said to his son: ﴿'O my son, do not associate anything with God. Indeed, association is a great wrong'﴾ [Luqman 13]" [142] (It is only shirk).

﴿And that was Our argument, which We gave to Abraham against his people﴾, that is, to overcome their argument and defeat them with proof. Ibn 'Abbas said: When the mother of Abraham became pregnant, the soothsayers said to Nimrod: "The boy we told you about has been conceived by his mother tonight." So Nimrod ordered the slaying of the boys. When the mother of Abraham's delivery drew near and her labor pains seized her, she went out fleeing, fearing that someone would see her and kill her child. She placed him in a dry river, then wrapped him in a cloth and placed him among reeds. She returned and reported that she had given birth, and that the child was in such and such a place. Azar went to take him from that place. He dug a tunnel for him beside a river and hid him in it, and sealed its entrance with a rock out of fear of wild beasts. His mother used to visit him and nurse him.

Al-Suddi said: When the belly of the mother of Abraham grew large, Azar feared that [the child] would be slaughtered, so he took her to a land between Kufa and Basra called Urmah. He lodged her in a tunnel in the earth and put water beside them both. He used to visit her secretly, hiding that from his companions. She gave birth in that tunnel, and he grew up. When he was one year old, he was like a three-year-old, and he became a youth, out of fear that [he would fall into] the greed of the slaughterers. Then Azar mentioned to his companions that he had a grown son, and he took him out to them.

Ibn Ishaq said: When the mother of Abraham felt the pains of labor, she went out at night to a cave near her and gave birth to Abraham in it. She tended to his needs as is done for a newborn, then sealed the cave and returned to her house. Then she would look in on him in the cave to see what had happened, and she would find him alive, sucking his thumb.

Abu Rawq said: Whenever the mother of Abraham entered upon Abraham, she found him sucking his fingers. One day she said: "I will look at his fingers." She found him sucking from one finger water, from another honey, from another milk, from another dates, and from another ghee.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Azar had asked the mother of Abraham what had happened with her pregnancy. She said: "I gave birth to a boy, and he died." So he believed her and remained silent about it. A day for Abraham in youth was like a month, and a month like a year. Abraham did not remain in the cave except for fifteen months. Then he returned to his father Azar, and he told him that he was his son, and his mother told him that he was his son, and she informed him of what she had done during his absence. Azar was delighted by that and rejoiced greatly.

They said: Abraham grew up while he was in the tunnel, after he had said to his mother: "Who is my Lord?" She said: "I am." He said: "Then who is your lord?" She said: "Your father." He said: "Then who is the lord of my father?" She said to him: "Be quiet." So he was quiet. When she returned to her husband, she said: "Did you see the boy about whom we used to talk, that he would be of a religion other than that of the people of the earth? He is your son." Then she told him what [Abraham] had said to her. Then his father Azar came to him, and Abraham said to him: "O my father, who is my Lord?" He said: "Your mother." He said: "Then who is my mother's lord?" He said: "I am." He said: "Then who is your lord?" He said: "Nimrod." He said: "Then who is the lord of Nimrod?" So [Azar] slapped him a slap and said: "Be quiet and get up!" He said to his parents: "Take me out." So they took him out of the tunnel. They set out with him when the sun had set. Abraham looked at the camels, the horses and the sheep, and said: "Father, what are these?" He said: "Camels, horses and sheep." He said: "These must have a lord and a creator." Then he looked and reflected on the creation of the heavens and the earth. He said: "The One who created me, provided for me, fed me and gave me drink, He is my Lord; I have no god besides Him." Then he looked, and behold, Jupiter had risen, and it is said Venus; that night was at the end of the month, so he saw the star before the moon. He said: ﴿This is my lord.﴾

That is His words, mighty and majestic: ﴿So when the night covered him﴾, that is, it entered. It is said: *janna al-layl* and *ajanna*, and *janahu al-layl* and *ajannahu*, and *janna 'alayhi al-layl yajunnu junuunan wa jinanan* when it grew dark and everything passed away. The jinn are so called because they are hidden [*ijtinan*], so they are not seen.

Abu 'Ubaydah said: *junun al-layl* is its blackness. He recited:
"Had it not been for the darkness of night, the pursuit of our riders would have overtaken him, at Dhu al-Ramth and al-Arta, 'Iyad ibn Nashib" [[al-Sihah: 5/2094, where it reads "rikabuna" (our riders); Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 7/25. *Al-Ramth* with a kasra is the pasture of camels, and *al-Arta* is a tree that grows in sand.]].

﴿And he saw a star, [and] said, "This is my lord."﴾ They differed concerning it. Some of them took it according to its apparent meaning and said: Abraham (peace be upon him) was not one who sought guidance, bewildered, seeking success, until God granted him success and gave him his rectitude. This statement of his was made in his childhood, before the proof was established against him. In that condition one would say that neither disbelief nor faith exists.

Evidence for this is what 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "When ﴿the night covered him, he saw a star, [and] said, 'This is my lord.'﴾ He worshipped it until it set. When it set, he said, ﴿'I do not like those that set.'﴾ When he saw the moon rising, he said, ﴿'This is my lord,'﴾ and worshipped it until it set. When it set, ﴿'If my Lord does not guide me, I will surely be among the people who are astray.'﴾ When he saw the sun rising, he said, ﴿'This is my lord; this is greater,'﴾ and worshipped it until the sun set. When it set, he said: ﴿'O my people, indeed I am free from what you associate.'﴾"

Others rejected this view and said: It is not permissible that a messenger of God should come upon a time when he was not monotheistic, knowing, and free from every worshipped other than Him.

They said: How could they accuse him of this, when God protected and purified him in his place of rest and his place of storage, and granted him his rectitude beforehand, and showed him His dominion, and He said: ﴿when he came to his Lord with a sound heart﴾ [al-Saffat 84], and He said: ﴿And thus We showed Abraham the dominion of the heavens and the earth, that he might be among the certain﴾ [al-An'am 75]? "He saw a star and said, 'This is my lord,'" based on belief and reality? This is something that could never happen.

Then four interpretations were given of it. The first interpretation: Abraham (peace be upon him) wanted to lead them step by step with this statement, to make them recognize their error and ignorance in exalting what they exalted, and to establish the proof against them, and to show them that he exalted what they exalted, and sought guidance from where they sought it. When [the star] set, he showed them the deficiency inherent in the stars, so they would see the error of what they claimed. They used to exalt the stars, worship them, and treat them as judges.

They said: The likeness of this is like the disciple (*al-hawari*) who came to a people who worshipped their idol, and he showed them its greatness, and they were guided by his opinion in many matters, until an enemy of theirs, whom the king feared for his kingdom, reproached them, and the king consulted the disciple about his affair.

They said [to the disciple]: "Our opinion is that you should call upon our god so that what has misled us may be removed, for we are gathered for such a day." So they gathered around it, crying out and supplicating, while their enemy hurried and relied [on that]. When it became clear to them that their lord neither benefits nor harms, he said to them, in the form of a question and a reproach for their action: ﴿This is my lord?﴾ And could such a thing be a lord? That is, this is not my lord, like God's words ﴿'Or you will be among the immortals'﴾ [al-A'raf 20], meaning that they are the immortals.

And like Moses' words to Pharaoh: ﴿And is it a favor of which you remind me that you have enslaved the children of Israel?﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 22], meaning: "Or is it a favor that you have granted?"

Al-Hudhali said:
"They raised me up and said, 'O Khuwaylid, do not be alarmed,'
so I said, and I denied the faces, 'They, they [are the ones]'" [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 7/325; al-Sihah: 3/1223; the verse is by Abu Khirash.]].

Another said:
"By your life, I do not know, though I am knowledgeable,
whether [he is] Shu'ayth ibn Sahm or Shu'ayth ibn Munqir" [[Same source.]].

The third interpretation: Abraham (peace be upon him) said this as an argument against his people, not in the sense of doubt about his Lord, as if he said: "This is my lord according to you." ﴿When it set, he said—and it was the crescent—﴾ he said: "This is greater than it," so he looked at what you were devoted to here, meaning with you. His words ﴿'Taste! Indeed you are the mighty, the noble'﴾ [al-Dukhan 49], with his saying to Abu Jahl [the trial in the fire]: "You are such in your own estimation, but in our view you are neither mighty nor noble." There is abbreviation and implication in the verse, and its meaning is: he said, "They say, 'This is my lord,'" like His words ﴿And when Abraham was raising the foundations of the House, and Ishmael [said], "Our Lord..."﴾ [al-Baqarah 127], meaning they say: "Our Lord, accept from us." ﴿When it set, that is, disappeared and vanished, he said: "I do not like those that set"﴾ as lords, for they do not last. ﴿When he saw the moon rising, that is, ascending, he said, "This is my lord." When it set, he said, "If my Lord does not guide me, I will surely be among the people who are astray,"﴾ from guidance. ﴿When he saw the sun rising, he said, "This is my lord."﴾

Muhammad ibn Muqatil al-Razi said: He said "This" [masculine] and not "This" [feminine] because he saw the light of the sun and did not see the sun itself, so he returned it to the ray.

Al-Akhfash said: He meant: "This one who rises is my lord," or "This one who comes, I see him as my lord." "This is greater," because he saw it as brighter and greater. When it set, he said: ﴿"O my people, indeed I am free from what you associate. Indeed I have turned my face toward..."﴾ up to the end of the verse.

Azar used to make idols. When Abraham was taken into his care, he began to make idols and give them to Abraham to sell. Abraham would take them and call out: "Who will buy what harms him and does not benefit him?" No one would buy them. When they became too many for him, he took them to a river, struck their heads in it, and said: "Drink!" mocking his people and the error they were in, until his disparagement of them and his mockery of them became widespread among his people and the people of his town.

﴿And his people disputed with him,﴾ that is, argued with him about his religion. ﴿He said, "Do you argue with me about God, when He has guided me?"﴾ that is, He informed me of monotheism and the truth. ﴿And I do not fear what you associate with Him﴾. That is because they said to him: "Are you not afraid that our gods will afflict you with harm, such as leprosy or madness, because of your disparagement of them?" He said to them: ﴿"And I do not fear what you associate with Him," that is, the idols, "except that my Lord wills something." Everything is in accordance with what He wills, ﴿"My Lord encompasses all things in knowledge"﴾, that is, His knowledge encompasses everything. ﴿"Will you not then remember? And how should I fear what you have associated, when you do not fear that you have associated with God that for which He has sent down no authority to you?"﴾ That is, the idols, which do not see, do not hear, do not harm and do not benefit. ﴿"Then which of the two parties has more right to security, if you know?"﴾ That is, more worthy of security [are we, or whoever follows my religion?]. Then God, the Mighty and Majestic, said, judging and deciding between them: ﴿Those who believed and did not mix their belief with wrongdoing [zulm]—for them is security, and they are guided.﴾ That is, they did not mix their faith with shirk: ﴿for them is security, and they are guided﴾.

'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud said: When this verse was revealed, the companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) took it to apply to themselves and said: "We have not wronged ourselves." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "It is not as you think; rather, it is as Luqman said to his son: ﴿'O my son, do not associate anything with God. Indeed, association is a great wrong'﴾ [Luqman 13]" [142] (It is only shirk).

﴿And that was Our argument, which We gave to Abraham against his people﴾, that is, to overcome their argument and defeat them with proof. He said: it is His words ﴿Those who believed and did not mix their belief with wrongdoing﴾; he said: "with worship of idols." ﴿We raise by degrees whom We will﴾, by knowledge.

The people of Kufa, Yahya ibn Ya'mur and Ibn Mahisin read *darajatin* with tanwin, meaning: "We raise whom We will by degrees." Its like is in Surah Yusuf: ﴿Indeed your Lord is Wise, Knowing﴾.

And when Abraham said to his father Azar, ﴿Do you take idols as gods?﴾

Muhammad ibn Ishaq, al-Dahhak and al-Kalbi said: Azar was the father of Abraham. He is a name like Israel and Jacob. He was from the people of Kutha, a village in the outskirts of Kufa [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 7/316.]].

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: "He was the father of Abraham."

Sulayman [al-Taymi] said: "It is an insult and a defect. In their speech it means 'the crooked one.'" It was also said that its meaning is "the old man" in Persian, *al-Hanam*. According to these opinions, it is in the genitive position as an apposition (*badal*) or a qualifier (*sifa*), but it is in the accusative form because it is *la yanṣarif* (a diptote, which does not take nunation).

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, Mujahid and Yaman said: "Azar is the name of an idol." According to this interpretation, it is in the accusative position.

In the speech there is an inversion of order. Its sense is: "Do you take Azar as idols and gods?"

Al-Hasan, Abu Yazid al-Madani and Ya'qub al-Hadrami read *Azaru* with a *damma* (in the vocative), meaning: "O Azar, do you take idols as gods besides God," up to His words ﴿And thus We showed Abraham the dominion of the heavens and the earth﴾.

This means: just as We gave him insight into his religion and the truth in opposition to his people, so We showed him *malakut al-samawat wal-ard*, that is, their dominion. *Al-malakut* means *al-mulk* (sovereignty). The *ta'* in it is added to show intensity, as in *al-jabarut* and *al-rahamut* (the ta' indicates the feminine, or an intensifier, as in these words).

It is reported from the Arabs: "*Sarra'an lahu malakut al-Yaman wal-Iraq*" (a rapid [ruler] whose sovereignty is Yemen and Iraq).

Al-Kisa'i said: "The *ta'* was added to it for emphasis," and he recited:
"And the worst of men is the cheat, the deceiver [*al-khalbut*]" [[Kitab al-'Ayn: 4/271.]].

'Ikrimah said: "It is the sovereignty, except that in Nabataean it is *malkuta*." He read it with a dotted *ya'* as *maliyyan* (meaning sovereignty).

Ibn 'Abbas said: "It means the creation of the heavens and the earth."

Mujahid and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "It means the signs of the heavens and the earth. That is because he was raised up on a rock, and the heavens and the earth were uncovered for him, even the Throne and the lowest part of the earth, and he looked at his place in Paradise."

This is the meaning of His words ﴿And We gave him his reward in this world﴾ [al-'Ankabut 27]: that is, We showed him his place in Paradise.

Qatadah said: Abraham (peace be upon him) said to himself that he was the most merciful of creation. So God, the Mighty and Majestic, raised him until he overlooked the people of the earth and saw their deeds. When he saw them committing acts of disobedience, he said to God: "Destroy them!" and he began to curse them. His Lord said to him: "I am more merciful to My servants than you. Descend, perhaps they will repent."

Qays ibn Abi Hazim narrated from 'Ali, may God honor his face, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "When God, the Exalted, showed Abraham the dominion of the heavens and the earth, he overlooked a man committing one of the sins against God, so he invoked God against him and he perished. Then he overlooked another and invoked God against him and he perished. Then he overlooked another, and when he wanted to invoke against him, God, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed to him: 'O Abraham, you are a man whose supplication is answered. So do not invoke against My servants, for they are in relation to Me in three situations: either they repent to Me and I accept their repentance, or I bring forth from them a soul that glorifies Me, or they [return] to Me. If I wish, I pardon him, and if I wish, I punish him.'"

Al-Dahhak said: "*Malakut al-samawat wal-ard*" is the sun, the moon and the stars. Qatadah said: Abraham (peace be upon him) was hidden from one of the tyrants, and provision was made for him in his fingers: whenever he sucked one of his fingers, he found provision in it. When he came out, God showed him *malakut al-samawat wal-ard*. The *malakut* of the heavens is the sun, the moon and the stars, and the *malakut* of the earth is the mountains, the trees and the seas.

﴿And that he might be among the certain ones.﴾ ﴿So when the night covered him, he saw a star...﴾ up to the end of the verse.

The exegetes said: Abraham (peace be upon him) was born in the time of Nimrod ibn Kan'an. Nimrod was the first to place a crown on his head and to put a crown on himself, and he called the people [...]. He had soothsayers and astrologers.

They said: "In this year a boy will be born in your city who will change the religion of the people of the earth, and your destruction and the end of your rule will be at his hands." It is said that they found this in the books of the prophets, peace be upon them.

Al-Suddi said: Nimrod saw in his dream as if a star had risen and taken away the light of the sun and the moon until neither of them had any light. He was terrified by this, a great terror. He summoned the sorcerers, the soothsayers, the magicians and the physiognomists, and asked them about it. They said: "A child will be born in your region this year who will bring about the ruin of your kingdom and your household at his hands."

So he ordered that every boy born in his region that year be slain, and he ordered that men be separated from women, and he appointed a man over every ten [women]. Whenever a woman menstruated, he allowed her to be with him, and when she became pure, he separated her from him. Then Azar, the father of Abraham, returned and found his wife had become pure from menstruation, so he lay with her in her purity, and she conceived Abraham (peace be upon him).

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Nimrod sent to every pregnant woman in his town and detained her with him, except the mother of Abraham, for he did not know of her pregnancy, because she was a young girl who did not recognize pregnancy in her womb.

Al-Suddi said: Nimrod took the men out to the encampment and kept them away from the women, out of fear of that child who might be. He remained in this state as long as God willed. Then he had a need in the city, and he did not trust anyone among his people except Azar, so he sent for him and summoned him. He said: "I have a need of you, and I want to advise you concerning it. I am sending you only because I trust you. I swear to you that you must not approach your wife or lie with her." Azar said: "I am more protective of my religion than that." So he advised him concerning his need, then sent him. He entered the city and fulfilled his need. Then he said: "I entered upon my family and looked at him [the child]." When he looked at the mother of Abraham, he could not restrain himself until he lay with her, and she conceived Abraham.

Ibn 'Abbas said: When the mother of Abraham became pregnant, the soothsayers said to Nimrod: "The boy we told you about has been conceived by his mother tonight." So Nimrod ordered the slaying of the boys. When the mother of Abraham's delivery drew near and her labor pains seized her, she went out fleeing, fearing that someone would see her and kill her child. She placed him in a dry river, then wrapped him in a cloth and placed him among reeds. She returned and reported that she had given birth, and that the child was in such and such a place. Azar went to take him from that place. He dug a tunnel for him beside a river and hid him in it, and sealed its entrance with a rock out of fear of wild beasts. His mother used to visit him and nurse him.

Al-Suddi said: When the belly of the mother of Abraham grew large, Azar feared that [the child] would be slaughtered, so he took her to a land between Kufa and Basra called Urmah. He lodged her in a tunnel in the earth and put water beside them both. He used to visit her secretly, hiding that from his companions. She gave birth in that tunnel, and he grew up. When he was one year old, he was like a three-year-old, and he became a youth, out of fear that [he would fall into] the greed of the slaughterers. Then Azar mentioned to his companions that he had a grown son, and he took him out to them.

Ibn Ishaq said: When the mother of Abraham felt the pains of labor, she went out at night to a cave near her and gave birth to Abraham in it. She tended to his needs as is done for a newborn, then sealed the cave and returned to her house. Then she would look in on him in the cave to see what had happened, and she would find him alive, sucking his thumb.

Abu Rawq said: Whenever the mother of Abraham entered upon Abraham, she found him sucking his fingers. One day she said: "I will look at his fingers." She found him sucking from one finger water, from another honey, from another milk, from another dates, and from another ghee.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Azar had asked the mother of Abraham what had happened with her pregnancy. She said: "I gave birth to a boy, and he died." So he believed her and remained silent about it. A day for Abraham in youth was like a month, and a month like a year. Abraham did not remain in the cave except for fifteen months. Then he returned to his father Azar, and he told him that he was his son, and his mother told him that he was his son, and she informed him of what she had done during his absence. Azar was delighted by that and rejoiced greatly.

They said: Abraham grew up while he was in the tunnel, after he had said to his mother: "Who is my Lord?" She said: "I am." He said: "Then who is your lord?" She said: "Your father." He said: "Then who is the lord of my father?" She said to him: "Be quiet." So he was quiet. When she returned to her husband, she said: "Did you see the boy about whom we used to talk, that he would be of a religion other than that of the people of the earth? He is your son." Then she told him what [Abraham] had said to her. Then his father Azar came to him, and Abraham said to him: "O my father, who is my Lord?" He said: "Your mother." He said: "Then who is my mother's lord?" He said: "I am." He said: "Then who is your lord?" He said: "Nimrod." He said: "Then who is the lord of Nimrod?" So [Azar] slapped him a slap and said: "Be quiet and get up!" He said to his parents: "Take me out." So they took him out of the tunnel. They set out with him when the sun had set. Abraham looked at the camels, the horses and the sheep, and said: "Father, what are these?" He said: "Camels, horses and sheep." He said: "These must have a lord and a creator." Then he looked and reflected on the creation of the heavens and the earth. He said: "The One who created me, provided for me, fed me and gave me drink, He is my Lord; I have no god besides Him." Then he looked, and behold, Jupiter had risen, and it is said Venus; that night was at the end of the month, so he saw the star before the moon. He said: ﴿This is my lord.﴾

That is His words, mighty and majestic: ﴿So when the night covered him﴾, that is, it entered. It is said: *janna al-layl* and *ajanna*, and *janahu al-layl* and *ajannahu*, and *janna 'alayhi al-layl yajunnu junuunan wa jinanan* when it grew dark and everything passed away. The jinn are so called because they are hidden [*ijtinan*], so they are not seen.

Abu 'Ubaydah said: *junun al-layl* is its blackness. He recited:
"Had it not been for the darkness of night, the pursuit of our riders would have overtaken him, at Dhu al-Ramth and al-Arta, 'Iyad ibn Nashib" [[al-Sihah: 5/2094, where it reads "rikabuna" (our riders); Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 7/25. *Al-Ramth* with a kasra is the pasture of camels, and *al-Arta* is a tree that grows in sand.]].

﴿And he saw a star, [and] said, "This is my lord."﴾ They differed concerning it. Some of them took it according to its apparent meaning and said: Abraham (peace be upon him) was not one who sought guidance, bewildered, seeking success, until God granted him success and gave him his rectitude. This statement of his was made in his childhood, before the proof was established against him. In that condition one would say that neither disbelief nor faith exists.

Evidence for this is what 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "When ﴿the night covered him, he saw a star, [and] said, 'This is my lord.'﴾ He worshipped it until it set. When it set, he said, ﴿'I do not like those that set.'﴾ When he saw the moon rising, he said, ﴿'This is my lord,'﴾ and worshipped it until it set. When it set, ﴿'If my Lord does not guide me, I will surely be among the people who are astray.'﴾ When he saw the sun rising, he said, ﴿'This is my lord; this is greater,'﴾ and worshipped it until the sun set. When it set, he said: ﴿'O my people, indeed I am free from what you associate.'﴾"

Others rejected this view and said: It is not permissible that a messenger of God should come upon a time when he was not monotheistic, knowing, and free from every worshipped other than Him.

They said: How could they accuse him of this, when God protected and purified him in his place of rest and his place of storage, and granted him his rectitude beforehand, and showed him His dominion, and He said: ﴿when he came to his Lord with a sound heart﴾ [al-Saffat 84], and He said: ﴿And thus We showed Abraham the dominion of the heavens and the earth, that he might be among the certain﴾ [al-An'am 75]? "He saw a star and said, 'This is my lord,'" based on belief and reality? This is something that could never happen.

Then four interpretations were given of it. The first interpretation: Abraham (peace be upon him) wanted to lead them step by step with this statement, to make them recognize their error and ignorance in exalting what they exalted, and to establish the proof against them, and to show them that he exalted what they exalted, and sought guidance from where they sought it. When [the star] set, he showed them the deficiency inherent in the stars, so they would see the error of what they claimed. They used to exalt the stars, worship them, and treat them as judges.

They said: The likeness of this is like the disciple (*al-hawari*) who came to a people who worshipped their idol, and he showed them its greatness, and they were guided by his opinion in many matters, until an enemy of theirs, whom the king feared for his kingdom, reproached them, and the king consulted the disciple about his affair.

They said [to the disciple]: "Our opinion is that you should call upon our god so that what has misled us may be removed, for we are gathered for such a day." So they gathered around it, crying out and supplicating, while their enemy hurried and relied [on that]. When it became clear to them that their lord neither benefits nor harms, he said to them, in the form of a question and a reproach for their action: ﴿This is my lord?﴾ And could such a thing be a lord? That is, this is not my lord, like God's words ﴿'Or you will be among the immortals'﴾ [al-A'raf 20], meaning that they are the immortals.

And like Moses' words to Pharaoh: ﴿And is it a favor of which you remind me that you have enslaved the children of Israel?﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 22], meaning: "Or is it a favor that you have granted?"
