So Abu Sufyan, Abu Jahl, al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, Umayya and Ubayy ibn Khalaf, 'Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt, 'Amr ibn al-'As, and al-Aswad ibn al-Muttalib set out to Abu Talib and said: "O Abu Talib, you are our elder and our chief, and Muhammad has harmed us and harmed our gods. We wish that you would call him and restrain him from mentioning our gods, and we will leave him and his God." So he called him, and the Prophet ﷺ came. Abu Talib said to him: "These are your people and your paternal cousins." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "What do they want?" They said: "We want you to leave us and our gods, and we will leave you and your God."

He said: "Your people have been fair; accept from them." The Prophet ﷺ said: "Do you see, if I give you this, will you give me a single word, which if you speak it, you will rule the Arabs and the non-Arabs will submit to you through it?"

Abu Jahl said: "Yes, by your father, we will give it to you and ten like it. What is it?" He said: "Say: There is no god but Allah." They refused and recoiled.

Abu Talib said: "Say something other than it, O my nephew, for your people have been alarmed by it." He said: "O uncle, I am not one who would say anything other than it; even if they brought me the sun and placed it in my hand, I would not say anything other than it."

﴿without knowledge﴾

When this verse was revealed, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to his companions: "Do not revile their Lord," and the Muslims refrained from reviling their gods.

﴿And thus We have made fair-seeming to every community their deeds﴾ — meaning: just as We made fair-seeming to these polytheists the worship of idols and obedience to Satan, [We made fair-seeming to them] deprivation and abandonment. ﴿Thus We have made fair-seeming to every community their deeds﴾ — of good and evil, obedience and disobedience. ﴿Then to their Lord is their return, and He will inform them﴾ — He will inform them and recompense them ﴿of what they used to do.﴾

﴿And they swore by Allah their most emphatic oaths.﴾

Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi and al-Kalbi said: The Quraysh said: "O Muhammad, you inform us that Moses had a staff with which he struck the rock, and from it burst twelve springs; and you inform us that Jesus used to revive the dead; and you inform us that Thamud had a she-camel. So bring us signs, that we may believe you." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "What would you like me to bring you?"

They said: "Make Safa gold for us, and send us some of our dead so that we may ask them about you, whether what you say is true or false; and show us the angels bearing witness for you, or bring Allah and the angels before us as a group." Then Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿And they swore by Allah their most emphatic oaths﴾ — meaning the strongest oaths they were able to make, by themselves.

Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: When a man swears by Allah, the Sublime, he is making his oath most emphatic. ﴿If a sign came to them, they would surely believe in it﴾ — like those nations before them. ﴿Say: Signs are only with Allah﴾ — O Muhammad — and He is able to bring them, besides me and besides every one of His creation. Then He said: ﴿And what will make you realize?﴾ — that is, what will inform you? The object is omitted: "And what will make you realize [that they will not believe]?" They differed regarding the addressees of ﴿what will make you realize﴾, according to their differing readings of ﴿that﴾. Some said: The address is to the polytheists who swore, and the speech is complete at ﴿what will make you realize,﴾ then it resumes, saying: ﴿that when they come, they will not believe﴾ — the signs, judging that they will not believe.

They read ʾinnahā with a kasra, as a new sentence, and this is the reading of Mujahid, Qatadah, Ibn Muhaysin, Ibn Kathir, Shibl, Abu 'Amr and al-Jahdari.

Others said: The address is to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his companions, and they read ʾannahā with a fatha, taking "lā" as superfluous, meaning: "And what will make you realize, O assembly of believers, that when they come to the polytheists, they will not believe?" like His saying: ﴿What prevented you from prostrating?﴾ [Surah al-A'raf: 12], meaning: "that you prostrate"; and His saying: ﴿And it is forbidden for a town which We destroyed that they will not return﴾ [Surah al-Anbiya: 95], meaning: "that they will return." It was also said: the meaning of ʾannahā is "perhaps" (la'alla), and so is the reading of Ubayy. The Arabs say: "Go to the market, you may buy something," meaning "perhaps you will pass by."

'Adi ibn Zayd said:

"O blamer, what will make you know that my death is at an hour in the day or in the forenoon of tomorrow?"

meaning: perhaps my death.

Durayd ibn al-Simma said:

"Leave me to roam the lands, for I see what you see, or a miserly one, eternal..."

meaning: perhaps I.

Abu al-Najm said:

"I said to Sinan: Come near to his meeting, for we feed the people from his gladness,"

meaning: a fox we feed.

Ibn 'Amir, al-Suddi and Hamza read ﴿lā yu'minūna﴾ with the ta' (you), addressing the disbelievers, ﴿And what will make you realize﴾; and they considered the reading of Ubayy: "Perhaps you, when they come to you, will not believe." The rest read it with the ya' (they), as a statement; and the reading of al-A'mash confirms it: "that when they come to them, they will not believe."

﴿And We will turn their hearts and their sights away, just as they did not believe in it the first time.﴾

Ibn 'Abbas and Ibn Zayd said: meaning: We will prevent them from belief. Had We brought them the signs they asked for, they would not have believed in them, just as they did not believe in those before, such as the splitting of the moon and other things, as a punishment for them for that.

It was also said: just as they did not believe in it in the world before their death. Its parallel is His saying: ﴿And if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden﴾ [Surah al-An'am: 28].

﴿And We leave them﴾ — Abu Raja read "wa-yadharuhum" with the ya'. An-Nakha'i read "wa-yuqallibu" and "wa-yadharuhum," both with the ya', ﴿in their transgression, wandering blindly.﴾

﴿And even if We had sent down to them the angels and the dead had spoken to them﴾ by Our reviving them, so they bore witness to you of prophethood as they asked, ﴿and We gathered against them every thing before them﴾ — with a kasra on the qaf and a fatha on the ba', meaning: face to face (ʿiyānan), and this is the reading of most reciters. Abu Ja'far read the one in al-An'am as "qiblan" with a kasra, and the one in al-Kahf "qubulan" with a damma, meaning "face to face." Abu 'Amr read it with a fatha, and so Abu 'Ubayd and Abu Hatim chose, because in the reading of Ubayy it is "qabilan," gathering the qabl. The one in al-Kahf, "qubulan," means "face to face."

The people of Kufa read with a damma on both the qaf and the ba', and it has three possible meanings: First, that it is the plural of qabil, meaning guarantor, i.e., they became sureties and guarantors. The qabala is the surety; it is said qabil and qabl, like raghif and raghf, and qadib and qadb.

Second, the plural of qabil, meaning tribe, i.e., group by group and kind by kind.

Third, that it means confrontation and facing, from the saying of one who says: "I came to you qablan, not dabran," when he came to him from the front of his face.

﴿They would not have believed unless Allah willed it.﴾ That is, that is for them. It was also said: the exception is for the people of happiness whose faith preceded in Allah's knowledge. ﴿But most of them are ignorant.﴾ That is so.

﴿And thus We made for every prophet before you an enemy﴾ — consoling His Prophet ﷺ, meaning: just as We brought you these people, so We made for every prophet before you enemies, and He explained them, saying: ﴿devils of mankind and jinn.﴾

Ikrimah, al-Dahhak, al-Suddi and al-Kalbi said: its meaning is: the devils of mankind who are with mankind, and the devils of the jinn who are with the jinn; and there are no devils among mankind.

That is because Iblis divided his army into two groups, sending one group to mankind and one group to the jinn, the devils of mankind and the jinn; they meet at all times, and the devil of mankind says to the devil of the jinn: "I have misled my companion with such-and-such; mislead yours with its like," and the devil of the jinn says the same to the devil of mankind. ﴿So some of them inspire to others﴾ — that is it.

Others said: Among mankind there are devils, and among the jinn there are devils; and the devil is the obstinate, rebellious one of every kind.

They said: When the devil misleads a believer and fails to mislead him, he goes to a rebellious man among mankind, who is a devil of mankind, and the believer overcomes him.

Abu Talha said, regarding what 'Awf ibn Malik narrated from Abu Dharr, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "O Abu Dharr, have you sought refuge in Allah from the evil of the devils of mankind and the jinn?" He said: "O Messenger of Allah, do mankind have devils?" He said: "Yes, it is worse than the devils of the jinn."

The Prophet ﷺ also said: "There is none of you but has a companion from the jinn assigned to him." It was said: "And not you, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Nor I, except that Allah has helped me against him, so he has embraced Islam, and he commands me only to good."

Malik ibn Dinar said: The devil of mankind is worse than the devil of the jinn, because when I seek refuge in Allah, the devil of the jinn leaves me, but the devil of mankind loves me and drags me openly into sins. ﴿They inspire one another with ornate speech as deception﴾ — that is, the deceptive speech adorned with falsehood; and everything you make good and adorn, you have embellished (zakhrafta). ﴿And had your Lord willed, they would not have done it, so leave them and what they fabricate.﴾ ﴿And that the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter may incline to it﴾ — that is, that they may be inclined to it (wa-litasgha ay wa-litamīl).

Ibn 'Abbas said: it means "return" (tarji'u). It is said: "saghā yasghā sagh'an and sagā yasghā wa-yasgū sagwan wa-sagwan" when he inclined. Al-Fitami said:

"They inclined to him, their necks in the sides of their jaws; their ears follow the drivers' whip,
their eye looks sidelong at the corner of her eye, watching my palm and the herd, restrained."

Meaning: to it — to the ornament and the deception. It is said: "Sagwu so-and-so is with you," and "sagahu with you," meaning his inclination and desire.

An-Nakha'i read "wa-litusgha" with a damma on the ta' and a kasra on the ghayn, meaning: incline; and al-isgha' is inclination. From it, the hadith: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to tilt the vessel for the cat.

﴿...the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter, and that they may be pleased with it, and that they may commit what they are committing.﴾ The afida is the plural of fu'ad, like ghurab and aghriba. ﴿And that they may be pleased with it and that they may earn what they are earning﴾ — that is, that they may acquire what they acquire.

Ibn Zayd said: that they may act upon what they are doing. It is said: "iqtaraf so-and-so money," meaning he acquired it; and "qarafa so-and-so this matter" when he engaged in it and did it. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And whoever earns a good deed﴾ [Surah al-Shura: 23].

Labid said:

"I come to what I have come to, and indeed I, for what my soul has earned, am a fearful monk."

It was also said: it is from accusation; it is said: "qarafahu bi-su'" when he accused him of it.

Ru'ba said:

"The earning of the attributed lie has wearied the piety of the pious and the chastity of the chaste."

And do not revile those whom they call upon besides Allah, lest they revile Allah in enmity without knowledge.

Ibn 'Abbas said: When this verse was revealed, ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are fuel for Hell﴾ [Surah al-Anbiya: 98].

The polytheists said: "O Muhammad, either you desist from reviling our gods, or we will revile your Lord." So Allah the Exalted forbade them to revile their idols.

Qatadah said: The Muslims used to revile the idols of the disbelievers, so Allah forbade them from that, lest they revile Allah, for they are an ignorant people.

As-Suddi said: When Abu Talib was on the verge of death, the Quraysh said: "Come, let us enter upon this man and order him to restrain his nephew from us, for we are ashamed to kill him after his death, lest the Arabs say: 'He used to protect him, and when he died, they killed him.'" So Abu Sufyan, Abu Jahl, al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, Umayya and Ubayy ibn Khalaf, 'Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt, 'Amr ibn al-'As, and al-Aswad ibn al-Muttalib set out to Abu Talib and said: "O Abu Talib, you are our elder and our chief, and Muhammad has harmed us and harmed our gods. We wish that you would call him and restrain him from mentioning our gods, and we will leave him and his God." So he called him, and the Prophet ﷺ came. Abu Talib said to him: "These are your people and your paternal cousins." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "What do they want?" They said: "We want you to leave us and our gods, and we will leave you and your God."

He said: "Your people have been fair; accept from them." The Prophet ﷺ said: "Do you see, if I give you this, will you give me a single word, which if you speak it, you will rule the Arabs and the non-Arabs will submit to you through it?"

Abu Jahl said: "Yes, by your father, we will give it to you and ten like it. What is it?" He said: "Say: There is no god but Allah." They refused and recoiled.

Abu Talib said: "Say something other than it, O my nephew, for your people have been alarmed by it." He said: "O uncle, I am not one who would say anything other than it; even if they brought me the sun and placed it in my hand, I would not say anything other than it."

They said: "Either you cease reviling our gods, or we will revile the one who commands you." So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿And do not revile those whom they call upon besides Allah﴾ — among the idols — ﴿lest they revile Allah in enmity﴾.

Abu Raja, al-Hasan, Qatadah and Ya'qub read ʿuduwwan with a damma on the ʿayn and the dal and a shadda on the waw, meaning "enemies of Allah."

﴿without knowledge﴾

When this verse was revealed, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to his companions: "Do not revile their Lord," and the Muslims refrained from reviling their gods.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 6, verses 114–119:

His saying, ﴿Shall I seek a judge other than God?﴾ contains an ellipsis (idmar); that is, say to them, O Muhammad: "Shall I seek other than God as a judge (qadi) between me and you? ﴿It is He who has sent down to you the Book, fully detailed﴾," that is, clarified. ﴿And those to whom We have given the Book﴾ means the Torah and the Gospel, and they are the believers among the People of the Book.

ʿAṭāʾ said: They are the companions of the Prophet ﷺ: Abu Bakr, ʿUmar, ʿUthman, ʿAli and their followers, may God be pleased with them. The Book is the Qur'an.

﴿Know that it is sent down﴾, that is, the Qur'an, ﴿from your Lord in truth. So do not be among the doubters.﴾

al-Hasan, al-Aʿmash and Abu ʿAmir read ﴿munazzal﴾ with doubled (tashdid) zay, from tanzil, because it was sent down in stages, time after time.

The rest read it with a single zay (takhfif), from inzal, based on His saying, ﴿Our Lord has sent it down to you in truth﴾.

﴿And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled in truth and justice.﴾ The people of Kufa read ﴿kalimatu﴾ in the singular, while the rest read ﴿kalimat﴾ in the plural. They differed over the meaning of "words."

Qatada said: They are the Qur'an; none can alter it. The distorters neither add to it nor subtract from it.

Others said: They are His decrees and His justice. ﴿None can change His words﴾, that is, none can alter them. ﴿And He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.﴾

﴿And if you obey most of those on earth, they will lead you astray from the way of God﴾, that is, the disbelievers will lead you away from the religion of God. Then He said: ﴿They follow only conjecture, and they are only guessing (yakhrusun)﴾, that is, they lie. ﴿Indeed your Lord knows best who strays from His way.﴾

Some said: The position (mawdi') is accusative (nasb), because the preposition is elided, which is the particle of attribution, i.e., "bi-man" (with whom).

It was also said: its position is nominative (raf'), since it carries the sense of "ayy" (which), and the verb "liyadill" governs it.

It was also said: its position is accusative because knowledge falls upon it, and aʿlam here means "yaʿlam" (knows), as in the saying of Hatim al-Ta'i:

"So Tayyi' allied itself with others besides us, and God knows we did not forsake them."

And al-Khansa' said:

"The people know that his generous pot will be boiled at dawn in the wind or at night."

﴿And He knows best who are guided.﴾

So ﴿eat of that over which the name of God has been pronounced﴾.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: The polytheists said to the believers: "You worship God; what, then, has God caused to die?" Meaning: "Is the truth that you eat what you kill with your knives?" So God revealed: ﴿Eat of that over which the name of God has been pronounced﴾ at the time of slaughter, meaning the slaughtered animal (mudhakkah) over which one says "in the name of God," ﴿if you are believers in His signs.﴾ ﴿And what is it with you that you do not eat of that over which the name of God has been pronounced?﴾, that is, what prevents you from not eating of the slaughtered animals ﴿when He has already detailed for you what He has forbidden to you.﴾

al-Hasan, Abu Raja' [al-A'raj], Qatada, al-Jubba'i, Talha, Mujahid, Humayd and the people of Medina read ﴿fassala﴾ and ﴿hurrima﴾ with fatha, meaning that God has detailed what He forbade to you, based on His saying ﴿ism Allah﴾, the mention of which has passed (referring to God, the Exalted).

Muhammad ibn ʿAmir and Abu ʿAmr read both with damma, as passive (ghayr tasmiyat al-fa'il), based on His saying ﴿dhukira﴾.

The companions of ʿAbdullah and the people of Kufa read ﴿fassala﴾ with fatha and ﴿yuharrama﴾ with damma.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 6, verses 120–126:

﴿Forsake the outward and the inward of sin﴾: that is, all sins. It cannot fall outside these two aspects.

They differed over it. Qatada said: its secret and its open form. ʿAtaʾ said: its little and its much. Mujahid said: what one intends and what one actually does. al-Kalbi said: ﴿the outward of sin﴾ is fornication, and ﴿the inward of it﴾ is taking a female companion (al-mukhala).

As-Suddi said: the prostitutes of the shops, which were the houses of the owners of banners, and ﴿the inward of it﴾ is the mistress whom a man takes and visits in secret.[[Tafsir al-Tabari: 8/20.]] Murra al-Hamdani said: the Arabs used to permit fornication. A nobleman who committed it would conceal it, while others did not care if they committed it openly. So Allah revealed this verse.

ad-Dahhak said: the people of the Jahiliyyah (Age of Ignorance) would conceal fornication and consider it lawful as long as it was secret. So Allah forbade this community both its secret and its open forms.

Hayyan narrated from al-Kalbi: ﴿the outward of sin﴾ is men circling the Ka'bah naked by day, and ﴿the inward of it﴾ is women circling it naked by night.

Saʿid ibn Jubayr said: the outward is what Allah forbade in His words: ﴿And do not marry those whom your fathers married of women﴾,[[Surah an-Nisa': 22.]] and His words: ﴿Forbidden to you are your mothers﴾[[Surah an-Nisa': 23.]] and the rest of the verse. The inward of it is fornication.

Ibn Zayd said: ﴿the outward of sin﴾ is nakedness and stripping off clothing during circumambulation, and the inward is fornication.

﴿Indeed, those who earn sin﴾ will be recompensed in the Hereafter ﴿for what they used to commit﴾, meaning for what they earn in the Hereafter.

Ibn Zayd said: by this light is meant Islam, corresponding to His words: ﴿He brings them out of darknesses into the light﴾.

Qatada said: this believer has with him light and a proof from Allah, by which he acts and to which the Book of Allah leads. ﴿Like one whose example is in darknesses﴾.

Some of them said: the word "example" is superfluous, and its implied meaning is "like one who is in darknesses."

Others said: its meaning is "be like" or "resemble something," which the one in darknesses resembles, namely the darkness of disbelief, ignorance, misguidance and wandering. ﴿He will not emerge from them﴾: he cannot see anything and does not know a path, like one who has lost his way in the darkness of the night, so he finds no exit and is not guided to a path.

It was said: this verse was revealed concerning two specific men, and then they differed about them.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: ﴿Is one who was dead and We gave him life, and made for him a light by which he walks among the people﴾ refers to Hamzah ibn ʿAbd al-Muttalib; ﴿like one whose example is in darknesses, not emerging from them﴾ refers to Abu Jahl. This is because:

Abu Jahl threw stones at the Prophet (ﷺ). Hamzah had not yet embraced Islam. Hamzah was informed of what Abu Jahl had done while he was returning from his hunting, with a bow in his hand. He came angrily and struck Abu Jahl with the bow, while Abu Jahl was humbling himself like a wretched slave, saying: "O Abu Yaʿla, do you not see what he has brought? He has made our minds foolish, reviled our gods, and opposed our father."

Hamzah said: "And who is more foolish than you, who worship stones instead of Allah? I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, He has no partner, and that Muhammad is His servant and messenger." So Allah revealed this verse.

ad-Dahhak and Yaman said: it was revealed concerning ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab and Abu Jahl.

ʿIkrimah and al-Kalbi said: it was revealed concerning ʿAmmar ibn Yasir and Abu Jahl.

﴿Thus the deeds of the disbelievers have been made attractive to them﴾, that is, the disbelief and disobedience they do. ﴿And thus﴾, meaning: just as We made their deeds attractive to the disbelievers, so We have done.

It was said: just as We placed the great ones among the wrongdoers of Makkah, so ﴿We placed in every town its greatest criminals﴾, meaning its great ones. The word ʾakābir is the plural of akbar, like afdal and ahmar, and aḥāmir, aswad and asāwid. ﴿Its criminals﴾: if you wish, you may put it in the accusative as a preposed object, its implied meaning being: "and thus We placed in every town its criminals as great ones," just as you say: "I made Zayd its chief." And if you wish, you may put it in the genitive by way of annexation.

﴿So that they may plot therein﴾ ﴿and they plot not except against themselves﴾, because the harm of their plotting and its punishment returns to them. ﴿And they are not aware﴾ that this is so.

﴿And when a sign comes to them, they say: "We will not believe until we are given what the messengers of Allah were given."﴾ That is, prophethood. This is because al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah said: "By Allah, if prophethood were true, I would be more deserving of it than you, for I am older than you and have more wealth than you." So Allah revealed this verse.

Muqatil said: it was revealed concerning Abu Jahl ibn Hisham, because he said: "ʿAbd Manaf competed with us in nobility until, when we became like two horses in a race, they said: 'Among us is a prophet to whom revelation comes.' By Allah, we will never believe in him or follow him, unless revelation comes to us as it comes to him." Allah revealed: ﴿And when a sign comes to them﴾, a proof for the truthfulness of Muhammad (ﷺ) and the soundness of his prophethood. ﴿They say﴾, meaning Abu Jahl and others: ﴿We will not believe until we are given what the messengers of Allah were given﴾, meaning Muhammad, the messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Then He said: ﴿Allah knows best where to place His message﴾, so He singled out Muhammad (ﷺ) for it. ﴿Those who committed crime will be struck with humiliation, meaning degradation and disgrace, ﴿from Allah﴾, that is, from the presence of Allah. It is in the accusative, by removal of the preposition.

an-Nahhas said: ﴿Those who committed crime will be struck with humiliation before Allah﴾ is with preposing and postposing, ﴿and a severe punishment for what they used to plot.﴾

Abu Rawq said: the humiliation is in this world, and this punishment is in the Hereafter.

﴿So whoever Allah wills to guide, He opens his breast to Islam﴾, that is, He widens his intellect or illumines it so that he accepts Islam. So Allah revealed this verse.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about the expansion of the breast: what is it? He said: "It is a light that Allah casts into the heart of the believer, so his breast is expanded and widened by it." They said: "Is there any sign by which it may be known?" He said: "Yes: turning towards the abode of eternity, withdrawing from the abode of delusion, and preparing for death before death comes."[157] [[Zad al-Masir: 3/82, where it says: "before its coming."]]

﴿And whoever Allah wills to lead astray, He makes his breast tight and constricted﴾. Ibn Kathir recited ḍayyiqan with the lightened form, while the rest recited it with the doubled form, and both are dialectal variants, like hayyin and hayyin, and layyin and layyin. ﴿Constricted (ḥarajan)﴾: the people of Madinah read its rāʾ with a kasra, and the others read it with a fatha, and both are dialectal variants, like al-anf and al-anf, al-fard and al-fard, al-waʿd and al-waʿd.

Sibawayh said: ḥaraj with a fatha is the verbal noun, like ṣalb and ḥalb, and its meaning is "possessing constriction." Ḥaraj with a kasra is the noun, and it is the most severe constriction. The meaning is: He makes his heart narrow, not admitting faith.

It was said: ḥarajan means sinful, from the saying of the Arabs: ḥaraja ʿalayka ḍalmī, meaning constricted and sinful. As-Suddi said: its ḥaraj means doubting. Qatada said: entangled. an-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: ḥaraj means "closed off," meaning that good has no outlet into it.

ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr said: Ibn ʿAbbas recited this verse and said: "Is there anyone here from the Banu Bakr?" A man said: "Yes." He said: "What is the ḥaraj among you?" He said: "A valley thick with trees, interlaced, with no path through it." Ibn ʿAbbas said: "Thus is the heart of the disbeliever."

Abu as-Salt ath-Thaqafi and ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) said regarding this verse: ḍayyiqan ḥarajan with the rāʾ in the accusative. Some of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) who were with them read ḥarijan with a kasra. ʿUmar said: "Send for a man from Kinanah and make him a shepherd." They brought him, and ʿUmar said to him: "O young man, what is the ḥarajah among you?" He said: "The ḥarajah among us is the tree that grows among other trees, which no grazing animal, no wild beast, and nothing else can reach."

ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "Thus is the heart of the hypocrite; nothing of good reaches it."

﴿As if he were climbing up into the sky﴾: that is, faith is hard for him, and he refuses it and is unable to attain it, just as it is hard for him to climb up into the sky.

The reciters differed about this. The people of Madinah, Abu ʿAmr, Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read yaṣṣaʿḍu with a doubled ṣād and ʿayn and without an alif, meaning yaṣʿadu, with the tāʾ assimilated into the ṣād. Abu Hatim and Abu ʿUbayd preferred this, supporting it with the recitation of ʿAbdullah: kaʾannamā yataṣaʿʿadu fī as-samāʾ.

Ṭalḥah, ʿĀṣim, Abu ʿUbayd, an-Nakhaʿi and Mujahid read it with an alif and a doubled ʿayn, meaning tasaʿʿada.[[See Tafsir al-Tabari: 8/42.]]

Ibn Kaysan, Ibn Muḥayṣin, al-Aʿraj and Abu Rajaʾ read yaṣʿudu, in its literal sense.[[That is, from as-suʿud (ascent).]]

﴿Thus Allah places filth upon those who do not believe.﴾ Mujahid said: ar-rijs is what has no good in it. Ibn Zayd said: ar-rijs is punishment, like ar-rijz. Ibn ʿAbbas said: it is the devil whom Allah sets upon him. al-Kalbi said: it is sin; it was also said: it is impurity. It is said: rajs, rijās, and najs, najāsah.[[See Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 7/83.]]

When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered the lavatory, he would say: "O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the male and female impure devils, the evil, the Satan who is accursed."[[Jami' al-Bayan: 8/43, with variation and difference.]][158]

﴿And this is the path of your Lord, straight﴾: that is, this which We have made clear is the path of your Lord, which He has approved as a religion for Himself, and made straight with no crookedness in it. It is Islam.

Ibn Masʿud said: it is the Qur'an. He also said: the path is attended; the devils attend it, calling out: "O servant of Allah, come, this is the way." ﴿To turn people away from the way of Allah﴾. ﴿So hold fast to the rope of Allah﴾, which is the Book of Allah. ﴿We have detailed the verses for a people who remember.﴾

The House of Peace (Dar al-Salam) is theirs with their Lord, meaning Paradise in the Hereafter.

Most exegetes (tafsir) said: "al-Salam" is God, Mighty and Majestic, and His house is Paradise. It has also been said that Paradise was named Dar al-Salam because it is free from calamities and defects.

It has also been said: because whoever enters it is safe from all trials and misfortunes.

It has also been said: because its inhabitants are spared the presence of God's enemies, so that God's friends are not troubled in it, as their companionship with such enemies troubles them in this world.

It has also been said: it was so named because every state of its people is linked with peace. As for the beginning of their entry, it is His words: ﴿Enter it in peace, secure﴾ [Qur'an 15:46]. After that, His words: ﴿and the angels will enter upon them from every gate﴾ [Qur'an 13:23–24]. Then His words: ﴿and their greeting therein is "Peace"﴾ [Qur'an 14:23]. Then His words: ﴿They will not hear therein any idle talk or sin, but only the saying "Peace, peace"﴾ [Surah Maryam: 62; Surah al-Waqi'ah: 25–26]. Then His words: ﴿Their greeting on the day they meet Him will be "Peace"﴾ [Surah al-Ahzab: 44]. And after that: ﴿"Peace," a word from a Lord, Most Merciful﴾ [Surah Yasin: 58]. Since the states of the people of Paradise are linked with peace, whether from the creatures or from the Truth, God named it the House of Peace.

﴿He is their Protector (Wali)﴾, that is, their helper and supporter, ﴿because of what they used to do﴾.

Al-Hasan ibn al-Fadl said: it means He takes charge of them in this world through success (tawfiq) and in the Hereafter through reward.

﴿And the day He will gather them all﴾, the jinn and mankind. He gathers them on the Day of Resurrection and says: ﴿"O company of jinn, you have taken much from mankind"﴾, that is, of misleading and seducing people. ﴿And their allies from mankind, who had obeyed them, will say: "Our Lord, some of us have enjoyed others"﴾.

Al-Kalbi said: the enjoyment of mankind from the jinn is that when a man travels or goes out and walks in a barren land, or catches some of their game, he fears for himself from them, so he says: "I seek refuge with the lord of this valley from the foolish ones of his people," and so he is granted protection from them. The enjoyment of the jinn from mankind is that they say: "We have been made masters over mankind and the jinn, since they seek refuge with us," so they gain more honor and greatness among their people. This is the meaning of His words, Exalted is He: ﴿And that there were men from mankind who sought refuge with men from the jinn﴾ [Qur'an 72:6], and so on.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b and Abd al-Aziz ibn Yahya said: it is the obedience of some of them to others and their agreement with one another. It has also been said: the enjoyment of mankind from the jinn is by what they brought to them, of false rumors, sorcery, and soothsaying, while the enjoyment of the jinn from mankind is their enticing the jinn and mankind's following them.

﴿And we have reached our appointed term which You appointed for us﴾, meaning death and resurrection. God, Exalted is He, said: ﴿The Fire is your dwelling, abiding therein forever, except what God wills﴾ [Qur'an 6:128], meaning: the span between their resurrection and their entry into Hell was determined.

Ibn Abbas said: this exception means that no one should pass judgment on God regarding His creatures, that He has not appointed for them either Paradise or Fire.

Al-Kalbi said: ﴿except what God wills﴾, and what God wills is forever.

It has also been said: its meaning is ﴿The Fire is your dwelling, abiding therein forever,﴾ apart from what God wills of the various kinds of punishment. It has also been said: ﴿except what God wills﴾ refers to God's bringing out the people of monotheism (tawhid) from the Fire.

It has also been said: ﴿except what God wills﴾ refers to His willing to increase their punishment therein.

It has also been said: ﴿except what God wills﴾ refers to their existence in this world without punishment.

Ata' said: ﴿except what God wills﴾ refers to the truth in His action, that some believe before the Conquest and some believe after the Conquest.

﴿Indeed your Lord is Wise, Knowing﴾. ﴿And thus We make some of the wrongdoers allies of others, because of what they used to earn﴾ [Qur'an 6:129].

It is reported from Qatadah: He makes some of them allies of others. The believer is an ally of the believer, and the disbeliever is an ally of the disbeliever, wherever they are.

Mu'ammar reported from Qatadah: they follow one another into the Fire through allegiance.

It has also been said: its meaning is that We make the wrongdoers among mankind allies of the wrongdoers among the jinn, and the wrongdoers among the jinn allies of the wrongdoers among mankind, meaning We leave some of them to others, like His words: ﴿We will leave him to what he has chosen﴾ [Qur'an 4:115].

Ibn Zayd said: We empower some of them over others. This is supported by the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Whoever helps a wrongdoer, God will empower him over him." [al-Jami' al-Saghir: 2/574, no. 8472.] [159]

Malik ibn Dinar said: I read in the revealed books of God that God, Exalted is He, said: "I will destroy My enemies by means of My enemies, then I will destroy them by means of My friends."

Hayyan reported from al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas, who said: its interpretation is that when God wills good for a people, He puts their affairs in the hands of their best, and when He wills evil for a people, He puts their affairs in the hands of their worst.

And in a report: God says: "I am God; there is no god but Me, the King of kings. The hearts and foreheads of kings are in My hand. Whoever obeys Me, I will make them a mercy upon him, and whoever disobeys Me, I will make them a vengeance upon him. So do not occupy yourselves with cursing the kings, but turn in repentance to God, Exalted is He, and He will incline them toward you."

﴿O company of jinn and mankind, did messengers not come to you from among yourselves?﴾ [Qur'an 6:130].

Al-A'raj and Ibn Abi Ishaq read ﴿ta'tikum﴾ with the letter ta' (تَأْتِكُمْ), as in His words: ﴿The messengers of our Lord have certainly come with the truth﴾ [Qur'an 7:43].

The rest of the readers read it with the letter ya' (يَأْتِكُمْ), as in His words: ﴿like what was given to the messengers of God﴾ [Qur'an 3:?] ... [the text as given contains a corrupted citation here] ... ﴿who recite to you My verses (يَقُصُّونَ عَلَيْكُمْ آياتِي) and warn you of the meeting of this your day﴾.

That is, the Day of Resurrection.

The scholars differed over whether messengers were sent to the jinn. Ubayd ibn Sulayman said: al-Dahhak was asked whether there were believers among the jinn before the Prophet (ﷺ) was sent. He said: "Have you not heard His words: ﴿O company of jinn and mankind, did messengers not come to you from among yourselves?﴾" He meant by this messengers from mankind and messengers from the jinn.

Al-Kalbi said: before the Prophet (ﷺ) was sent, messengers were sent to both the jinn and mankind together.

Mujahid said: the messengers were from mankind, and the warners were from the jinn, then he recited: ﴿and they returned to their people as warners﴾ [Qur'an 46:29].

Ibn Abbas said: they are those who listened to the Qur'an and conveyed it to their people.

Scholars of meanings (Ahl al-Ma'ani) said: there were no messengers from the jinn; rather, the messengers were from mankind only. This is like His words: ﴿From both of them come out pearls and coral﴾ [Qur'an 55:22], whereas they come out only from the salt water, not the fresh.

And His words: ﴿that they may mention the name of God on known days﴾ [Qur'an 22:28], which are the ten days, whereas the slaughter is only on one day of the ten, which is the day of sacrifice (al-nahr). And His words: ﴿and made the moon therein a light﴾ [Qur'an 71:16], whereas it is only in one heaven.

﴿They will say: "We bear witness against ourselves." The life of this world deceived them, and they bore witness against themselves that they had been disbelievers﴾ [Qur'an 6:130]. ﴿That is because your Lord would never destroy the towns unjustly, while their people were unaware﴾ [Qur'an 6:131], that is, due to the polytheism of those who associated partners with God, until He sends to them messengers to warn them. It has also been said: its meaning is that He would not destroy them without clear proof and reminder through messengers and signs, for then He would have wronged them.

﴿And for all there are degrees according to what they did﴾ [Qur'an 6:132], meaning in reward and punishment according to the measure of their deeds in this world. Some of them will have more severe punishment and some will have greater reward. ﴿And your Lord is not unaware of what they do﴾ [Qur'an 6:132].

Then His words: ﴿They will not hear therein any idle talk or sin, but only the saying "Peace, peace"﴾ [Surah Maryam: 62; Surah al-Waqi'ah: 25–26]. Then His words: ﴿Their greeting on the day they meet Him will be "Peace"﴾ [Surah al-Ahzab: 44]. And after that: ﴿"Peace," a word from a Lord, Most Merciful﴾ [Surah Yasin: 58]. Since the states of the people of Paradise are linked with peace, whether from the creatures or from the Truth, God named it the House of Peace.

﴿He is their Protector (Wali)﴾, that is, their helper and supporter, ﴿because of what they used to do﴾.

Al-Hasan ibn al-Fadl said: it means He takes charge of them in this world through success (tawfiq) and in the Hereafter through reward.

﴿And the day He will gather them all﴾, the jinn and mankind. He gathers them on the Day of Resurrection and says: ﴿"O company of jinn, you have taken much from mankind"﴾, that is, of misleading and seducing people. ﴿And their allies from mankind, who had obeyed them, will say: "Our Lord, some of us have enjoyed others"﴾.

Al-Kalbi said: the enjoyment of mankind from the jinn is that when a man travels or goes out and walks in a barren land, or catches some of their game, he fears for himself from them, so he says: "I seek refuge with the lord of this valley from the foolish ones of his people," and so he is granted protection from them. The enjoyment of the jinn from mankind is that they say: "We have been made masters over mankind and the jinn, since they seek refuge with us," so they gain more honor and greatness among their people. This is the meaning of His words, Exalted is He: ﴿And that there were men from mankind who sought refuge with men from the jinn﴾ [Qur'an 72:6], and so on.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b and Abd al-Aziz ibn Yahya said: it is the obedience of some of them to others and their agreement with one another. It has also been said: the enjoyment of mankind from the jinn is by what they brought to them, of false rumors, sorcery, and soothsaying, while the enjoyment of the jinn from mankind is their enticing the jinn and mankind's following them.

﴿And we have reached our appointed term which You appointed for us﴾, meaning death and resurrection. God, Exalted is He, said: ﴿The Fire is your dwelling, abiding therein forever, except what God wills﴾ [Qur'an 6:128], meaning: the span between their resurrection and their entry into Hell was determined.

Ibn Abbas said: this exception means that no one should pass judgment on God regarding His creatures, that He has not appointed for them either Paradise or Fire.

Al-Kalbi said: ﴿except what God wills﴾, and what God wills is forever.

It has also been said: its meaning is ﴿The Fire is your dwelling, abiding therein forever,﴾ apart from what God wills of the various kinds of punishment. It has also been said: ﴿except what God wills﴾ refers to God's bringing out the people of monotheism (tawhid) from the Fire.

It has also been said: ﴿except what God wills﴾ refers to His willing to increase their punishment therein.

It has also been said: ﴿except what God wills﴾ refers to their existence in this world without punishment.

Ata' said: ﴿except what God wills﴾ refers to the truth in His action, that some believe before the Conquest and some believe after the Conquest.

﴿Indeed your Lord is Wise, Knowing﴾. ﴿And thus We make some of the wrongdoers allies of others, because of what they used to earn﴾ [Qur'an 6:129].

It is reported from Qatadah: He makes some of them allies of others. The believer is an ally of the believer, and the disbeliever is an ally of the disbeliever, wherever they are.

Mu'ammar reported from Qatadah: they follow one another into the Fire through allegiance.

It has also been said: its meaning is that We make the wrongdoers among mankind allies of the wrongdoers among the jinn, and the wrongdoers among the jinn allies of the wrongdoers among mankind, meaning We leave some of them to others, like His words: ﴿We will leave him to what he has chosen﴾ [Qur'an 4:115].

Ibn Zayd said: We empower some of them over others. This is supported by the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Whoever helps a wrongdoer, God will empower him over him." [al-Jami' al-Saghir: 2/574, no. 8472.] [159]

Malik ibn Dinar said: I read in the revealed books of God that God, Exalted is He, said: "I will destroy My enemies by means of My enemies, then I will destroy them by means of My friends."

Hayyan reported from al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas, who said: its interpretation is that when God wills good for a people, He puts their affairs in the hands of their best, and when He wills evil for a people, He puts their affairs in the hands of their worst.

And in a report: God says: "I am God; there is no god but Me, the King of kings. The hearts and foreheads of kings are in My hand. Whoever obeys Me, I will make them a mercy upon him, and whoever disobeys Me, I will make them a vengeance upon him. So do not occupy yourselves with cursing the kings, but turn in repentance to God, Exalted is He, and He will incline them toward you."

﴿O company of jinn and mankind, did messengers not come to you from among yourselves?﴾ [Qur'an 6:130].

Al-A'raj and Ibn Abi Ishaq read ﴿ta'tikum﴾ with the letter ta' (تَأْتِكُمْ), as in His words: ﴿The messengers of our Lord have certainly come with the truth﴾ [Qur'an 7:43].

The rest of the readers read it with the letter ya' (يَأْتِكُمْ), as in His words: ﴿like what was given to the messengers of God﴾ [Qur'an 3:?] ... [the text as given contains a corrupted citation here] ... ﴿who recite to you My verses (يَقُصُّونَ عَلَيْكُمْ آياتِي) and warn you of the meeting of this your day﴾.

That is, the Day of Resurrection.

The scholars differed over whether messengers were sent to the jinn. Ubayd ibn Sulayman said: al-Dahhak was asked whether there were believers among the jinn before the Prophet (ﷺ) was sent. He said: "Have you not heard His words: ﴿O company of jinn and mankind, did messengers not come to you from among yourselves?﴾" He meant by this messengers from mankind and messengers from the jinn.

Al-Kalbi said: before the Prophet (ﷺ) was sent, messengers were sent to both the jinn and mankind together.

Mujahid said: the messengers were from mankind, and the warners were from the jinn, then he recited: ﴿and they returned to their people as warners﴾ [Qur'an 46:29].

Ibn Abbas said: they are those who listened to the Qur'an and conveyed it to their people.

Scholars of meanings (Ahl al-Ma'ani) said: there were no messengers from the jinn; rather, the messengers were from mankind only. This is like His words: ﴿From both of them come out pearls and coral﴾ [Qur'an 55:22], whereas they come out only from the salt water, not the fresh.

And His words: ﴿that they may mention the name of God on known days﴾ [Qur'an 22:28], which are the ten days, whereas the slaughter is only on one day of the ten, which is the day of sacrifice (al-nahr). And His words: ﴿and made the moon therein a light﴾ [Qur'an 71:16], whereas it is only in one heaven.

﴿They will say: "We bear witness against ourselves." The life of this world deceived them, and they bore witness against themselves that they had been disbelievers﴾ [Qur'an 6:130]. ﴿That is because your Lord would never destroy the towns unjustly, while their people were unaware﴾ [Qur'an 6:131], that is, due to the polytheism of those who associated partners with God, until He sends to them messengers to warn them. It has also been said: its meaning is that He would not destroy them without clear proof and reminder through messengers and signs, for then He would have wronged them.

﴿And for all there are degrees according to what they did﴾ [Qur'an 6:132], meaning in reward and punishment according to the measure of their deeds in this world. Some of them will have more severe punishment and some will have greater reward. ﴿And your Lord is not unaware of what they do﴾ [Qur'an 6:132].

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 6, verse 133–140:

﴿And your Lord is the Self-Sufficient, the Possessor of mercy. If He wills, He can take you away and replace you with whatever He wills, just as He produced you from the descendants of another people.﴾ Sufficient in His knowledge, full of mercy towards them. If He wills, He takes you away, causes you to die and destroys you; and He will ﴿replace you﴾, that is, create after you ﴿whatever He wills﴾ of a creation other than you, more obedient and more compliant than you.

Ata' said: He means the Companions and the Successors (al-Tabi'un). ﴿Just as He produced you from the descendants of another people, generation after generation.﴾ Muqatil said: He means the people of the ship of Nuh (Noah).

Zayd ibn Thabit recited dhurriyyati with a kasra on the dhal and a shadda. Aban ibn Uthman recited dhurriyyati with a fatha on the dhal and a light kasra on the ra', in accordance with the form of the verb; the rest recited it with a damma on the dhal and a shadda. These are all sound dialectal readings. Tha'lab said: dhirriyya with a kasra is the original form, while dhurriyya with a damma means "offspring."

﴿Indeed, what you are promised is surely coming﴾, that is, arriving, existing. ﴿And you cannot escape﴾, that is, you cannot get away or outrun it; wherever you are, it will overtake you. I'jaz (rendering incapable) means to bring something by which one's opponent is powerless and falls short, so that he has been overcome and made incapable of it.

﴿Say, O Muhammad, to them: O my people, act according to your standing (makanatikum).﴾

Ibn Abbas said: "according to your side." Ibn Zayd said: "according to your position." Yaman said: "according to your ways." Ata' said: "according to your state in which you are." Muqatil said: "according to your braid (jadilatikum)." Mujahid said: "according to your habit (wateeratikum)." al-Kalbi said: "according to your dwellings." It was also said: "act as much as you are able."

al-Sulami and Asim recited makanatikum in the plural throughout the Qur'an.

﴿Indeed, I am acting﴾ means: say, "Do what you do, for I am doing what my Lord has commanded me." This is a command of warning and threat, not a command of permission and license, like His saying: ﴿Do whatever you will﴾ (Fussilat 41:40).

al-Kalbi said: its meaning is, "Do as much as you are able of my affair, for I am acting against you in your affairs by destruction."

﴿So you will soon know who will have the good outcome of the abode﴾. Mujahid and the people of Kufa recited yakunu with the ya', while the rest recited it with the ta'. ﴿The good outcome of the abode﴾ means Paradise. ﴿Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed﴾, that is, the disbelievers will not be safe.

Ata' said: "will not prosper." al-Dahhak said: "will not triumph." Ikrimah said: "will not endure in reward."

﴿And they assign to God a share of what He has produced of the tilth and the cattle﴾.

The commentators said: They used to assign to God a portion of their crops, their livestock, their fruits and all their wealth, and a portion to the idols. What was for the idol they spent on it, and what was for God they gave to the guests and the needy, and they would not eat any of all that. If something fell from what they had assigned to God into the portion of the idols, they left it; and they said: "God is free of need of this." But if something fell from what they had assigned to the idols into the portion of God, they gathered it up and returned it to the portion of the idol, and said: "It is poor."

When they sowed seed that fell into the idol's share, they left it; and what fell from the idol's share into God's share they returned. If water from irrigation flowed from what they had assigned to God into the share of the Devil, they held it back; and if water from irrigation flowed from what they had assigned to God into the share of the idols, they left it. When what they had designated for their associates perished or was barren, and what was for God increased, they said: "Our gods must have their expenditure." So they took what was for God and spent it on their gods. When what was for God was barren and what was for their gods increased, they said: "If God had willed, He would have made pure what was His," and they would not return anything of what belonged to the gods. When drought struck them, they sought help from what they had set apart, and gathered for their associates what they set apart. This is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿of what He has produced of the tilth and the cattle a portion﴾, that is, of what He has left over from the tilth and the cattle a portion. There is an implied ellipsis here, its meaning being: they assigned to God a portion and to their associates a portion.

﴿They say: "This is for God," by their claim﴾.

Yahya ibn Ri'ab, al-Sulami, al-A'mash and al-Kisa'i recited it with a damma. The rest recited it with a fatha. Both are dialectal forms, and it means a saying without reality.

I heard al-Husayn say: I heard al-Anbari relate from Abu al-Abbas al-Azhari from Abu Hatim that he said:
Shurayh the judge said: "Indeed everything has a kunya (figurative name), and the kunya of falsehood is 'they claim' (za'amu). And zaim also means greed."

﴿And this is for our associates﴾, meaning the idols. ﴿But what is for their associates does not reach God, while what is for God reaches their associates.﴾ ﴿Evil is what they judge﴾, that is: wretched is what they were deciding.

﴿And thus did their associates make attractive to many of the polytheists the killing of their children﴾: just as they made attractive to them the prohibition of the tilth and the cattle, so too they made attractive to many of the polytheists the killing of their children. ﴿Their associates﴾, meaning their devils, adorned and beautified it for them, namely burying daughters alive out of fear of poverty.

al-Kalbi said: "Their associates" are the custodians (sadana) of their idols, and they are the ones who used to make the killing of their children attractive to the disbelievers. A man in the Jahiliyya would swear by God that if a son were born to him, he would surely slaughter one of them, just as Abd al-Muttalib swore concerning his son Abd Allah. [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 7/91.]

The people of Syria recited zuyyina with a damma, qatlu in the nominative, awladihim in the accusative, and shurakaihim in the genitive by way of advancement, as if he said: "He made attractive to many of the polytheists the killing of their associates' children." They thereby separated the verb from its agent.

A poet says:
"He passes over what passes, and the garments have been torn, not the self, their chests"
He means: shaqqat (were torn).
The tribe of Abd al-Qays: "ghalail suduruha" (the garments of their chests).

Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami recited zuyyina with a damma on the zay, qatlu in the nominative, awladihim in the genitive, and shurakauhum in the nominative by way of "al-tawdih" and repetition. [The text here reads "al-tawdih," as in the original.]

As if, when He said: "He made attractive to many of the polytheists the killing of their children," the statement was complete; then He said: "By whom was it made attractive?" And He said: "Their associates," meaning their associates made it attractive. So the associates are raised by a verb of a pronoun indicated by zuyyina, as you say: "The meat was eaten by Zayd," as if it were said: "Who is the eater?" and you say: "Zayd."

A poet says:
"Let him weep for Zayd, the one who is afflicted by a dispute, and the one who is struck by what the calamities strike down."
So Zayd is an object standing by itself, whose agent is not named; then he explained it by saying: "ḍāri'," meaning: let the one afflicted weep for him.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿to ruin them﴾, that is, to destroy them; ﴿and to confuse them﴾, that is, to mix up and make ambiguous for them ﴿their religion﴾. They had been upon the religion of Ismail, but they turned away from it. ﴿And had God willed, they would not have done it﴾, that is, had God willed, He would have guided them, granted them success and preserved them from doing that prohibition of the cattle and the tilth. It was also said: "the children." ﴿So leave them, O Muhammad, and what they fabricate﴾, that is, what they invent against God of falsehood, for God is ever watchful over them and ﴿will not fail His promise﴾.

﴿And they say﴾, meaning the polytheists: ﴿These are cattle and tilth, forbidden﴾, meaning what they had assigned to God and to their gods, which has already been mentioned. [Tafsir al-Tabari: 8/59.]

Mujahid said: By "cattle" he means the bahira, the sa'iba, the wasila and the ham. "Hijr" means forbidden. God said: ﴿and they say, "a forbidden barrier"﴾ (al-Furqan 25:22), that is, forbidden and prohibited.

al-Layth said:
"She longed for the farthest palm, so I said to her: 'Forbidden, forbidden; behold those are the rugged lands.'" [Kitab al-'Ayn: 4/120; Lisan al-'Arab: 6/90; the verse is attributed to Jarir, and is also narrated as "hajjat."]

Its origin is from hajr, which means prevention and prohibition, and from it: the judge's restriction (hajr) of a wrongdoer.

al-Hasan and Qatadah recited wa-harthun hujr with a damma on the ha', both being dialectal forms. Ubayy ibn Ka'b, Ibn Abbas, Ibn al-Zubayr, Abu Talha and al-A'mash recited wa-harthun harj with a kasra on the ha' and a ra' before the jim; this is also a dialect, like jadhab and jabadh.

Abu Amr recited:
"Did you not kill the two harijin when they appeared to you, passing by with hands of tough, braided bark?" [Lisan al-'Arab: 2/236; the verse is by al-Hudhali.]

﴿None shall eat of it except whom we will﴾, according to their claim. They mean men without women. ﴿And cattle whose backs are forbidden﴾ means the ham, when its offspring's offspring rides. They said: "He has protected its back, so it is not ridden nor carried upon." ﴿And cattle over which they do not mention the name of God﴾.

Mujahid said: among their cattle there was a group over which they did not mention the name of God, nor in anything concerning them: neither when they rode them, nor when they milked them, nor when they birthed them, nor when they sold them, nor when they carried loads on them.

Abu Asim said: Abu Wa'il said to me: "Do you know what 'cattle whose backs are forbidden' means?" I said: "No." He said: "They do not perform the hajj upon them."

al-Dahhak said: they are those which, when they slaughtered them, they invoked their idols over them. ﴿And over which they do not mention the name of God﴾, fabricating against Him. That is, they used to do that and claimed that God had commanded them to it. ﴿He will recompense them for what they used to fabricate.﴾

﴿And they say: "What is in the bellies of these cattle is exclusively for our males"﴾.

Ibn Abbas, al-Sha'bi and Qatadah said: it means the milk of the slaughtered-for-idols animals was for the males and not for the women; when it died, its meat was shared by their males and females.

al-Suddi said: it means the offspring of the slaughtered-for-idols animals: a portion exclusively for the man and not for the women; [but what is born dead, that is eaten by] men and women. The ta' in khalisatun was added for emphasis and intensification, as it was done with rawiyah, nassabah and 'allamah.

al-Farra' said: the ta' was added because of the feminine gender of the cattle, since what is in its belly is like it, so it was made feminine by its femininity. He said: khalisah may also be like 'aqibah. Among its instances is His saying: ﴿Indeed We purified them with an exclusive remembrance of the abode﴾ (Sad 38:46). Abdullah and al-A'mash recited khalis li-dhukurina without the ta', referring it back to ma. Ibn Abbas recited khalisatun in the construct form, and khalisah, khuliyasah and khalsan are one and the same. The poet says:
"I was my confidant, and I was my exclusive one, and not every man is trustworthy."
[This line is from verses composed by Sulayman ibn Qatta lamenting Imam al-Hasan (peace be upon him), as in Sharh Nahj al-Balagha by Ibn Abi al-Hadid: 6/52, where the second half reads instead: "For every living one there is a dwelling among his people."]

﴿And forbidden to our wives﴾, meaning the women. ﴿And if it should be dead﴾: Ahl al-Madina recited takun with the ta', and mayta with a damma, meaning: if the cattle should become dead. The people of Mecca recited yakun with the ya', and mayta with a damma, meaning: if what is in the bellies of the cattle should become dead. al-A'mash recited takun with the ta' and mayta with a fatha, meaning: if it should be [what is in the bellies of the cattle is dead]. [Addition from Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 7/96.] The rest recited yakun with the ya' and mayta with a fatha, referring it to what supports this: His saying ﴿then they are partners in it﴾, and He did not say "in them." ﴿He will recompense them for their description﴾, that is, for their description and their claim of falsehood against God, like His saying: ﴿and their tongues describe the lie﴾ (al-Nahl 16:62). Wasf and sifah are one, like wizn and zinah, and wa'd and 'idah. ﴿Indeed, He is Wise, Knowing.﴾

﴿Certainly, those have lost who killed their children in foolishness﴾, the verse was revealed concerning Rabi'ah and Mudar, and concerning the Arabs who buried their daughters alive out of fear of captivity and poverty, except for the Banu Kinanah, for they did not do that.

Abu Abd al-Rahman, al-Hasan, the people of Mecca and Syria recited qatthalu with an emphatic doubled tა' for intensification; the rest recited it lightly. ﴿Without knowledge﴾, ﴿and they have prohibited what God provided them﴾, meaning the bahira, the sa'iba, the wasila and the ham, ﴿fabricating against God﴾ when they said that God commanded them with it. ﴿They have certainly gone astray and were not guided.﴾
